stories.title: Trump and Netanyahu finally sit down at the White House, with Iran the make-or-break topic
stories.what_happened: Netanyahu flew to Washington for a scheduled 11 a.m. meeting with Trump at the White House on Tuesday, July 28 — held away from press cameras rather than in a public Oval Office session, a departure from Trump's usual style with visiting leaders. Israeli media reported that Trump had **initially refused the meeting** and only agreed after Israel signaled a concession on Gaza policy. The agenda centers on **Iran** — where Netanyahu wants continued military pressure and Trump prefers the negotiated track his administration has underway — plus the postwar plan for Gaza (including the stalled effort to dismantle Hamas), whether Israeli forces stay in security zones inside Lebanon and Syria, and the long-stalled push to expand the **Abraham Accords** to include Saudi Arabia. Netanyahu and his wife flew out of an Israeli air force base rather than a commercial airport, a precaution taken amid a reported security threat linked to Iran.
key_points: Trump and Netanyahu met privately at the White House at **11 a.m. Tuesday**, their **first face-to-face talks in over five months**.
Iran topped the agenda, with Netanyahu wanting to keep military pressure on Tehran while Trump favors the **diplomatic track his team is already running**.
Trump reportedly **initially refused the meeting** until Israel made a **concession on Gaza**, according to Israeli press reports.
The talks also covered **Gaza's postwar order**, Lebanon and Syria security-zone withdrawals, and prospects for **Saudi-Israel normalization**.
Netanyahu traveled under **tightened security** over a reported Iranian threat, flying out of Nevatim Air Force Base rather than a commercial route.

depth.background: Israel and the US have been the closest of allies for decades, but the relationship between Trump and Netanyahu has been unusually strained through 2026 as the two disagree on how hard to press Iran after weeks of direct US-Iran strikes and counter-strikes. Trump's White House has separately been negotiating a **fragile ceasefire and Strait of Hormuz safe-passage arrangement with Iran**, a diplomatic track Netanyahu has been publicly skeptical of. This is their **first in-person meeting in more than five months** — an unusually long gap for two leaders whose countries are this tightly linked, and a sign of how much friction had built up beforehand.

thread.previously: We reported Netanyahu was departing Israel for Washington ahead of a tense Tuesday meeting with Trump, with the two leaders split over Iran policy — Netanyahu wanting to keep pressure on Tehran, Trump leaning toward the diplomatic off-ramp his own administration has been negotiating.
thread.changed: The meeting itself is now happening — Netanyahu landed in Washington and the two leaders sat down at the White House at 11 a.m. local time, away from cameras, with reports the visit almost didn't happen after Trump initially refused to meet until Israel made a Gaza-related concession.

stories.title: Pakistan and Sri Lanka's women meet in a series decider after two wildly different ODIs
stories.what_happened: Pakistan Women and Sri Lanka Women are playing a **series-deciding 3rd ODI** at the Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium in Hambantota, with the series tied at **1-1**. Pakistan won the series opener by **5 wickets**, chasing down Sri Lanka's 210 with a score of 211/5. Sri Lanka responded in the second match by chasing Pakistan's total of **273/5**, reaching 275/2 thanks to centuries from **Vishmi Gunaratne and Harshitha Samarawickrama** -- one of their finest ODI run-chases in years. Sri Lanka go into the decider with strong momentum after that performance.
key_points: The **3rd and final ODI** is a series decider, with the series **tied 1-1**
Pakistan won the 1st ODI by **5 wickets**; Sri Lanka leveled with an **8-wicket** win in the 2nd
Sri Lanka's 2nd-ODI win came on the back of **twin centuries** from Vishmi Gunaratne and Harshitha Samarawickrama, chasing 273
The decider is being played at the **Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium**, Hambantota

depth.background: Pakistan's women's team is touring Sri Lanka for a three-match ODI series. The first two matches produced contrasting results: Pakistan won a low-scoring opener by 5 wickets, while Sri Lanka hit back in the second match with one of their best ODI run-chases in years, chasing down 273 with centuries from Vishmi Gunaratne and Harshitha Samarawickrama. That win leveled the series and set up a decisive third match.

stories.title: Sensex opens flat, Nifty dips below 24,000 as cheaper oil and Fed jitters pull markets both ways
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark indices opened nearly unchanged on Tuesday: the **BSE Sensex dipped just 4.03 points** to 76,831.75, while the **Nifty 50 fell 24.7 points** to open at 23,971.25, slipping below the psychologically important **24,000 level**. The muted open followed a strong previous session, in which the Sensex had surged over 776 points (1.02%) and the Nifty gained 228 points (0.96%) on **easing West Asia tensions** and a sharp drop in crude oil, which extended its decline to touch **$86.89 a barrel** on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal. In early trade, **IT stocks led the gainers** -- TCS rose as much as 2.6%, followed by Infosys, Tech Mahindra and HCL Tech -- while investors also braced for elevated volatility ahead of the monthly **F&O expiry** and the outcome of the US Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting.
key_points: Sensex opens **nearly flat**, dipping 4 points to 76,831.75
Nifty slips **24.7 points** to open below the **24,000 mark**
Crude oil extends its slide to **$86.89 a barrel** on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal
IT stocks -- **TCS, Infosys, Tech Mahindra** -- lead gainers in early trade

depth.background: Indian markets often move on a mix of domestic cues and global signals -- crude oil prices matter a lot because India imports the vast majority of its oil, so cheaper crude usually helps corporate margins and the currency. This week, two big global stories are pulling in different directions: easing US-Iran tensions are pushing oil prices down (good for India), while investors are also nervously awaiting the US Federal Reserve's rate decision, a source of global uncertainty.

stories.title: Parliament strikes a deal to actually debate the anti-paper-leak bill, easing the NEET-crackdown standoff
stories.what_happened: After repeated adjournments this week over the opposition's protest against the July 20 crackdown, the government and opposition reached an agreement to hold a substantial, extended debate — reported at eight to ten hours — on the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026**, which had already been introduced in the Lok Sabha. The bill would toughen penalties for exam paper leaks and related malpractice, raising the maximum jail term to 10 years and fines up to ₹10 crore. Congress leader **Rahul Gandhi** is expected to speak during the debate, giving the opposition a high-profile platform to raise its concerns about both the bill and the police crackdown. Rather than rushing the bill to a vote today, both sides agreed to the longer discussion format, effectively de-escalating — at least temporarily — the standoff that had repeatedly halted proceedings.
key_points: The government and opposition agreed to an **extended 8-to-10-hour debate** on the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026**.
**Rahul Gandhi** is set to speak on the bill, marking the opposition's most prominent voice entering the debate directly.
The bill proposes raising penalties for **paper-leak offences** to up to **10 years in jail and a ₹10 crore fine**.
It comes after days of deadlock over the **July 20 police crackdown** on NEET protesters at Jantar Mantar.
Both sides chose a **full debate over passing the bill immediately**, allowing extended scrutiny rather than a rushed vote.

depth.background: India's original Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act was passed in 2024 after repeated exam paper leaks disrupted competitive exams like NEET (the national medical-entrance test) for millions of students. A fresh 2026 paper-leak and CBSE on-screen-marking scandal reignited nationwide protests, including a sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar that drew a police crackdown on July 20 — an event the opposition has used to stall Parliament's Monsoon Session for days, demanding accountability from Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. That standoff even bled into the unrelated hunger strike by activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose fast over the same paper-leak issue ended only after the government agreed to his demands.

thread.changed: Rather than staying stuck, the government and opposition reached an agreement today for an extended eight-to-ten-hour debate on the bill, with Rahul Gandhi set to speak — a concrete step out of the standoff rather than another adjournment.

stories.title: Parliament is adjourned again as opposition presses the NEET-crackdown showdown into a new bill fight
stories.what_happened: Today's session opened straight into disruption, with both houses gaveled shut amid heavy sloganeering before resuming later in the morning. The government used the session to formally introduce the **Public Examinations Amendment Bill, 2026**, which amends the existing 2024 anti-cheating law with seven new provisions: prison terms of **up to 10 years**, fines of **up to ₹10 crore**, confiscation of a guilty party's assets, and the power for states to set up fast-track special courts so cases are resolved within three months rather than dragging for years. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju urged all parties to actually debate the bill's substance. But opposition MPs, including from Congress and regional parties, are using the four-hour debate slot to keep the spotlight on the police response to the July 20 march rather than the bill's text — arguing accountability for the crackdown matters as much as new penalties for future leaks.
key_points: Both the **Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha were adjourned** today amid renewed opposition sloganeering, continuing yesterday's showdown.
The flashpoint bill this week is the **Public Examinations Amendment Bill, 2026**, meant to toughen penalties for exam paper leaks.
The bill proposes **up to 10 years in prison, fines up to ₹10 crore**, asset confiscation, and fast-track special courts for offenders.
The government has scheduled a **4-hour debate** with young NDA MPs including Bansuri Swaraj and Tejasvi Surya leading the case for it.
Opposition MPs are using the bill debate to keep pressing on the **July 20 police crackdown** on NEET paper-leak protesters, not just the bill's contents.

depth.background: India's Monsoon Session of Parliament, which began July 20, has been dominated by fallout from the NEET-UG 2026 exam paper leak scandal. A youth-led protest movement (the 'Cockroach Janta Party') demanded the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, culminating in a massive Jantar Mantar-to-Parliament march on July 20 that was met with a police lathi-charge (baton charge) and tear gas. Pradhan ultimately resigned on July 25 after a 26-day hunger strike by activist Sonam Wangchuk and government assurances on protester amnesty — but the opposition has kept the political pressure on over how the protest itself was policed, forcing repeated adjournments this week (see yesterday's coverage).

thread.previously: Yesterday, the opposition forced a showdown in Parliament specifically over the July 20 police crackdown on NEET protesters, disrupting proceedings.
thread.changed: Today the fight has attached itself to a concrete piece of legislation — the Public Examinations Amendment Bill — with the government trying to steer debate toward the bill's tough new penalties while the opposition keeps redirecting it back to crackdown accountability, and both houses were adjourned again as a result.

stories.title: The Fed's two-day meeting starts today — traders now think a rate hold is more likely than a cut
stories.what_happened: The Fed's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) — the group of officials who set US interest rates — began its scheduled two-day meeting today, with the rate decision due tomorrow, July 29. Going into the meeting, futures markets (where traders bet on what the Fed will do) put the odds of a **hold at rates unchanged around 64%**, a sharp shift from just a week earlier when a hold looked far more certain at 87%. That shift reflects genuine uncertainty: inflation is running hot, with the Consumer Price Index up **4.2% year-over-year through May 2026** — the sharpest annual rise since April 2023 — which normally argues for the Fed to keep rates high or even raise them. But there are also signs of a softening labor market pulling in the opposite direction, toward a cut. The rate has held at **3.50%-3.75%** since the last change, and Warsh's shift away from forward guidance means officials aren't tipping their hand before Wednesday.
key_points: The **Federal Reserve's policy meeting runs July 28-29**, with a decision due Wednesday.
Markets now price roughly a **64% chance the Fed holds rates steady**, down sharply from an 87% chance just a week ago.
The Fed's target range has sat at **3.50%-3.75%** since its last move.
New Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh** has already changed how the Fed communicates — dropping traditional forward guidance for a **pure 'data-dependent' approach**, making each meeting harder to predict.
US inflation (CPI) rose **4.2% over the year to May 2026**, the biggest 12-month jump since April 2023 — well above the Fed's usual 2% comfort zone.

depth.background: The Federal Reserve is the US central bank — it sets the short-term interest rate that ripples through mortgages, credit cards, business loans, and, because the US dollar and Treasury market are the anchor of global finance, borrowing costs worldwide including in India. Earlier this year the Fed brought in a new chair, Kevin Warsh, who has shifted the Fed's style: instead of pre-signaling what it plans to do next ("forward guidance"), the Fed now says it will decide meeting-by-meeting based purely on incoming data. That makes each Fed decision, including this one, more of a genuine toss-up for markets than it used to be.

stories.title: India's Commonwealth Games medal count hits 10 after an all-night session in Glasgow
stories.what_happened: India's medal count at the Commonwealth Games 2026 climbed to **10 overall** (two gold, five silver, three bronze) after an eventful overnight session in Glasgow. **Weightlifting remains India's strongest suit**, contributing six of the ten medals so far. On the track, **Sarvesh Kushare won silver in the men's high jump final**, while weightlifters and para-athletes added further medals across multiple weight categories. Tuesday's schedule (Day 5) is headlined by **Gulveer Singh**, the national 10,000m record holder and Asian champion, competing in a direct final for his first-ever Commonwealth Games podium finish. India's boxing squad also has **five fighters in quarter-final bouts**, each already guaranteed a shot at a semi-final spot and at least a bronze medal if they win.
key_points: India's medal tally **doubles to 10** (2 gold, 5 silver, 3 bronze) by Day 5
**Weightlifting has delivered 6 of India's 10 medals** so far
Sarvesh Kushare wins **silver in the men's high jump final**
Gulveer Singh, the national record holder, runs the **men's 10,000m final** today chasing a first CWG podium
Five Indian boxers reach **quarter-finals**, each guaranteed at least a shot at bronze if they advance

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games 2026 are being held in Glasgow, and India has fielded a large contingent across athletics, weightlifting, boxing, swimming and more. India's campaign opened with a high-jump storyline (Kushare vs Tejaswin) and built momentum through Mirabai Chanu's opening weightlifting gold and a run of medals from the weightlifting team. Sharmila Dhankar's para-athletics gold on Day 4 was historic, ending a 20-year wait for an Indian medal in that discipline at the Games.

stories.title: Zelensky's 30,000-more-troops claim meets Seoul's skepticism as North Korea's war role deepens
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia is preparing to receive **30,000 additional North Korean troops**, with preparations under way since June in Russia's Voronezh region, close to the Ukrainian border. If it happens, this would **almost triple** North Korea's troop commitment beyond the roughly 14,000 currently believed to be serving with Russian forces. Zelensky added that Russia is also readying new North Korean ballistic missile launchers. South Korean government sources, however, say they are only tracking the reports and have **no confirmed evidence** yet that a new deployment is under way -- a notable gap between Kyiv's warning and Seoul's official caution.
key_points: Zelensky says Russia is preparing space for **30,000 more North Korean troops** in its Voronezh region
That would **roughly triple** North Korea's current troop contribution to the war
**South Korea's own government** says it has no confirmed signs of a new deployment yet
Zelensky also says Russia is preparing to receive new **North Korean ballistic missile launchers**

depth.background: North Korea has backed Russia's war on Ukraine since 2024, when it first sent thousands of troops to help Russia retake territory in its own Kursk region after a surprise Ukrainian incursion. Around **14,000-20,000 North Korean soldiers**, including special forces and combat engineers, have been deployed to Russia so far, alongside artillery shells and missiles. In return, Pyongyang has reportedly gained battlefield experience for its army and technological help from Moscow. South Korea, the US and their allies see the arrangement as a serious escalation because it ties two adversaries closer together militarily.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Russia was trying to bring in another 30,000 North Korean troops for the Ukraine war, on top of the roughly 14,000-20,000 already deployed since 2024.
thread.changed: Today, South Korean government sources say they are watching the reports closely but have found no confirmed signs of a new deployment yet -- an official note of caution on Zelensky's claim -- while new reporting adds that Russia is also preparing to receive new North Korean ballistic missile launchers.

stories.title: Desert Vipers Thrash San Francisco Unicorns by 9 Wickets in Global Super League
stories.what_happened: San Francisco Unicorns won the toss, batted first, and could only post 151 for 7 in their 20 overs. In reply, Desert Vipers made light work of the chase, racing to 152 for 1 in just 16.1 overs to win by nine wickets with 23 balls unused. Zachary Carter led the chase with a rapid 55 off 29 balls and also chipped in with the ball, taking 1 for 9, earning him the Player of the Match award.
key_points: **San Francisco Unicorns** were held to **151/7** batting first at Providence Stadium in Guyana
**Desert Vipers** chased the target down for the loss of just **one wicket**, finishing on **152/1 in 16.1 overs**
West Indies all-rounder **Zachary Carter** starred with an unbeaten-paced **55 off 29 balls** plus **1/9** with the ball to win Player of the Match
It was **Match 7** of the 2026 Global Super League, a five-team T20 tournament running **July 23 to August 1**
The dominant win strengthens Desert Vipers' position as the competition heads into its final week before the August 1 final

depth.background: The Global Super League is a T20 franchise tournament now in its third edition, bringing together five club sides from different countries and leagues — Desert Vipers (UAE's ILT20), Lahore Qalandars (Pakistan Super League), Perth Scorchers (Australia's Big Bash), Guyana Amazon Warriors (Caribbean Premier League) and San Francisco Unicorns (USA's Major League Cricket) — to play a round-robin plus playoffs, all hosted at Providence Stadium in Guyana. Desert Vipers, champions of the UAE's ILT20 in 2026, came into this match looking to build on an already useful position in the group table.

stories.title: West Indies rip through 14 wickets in a single day to seize control of the Trinidad Test
stories.what_happened: Day 3 turned into one of the most eventful days of Test cricket this year, with **14 wickets falling across both innings** in a single session-packed day. West Indies seamer **Justin Greaves** ran through Pakistan's lower order with a career-best five-wicket haul, helping bowl Pakistan out cheaply in their second innings. But Pakistan's own bowlers, **Abbas and Ali**, struck back hard when West Indies batted again, cutting through the top order and giving themselves a real chance at a comeback win. Late in the day, an unbeaten **33-run partnership between Kemar Roach and Shamar Joseph** steadied West Indies and pushed their overall lead past 150 runs, closing the day at a **155-run lead** with wickets still in hand.
key_points: **14 wickets fell** on Day 3 of the West Indies-Pakistan 1st Test at Tarouba — an unusually violent day of cricket.
West Indies' **Justin Greaves took a career-best five-wicket haul** to tear through Pakistan's lower order.
Pakistan struck back too, with **Abbas and Ali** taking wickets to cut into the West Indies innings.
An unbeaten **33-run stand between Kemar Roach and Shamar Joseph** pushed West Indies' lead past 150.
West Indies ended Day 3 with a lead of **155 runs**, putting them firmly in control heading into Day 4.

depth.background: This is the first Test of Pakistan's tour of the West Indies, being played at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad, from July 25-29. Pakistan had already given up a slim first-innings advantage after West Indies bowled them out for 282, with Shan Masood's gritty century not enough to prevent a 29-run deficit (covered here yesterday) — a story that turned dramatically today.

thread.previously: Yesterday, Shan Masood's century wasn't enough to stop West Indies bowling Pakistan out for 282, leaving West Indies with a slim 29-run first-innings lead.
thread.changed: Today that slim lead exploded into a commanding one: 14 wickets fell in a single day, Justin Greaves took a career-best five-for, and West Indies closed Day 3 leading by 155 runs with wickets in hand.

stories.title: AI Spending Fears Trigger Kospi Circuit Breaker as Samsung, SK Hynix Crash
stories.what_happened: On Tuesday, July 28, investors dumped Korean chip stocks the moment markets opened, sending the Kospi down more than 8% and forcing Korea Exchange to freeze all trading for 20 minutes at 10:13:43 a.m. — the third circuit breaker this month alone. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which together make up a huge share of the index's value, led the rout, both falling by double digits at their worst point. The Kosdaq saw an identical plunge and matching halt. The selloff had been building since Monday, when SanDisk, Micron and Western Digital all sank on Wall Street over the same worry: that hyperscalers' (the giant cloud companies like Microsoft, Google and Meta) massive AI data-center spending is running ahead of any proven payoff, and that CXMT's blockbuster IPO signals Chinese competitors can now undercut Korean and US memory makers on price. SK Hynix was due to report its second-quarter earnings the same day, adding extra volatility around the stock.
key_points: South Korea's benchmark **Kospi** index plunged more than **8%** at the open, forcing the exchange to trigger a marketwide **circuit breaker** (an automatic 20-minute trading halt) at **10:13 a.m.** local time — the **8th** such halt in 2026 and the **14th** ever.
**Samsung Electronics** fell as much as **9.5–10%** and **SK Hynix** dropped up to **11–13%**, making them the two biggest losers in the entire **MSCI Asia Pacific** index, which fell about **3%**.
The **Kosdaq** (Korea's smaller-cap tech exchange) also fell over **8%** and triggered its own separate circuit breaker.
SK Hynix's US-listed shares had already closed overnight at **$143.02**, below their **$149** IPO price, after SanDisk sank **12%** and Micron dropped **5%** on Wall Street the prior session.

The panic followed China's memory-chip maker **CXMT** going public a day earlier and soaring as much as **530%**, becoming the world's 4th-largest DRAM maker and reviving fears it can undercut Samsung and SK Hynix on price.

depth.background: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together control roughly **65%** of the world's DRAM (computer memory chip) market, and their stocks have soared through 2026 on a wave of investment tied to the artificial intelligence boom — chips like theirs go into the servers that power AI systems like ChatGPT and Gemini. That rally has made Korea's Kospi index a global bellwether for whether investors still believe AI spending will pay off. China's CXMT, a state-linked memory maker, is racing to catch up and just listed its shares in Shanghai on July 27, instantly becoming China's most valuable listed company and stoking fears it will flood the market with cheaper chips.

stories.title: Defence PSU Bharat Electronics posts 9% profit jump as its order book crosses ₹72,000 crore
stories.what_happened: BEL's board approved and released its first-quarter results for the financial year 2026-27 (April-June 2026) on July 28. Consolidated net profit came in at ₹1,054.34 crore, up 9% from ₹969.91 crore in the same quarter last year, while revenue climbed a sharper 25.27% to ₹5,533.06 crore, showing the company converting its large order pipeline into billed work faster. The company's order book — contracts already signed but not yet delivered or billed — stood at ₹72,258 crore as of July 1, 2026, effectively multiple years of future revenue already secured. The board also raised the company's authorised capital to ₹1,000 crore, giving it more room to raise funds if needed. Brokerages including Motilal Oswal reaffirmed bullish ratings after the results.
key_points: **Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL)**, India's state-run defence electronics maker, reported Q1 FY27 results on **July 28**
Consolidated net profit rose **9%** year-on-year to **₹1,054.34 crore**, from ₹969.91 crore a year earlier
Revenue jumped **25.27%** year-on-year to **₹5,533.06 crore**
Order book stood at **₹72,258 crore** as of July 1, 2026 — work already lined up for years ahead
Brokerage Motilal Oswal kept a 'Buy' rating with an unchanged target price of **₹510**

depth.background: BEL is a **Navratna** (top-tier) defence public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, headquartered in Bengaluru, that makes radars, sonars, electronic-warfare systems, and communication equipment for India's armed forces. It has become a bellwether stock for India's push toward defence self-reliance (**"Atmanirbhar Bharat"** in defence manufacturing), which aims to cut costly imports of military hardware and build a domestic arms industry. India's overall defence production touched a record **₹1.78 lakh crore** in FY26, with exports near ₹39,000 crore, and BEL is one of the biggest contributors to that number.

stories.title: India's foreign secretary meets China's vice foreign minister in Beijing, both sides pledge to keep the border calm
stories.what_happened: On Monday, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri traveled to Beijing and held talks with China's Vice Foreign Minister Hua Chunying — the latest round of a diplomatic dialogue track that has run alongside military-level border talks since 2020. The two sides said they "acknowledged the importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity" in border areas, standard diplomatic language signaling neither wants a fresh flare-up, without claiming any new breakthrough on the actual territorial dispute. They reviewed the entire bilateral relationship and discussed advancing the Modi-Xi vision of India and China as **"development partners,"** touching on trade, economic ties, and people-to-people exchanges. Misri also met Sun Haiyan of the Chinese Communist Party's International Department to discuss political and academic exchanges. No new agreements, dates, or concrete deliverables were announced.
key_points: Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri** met China's Vice Foreign Minister **Hua Chunying** in Beijing on **July 27**
Both sides acknowledged the importance of keeping **peace and tranquillity** along the disputed border
They reviewed the full bilateral relationship, from trade to culture, under the Modi-Xi 'development partners' framing
Misri separately met a senior Chinese Communist Party official, Sun Haiyan, for party-to-party exchanges
Comes as India runs a record **$151 billion** trade relationship with China but exports back only **$16.6 billion**

depth.background: India and China share a roughly 3,488-km disputed border called the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, and a deadly clash in Ladakh's Galwan Valley in June 2020 froze high-level ties for over four years. Relations began thawing after Prime Minister **Modi** met President **Xi Jinping** at the October 2024 **Kazan summit** (on the sidelines of a BRICS meeting in Russia), where both agreed troops should disengage from remaining friction points. Since then, direct flights have restarted, the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage has resumed, and border trade has reopened — but the two countries remain economically lopsided, with India heavily dependent on China for rare-earth magnets used in electronics and EVs.

stories.title: Shan Masood's century in vain as West Indies bowl Pakistan out for 282, taking a 29-run lead in the Trinidad Test
stories.what_happened: Pakistan resumed Day 3 at 199 for 3, with overnight batters Shan Masood and Salman Ali Agha looking to build a lead over West Indies' first-innings total of 311. The pair added 47 runs for the fourth wicket before Masood brought up his seventh Test century — and the first century ever scored at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy — before eventually being dismissed for 109 off 184 balls with 12 fours. Once Masood departed, West Indies' Justin Greaves ran through the rest of the batting order, finishing with figures of 5 for 27 in 11 overs, with support from Kemar Roach and Shamar Joseph, who took two wickets each. Pakistan were bowled out for 282 in 80.1 overs, falling 29 runs short of West Indies' 311, handing West Indies a first-innings lead heading into Day 4.
key_points: **Shan Masood** scored his **seventh Test century** (109 off 184 balls), the first-ever Test hundred at the newly-built **Brian Lara Cricket Academy** venue.
Pakistan, resuming Day 3 at 199/3, were eventually **bowled out for 282**, falling short of West Indies' first-innings total of 311.
West Indies all-rounder **Justin Greaves** ran through the Pakistan tail with **5 wickets for 27 runs**, his best Test bowling figures.
West Indies now hold a **29-run first-innings lead** heading into Day 4 of the series-opening Test.
Masood, playing his first innings since being relieved of Pakistan's captaincy, anchored the innings with a **155-run partnership** with Imam-ul-Haq before the tail folded quickly.

depth.background: This is the first Test of a two-match series between Pakistan and hosts West Indies, being played at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad — the ground's first-ever international red-ball match. Shan Masood was recently removed as Pakistan's Test captain after a run of poor results, making this century, his first innings as a specialist batter rather than skipper, personally significant as he tries to justify his place in the side on batting alone. West Indies' Justin Greaves is a fast-bowling all-rounder who has been growing into a senior bowling role for the hosts.

thread.previously: West Indies were bowled out for 311 on Day 2 after reaching 303/7 at lunch, with Shai Hope's unbeaten 89 the key contribution; Pakistan closed Day 2 at 60/1 in reply, still 251 runs behind.
thread.changed: Pakistan built on that platform through Day 3 — Masood converted a fifty into a century — but were eventually bowled out for 282, handing West Indies a 29-run first-innings lead rather than the deficit narrowing further.

stories.title: MI London beat Southern Brave Men off the final ball in a Hundred thriller at Southampton
stories.what_happened: Southern Brave Men posted 129 for 9 in their 100 balls, with Jamie Smith top-scoring with 49 as Trent Boult (2/15) and other MI London bowlers kept the total in check. Chasing, MI London got home with three wickets and just one ball to spare, with Will Jacks making 54 to anchor the pursuit before Ollie Pope sliced the winning runs — a two through backward point off the final delivery — to seal a three-wicket win. Marcus Stoinis had earlier taken 3 for 17 in the Southern Brave innings. The result was Southern Brave's third defeat of the competition, while MI London's win lifted them to third place in the men's table. The match capped a thrilling day of Hundred cricket at Southampton, after the venue's women's fixture between the same two clubs also went to the final overs, with Southern Brave's women winning by just 1 run.
key_points: **MI London** chased down Southern Brave's total with a **three-wicket win off the final ball**, with Ollie Pope steering the winning runs through backward point.
**Will Jacks** top-scored for MI London with **54** to anchor the chase of Southern Brave's 129/9.
**Jamie Smith** top-scored for Southern Brave with **49**, but the innings stalled as MI London's bowlers, led by **Marcus Stoinis (3/17)**, kept the total below 130.
The result is Southern Brave Men's **third loss** of the competition, while MI London moves up to **third place** in the table.
It came on the same day the two clubs' women's teams also played a nail-biter at the same Southampton venue, with Southern Brave's women winning by just 1 run.

depth.background: The Hundred is a franchise cricket tournament in English cricket, with each innings limited to 100 balls instead of the usual 120 in T20 cricket, designed for a shorter TV window and to attract new fans. Eight city-based men's and women's teams compete in parallel each season; Southern Brave, based in Southampton, and MI London, a newer franchise backed by the Mumbai Indians ownership group, are two of the eight teams. Both clubs' men's and women's sides played at the same Southampton venue on the same day, giving the ground a rare doubleheader.

stories.title: US and Iran edge toward a formal ceasefire deal, with the Strait of Hormuz the last sticking point
stories.what_happened: Regional mediators say they've made genuine headway getting US and Iranian officials back to the table after the fighting paused. The emerging shape of a deal centers on the Strait of Hormuz: rather than Iran ceding full control, it would be allowed to **run vessel-transit management through the strait with fewer restrictions on ships** than the US originally wanted — a face-saving compromise for Tehran. President Trump said the US held off on resuming strikes **because Iran asked it to**, while making clear the US remains ready to hold Iran to account if talks collapse. Muddying the picture, Iran's Foreign Ministry told reporters there are **no current negotiations** taking place — a direct contradiction of the mediators' account. Meanwhile the ceasefire remains fragile in practice: Saudi Arabia intercepted and shot down drones this week fired by Iran-backed militia groups operating out of Iraq, a reminder that the wider network of Iran-aligned armed groups across the region hasn't stood down.
key_points: Mediators report **real progress** reviving talks after nearly two weeks of direct US-Iran fighting.
The sketched compromise would let Iran manage ship traffic through the **Strait of Hormuz** with **fewer restrictions**, instead of the US demanding open access outright.
President Trump says Washington paused renewed strikes **at Iran's request**, but warns they resume if no deal is reached.
Iran's Foreign Ministry publicly denies any active negotiations are underway — the two sides are not yet aligned on the basic facts.
Even with a pause, Iran-backed militia drones are still flying: **Saudi Arabia shot down drones** fired at it from Iraq this week.

depth.background: In early July 2026, a rapid escalation between the US and Iran turned into the most direct fighting between the two countries in decades, with US strikes on Iranian targets and Iranian retaliation that spilled into the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which **about a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments pass** every day. Iran responded to strikes by asserting more control over the strait and firing on vessels, which is what sent oil prices spiking and then, on hopes of a ceasefire, tumbling nearly 7% (as covered here yesterday). A truce has technically been holding for over a week, but the two sides have not yet signed anything formal.

thread.previously: Yesterday, oil prices sank nearly 7% as the ceasefire held and Tehran opened talks on the Strait of Hormuz, with early signs the two sides were moving toward de-escalation.
thread.changed: Today mediators say real progress is being made on a Hormuz vessel-transit compromise, but Iran's own Foreign Ministry is publicly denying any negotiations are happening — and Saudi Arabia just shot down Iran-backed militia drones, showing the ceasefire is still fragile on the ground.

stories.title: India clears ₹41,863 crore in new electronics-component factories, betting on Foxconn, Samsung and Dixon
stories.what_happened: India's electronics ministry (MeitY) signed off on 22 new project proposals under this scheme, representing a planned investment of **₹41,863 crore** and projected output worth **₹2,58,152 crore**. Major names behind the new projects include Dixon Technologies, Samsung Display's Noida unit, Foxconn's India arm (Yuzhan Technology India), and metals giant Hindalco. The projects span 11 different product categories — mobile phones, telecom gear, consumer electronics, IT hardware, automotive electronics, and strategic/defense electronics — and will be built across eight states including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Combined with two earlier rounds this year, the scheme has now approved **46 projects worth ₹54,567 crore** in total, expected to directly employ about 51,000 people.
key_points: The government approved **22 new electronics-manufacturing projects** worth a combined **₹41,863 crore** (about $5 billion).
Backers include **Dixon, Samsung Display, Foxconn (Yuzhan Technology) and Hindalco**.
The projects are expected to create **33,791 direct jobs** across **eight states**.
They'll produce components India mostly imports today: **PCBs, capacitors, camera and display modules, lithium-ion cells**, and materials like aluminium extrusion.
This is the scheme's **third approval round** — total commitments now stand at **₹54,567 crore** across 46 approved projects since it launched.

depth.background: The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) is a government incentive program designed to build up India's supply of the small but essential parts that go into phones, laptops, cars, and electronics — the pieces India currently imports heavily, mostly from China and East Asia. It's part of a broader 'China+1' push: as global electronics brands look to diversify manufacturing away from China, India is trying to make itself the alternative by subsidizing local component factories rather than just final-assembly plants.

stories.title: Sharmila Dhankar wins para-athletics gold as India close Commonwealth Games Day 4 with 5 medals, resolving the high-jump duel
stories.what_happened: India wrapped up Day 4 of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with five medals — one gold, three silver, and one bronze — its best single-day haul of the Games so far. Sharmila Dhankar won the gold, India's only one of the day, in the women's shot put F57 para-athletics event. In the men's high jump, Sarvesh Kushare cleared **2.25m** for silver, settling the marquee duel previewed as the day's headline event before competition began. Weightlifting continued to deliver: Bindyarani Devi Sorokhaibam won bronze in the women's 58kg category and Valluri Ajaya Babu took silver in the men's 79kg, both lifting a combined 330kg. Weightlifting alone has now produced six of India's medals at these Games, extending a pattern that started with Mirabai Chanu's gold earlier in the competition.
key_points: Para-athlete **Sharmila Dhankar** won India's only gold of the day, in the women's **shot put F57** category at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
**Sarvesh Kushare** claimed silver in the men's high jump, clearing **2.25m**, settling the closely-watched duel previewed as the day's headline event.
Weightlifters **Bindyarani Devi** (women's 58kg) and **Valluri Ajaya Babu** (men's 79kg) added a bronze and a silver, both lifting **330kg**.
India closed Day 4 with **1 gold, 3 silver, 1 bronze** — five medals in a single day, its best haul so far.
Weightlifting alone has now produced **six** of India's medals at these Games, building on Gyaneshwari Yadav's and Mirabai Chanu's earlier golds.

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games bring together athletes from 74 nations and territories of the Commonwealth every four years, and India has traditionally been strongest in weightlifting, shooting, wrestling, and badminton. This year's Games are being held in Glasgow, Scotland. India's Monday campaign had been previewed around the men's high jump as a marquee event, pitting Sarvesh Kushare against other contenders, while the country's deep weightlifting squad kept adding medals through the week. Para-athletics has grown into a genuine medal source for India at recent Games — Sharmila Dhankar's **F57** category covers field athletes who compete seated because of a lower-limb impairment.

stories.title: NIA raids two states in a human-trafficking case that lured Indian youth to fake jobs — then forced them into Myanmar cyber-fraud centres
stories.what_happened: NIA teams carried out searches on Monday at two locations — **Durgapur** in West Bengal and **Jagdalpur** in Chhattisgarh — as part of the continuing investigation into the Myanmar-linked trafficking and cyber-fraud network. The case dates back to a February chargesheet against three accused: **Ankit Kumar (alias Ankit Bhardwaj)**, **Ishtikhar Ali**, and a fugitive Chinese national identified as **Lisa**. Investigators say the network lured young Indians with promises of lucrative jobs in Thailand advertised on online platforms, then trafficked them into Myanmar, where the victims discovered the jobs were fake and were forced to work in cyber-fraud operations against their will.
key_points: India's **National Investigation Agency (NIA)** searched locations in **Durgapur (West Bengal)** and **Jagdalpur (Chhattisgarh)** on Monday
The case centers on a network accused of trafficking Indian citizens to **Myanmar** under the guise of overseas jobs
Victims were lured with promises of **well-paid jobs in Thailand**, then trafficked onward into Myanmar and forced to work in **cyber-fraud call centres**
The raids follow a February chargesheet naming **three accused**, including a fugitive Chinese national, in the same racket
The case exposes a well-organized, cross-border network spanning **Indian and foreign agents**

depth.background: Over the past few years, Indian investigators have uncovered a pattern of trafficking networks that lure young, often unemployed Indians with fake job offers — typically for call-centre or tech-support work in Thailand — then smuggle them across the border into Myanmar, where armed groups and criminal syndicates run scam compounds. Once inside Myanmar, workers are frequently stripped of their passports and forced, often under threat of violence, to run online fraud schemes targeting victims abroad. The NIA, India's federal anti-terrorism and organised-crime agency, has been investigating several such networks and had already chargesheeted three people — including an absconding Chinese national — in this specific case back in February.

stories.title: An IndiGo flight from Mumbai to Dubai makes an emergency landing in Rajkot after smoke is detected in its cargo hold — all 194 aboard safe
stories.what_happened: IndiGo flight 6E 1452 from Mumbai to Dubai, carrying 194 passengers and crew, diverted to Rajkot International Airport on Monday after the crew detected smoke in the aircraft's cargo hold and alerted air traffic control. Rajkot airport declared a full emergency, deploying fire tenders and ambulances to standby positions along the runway before the plane touched down. The aircraft landed safely at 3:27 p.m., and all 194 people on board disembarked without injury. Authorities have not yet disclosed what triggered the smoke warning, and inspectors have reported no visible damage to the aircraft so far.
key_points: Flight **6E 1452**, carrying **194 people**, was diverted after crew spotted **smoke in the cargo hold**
Rajkot airport declared a **full emergency**, scrambling fire tenders and ambulances before touchdown
The aircraft landed safely at **3:27 p.m.**, and everyone on board walked away **unhurt**
The cause of the smoke has **not yet been disclosed**, and no damage to the aircraft has been reported

depth.background: The flight was operating IndiGo's Mumbai-to-Dubai route when the crew detected smoke, a serious enough warning that pilots are trained to treat any cargo-hold smoke alert as a potential in-flight fire risk rather than wait to see if it's a false alarm. Diverting to the nearest suitable airport — in this case Rajkot in Gujarat, rather than continuing to Dubai or turning back to Mumbai — is standard procedure to get the aircraft on the ground as fast as possible. India's aviation sector has faced repeated scrutiny this year over maintenance and safety incidents, so any emergency landing draws close attention from regulators and the public alike.

stories.title: Southern Brave Women edge MI London by 1 run in a Hundred thriller at Southampton
stories.what_happened: In the **9th match of The Hundred Women's Competition 2026** at the Utilita Bowl in Southampton, Southern Brave Women posted **126 for 7**. Chasing 127 to win, MI London's **Hayley Matthews** struck four boundaries early before being bowled by **Issy Wong** with the score on 42. **Danni Wyatt-Hodge** then anchored the chase, finishing **52 not out**, but MI London fell **1 run short**, reaching 125/3. **Lauren Bell** held her nerve to defend just 8 runs off the last 5 balls and seal the win for Southern Brave, who remain unbeaten this season.
key_points: Southern Brave Women won by just **1 run**, defending 126/7 against MI London's 125/3.
**Lauren Bell** defended **8 runs off the final 5 balls** to seal the win.
**Danni Wyatt-Hodge** top-scored for MI London with **52 not out** against her former side.
The win keeps Southern Brave **unbeaten** so far this Hundred season.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format, 100-ball domestic cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments in parallel each summer since 2021. Southern Brave, based in Southampton, have been one of the stronger women's sides in the competition's history. Danni Wyatt-Hodge previously played for Southern Brave before moving to MI London, adding a personal edge to the contest against her old team.

stories.title: India's Gyaneshwari Yadav wins silver in a record-breaking weightlifting duel, India's 5th CWG medal
stories.what_happened: On Day 4 in Glasgow, India's **Gyaneshwari Yadav** went head-to-head with Nigeria's Didih Onome Omolola in the women's **53kg weightlifting final**, with both lifters trading Games-record lifts throughout the contest. Yadav ultimately finished with a personal-best total of **199kg** (an 88kg snatch and a 111kg clean and jerk) to take **silver**, while Omolola's stronger **206kg** total (93kg snatch, 113kg clean and jerk) secured gold; Canada's Rebeka Groulx took bronze with 178kg. The result is India's third weightlifting medal of the Games and its fifth medal overall, moving the country up to **8th place** on the Day 4 medal table.
key_points: Gyaneshwari Yadav lifted a personal-best **199kg total** (88kg snatch + 111kg clean & jerk) in the women's 53kg final.
Nigeria's Didih Onome Omolola took gold with **206kg**, as both lifters kept breaking the Games record back and forth.
It's India's **5th medal** of these Commonwealth Games and its **3rd in weightlifting**, after Mirabai Chanu (gold) and Raja Muthupandi (silver).
India climbed to **8th on the medal table** after four days of competition in Glasgow.

depth.background: The **Commonwealth Games** is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from Commonwealth nations (mostly former British territories); the 2026 edition is being hosted in **Glasgow**. Weightlifting has become one of India's most reliable medal sources at the Games, and this edition opened strongly: legendary lifter **Mirabai Chanu** won gold in the 48kg category on Day 3 to complete a hat-trick of CWG titles, and **Raja Muthupandi** added a silver in the 65kg category the same day.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 3 more Palestinians in Gaza, the latest breach of a ceasefire in name only
stories.what_happened: Israeli drone and air strikes killed at least **three Palestinians** and injured **11 others**, in incidents in Jabalia, Deir al-Balah and near the Al-Qarara Bridge in southern Gaza. Local health officials say the ceasefire that began on October 10, 2025 has not stopped Israeli operations: more than **1,200 Palestinians have been killed** and nearly **3,900 injured** in the roughly nine months since it took effect. Israel's military maintains control over about **70% of Gaza's territory**, squeezing the population into less than a third of the strip. The pattern of near-daily strikes despite a nominal truce has become a recurring feature of the post-ceasefire period.
key_points: **3 Palestinians killed, 11 injured** in fresh Israeli strikes despite the ceasefire
Strikes hit **Jabalia, Deir al-Balah and near Al-Qarara Bridge** in different parts of Gaza
Since the ceasefire took effect in **October 2025**, over **1,200 more Palestinians** have been killed regardless
Israel controls roughly **70% of Gaza**, confining Palestinians to under a third of the strip

depth.background: A ceasefire in Gaza took effect on **October 10, 2025**, after nearly two years of war that followed Hamas's October 2023 attack on Israel. On paper, it was meant to stop major hostilities and let reconstruction and aid begin. In practice, Israeli strikes and Gazan casualties have continued at a lower but steady pace ever since, and Israeli forces still occupy a large majority of the territory.

stories.title: Karnataka's CM summons every MP to Delhi in one room to make a united case for drought relief
stories.what_happened: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar called a meeting of every Karnataka Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MP, regardless of party, at Karnataka Bhavan in Delhi on Monday evening. The agenda covered the state's pending proposals for drought relief funds, delayed development projects and other Central-government clearances. Around seven or eight state ministers also attended. Shivakumar separately announced the state Assembly's next session will begin August 13.
key_points: DK Shivakumar convened all Karnataka MPs, across parties, at Karnataka Bhavan in Delhi
Agenda: drought relief funds, pending Central projects, policy clearances
He also announced Karnataka's state Assembly session will begin August 13
Move aims to present a single, bipartisan state voice during Parliament's Monsoon Session

depth.background: Large parts of Karnataka have been hit by drought this year, straining agriculture, drinking water and rural incomes. States routinely have to lobby the Union government for disaster relief funds and project clearances, and a fragmented, party-line approach usually weakens their leverage in Delhi.

stories.title: Delhi High Court orders X and YouTube to pull 'Kala Hiran' links after Salman Khan says the film violates his personality rights
stories.what_happened: Hearing Salman Khan's plea, the Delhi High Court directed the producer of 'Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy,' Amit Jani, to remove all links to the film's teaser from X and YouTube within 24 hours. The court sharply criticised the producer during the hearing, saying, 'You seem to think you are above the law. Things are only getting worse day by day. You cannot do this even to an ordinary citizen.' The producer's counsel pushed back, arguing the teaser never named Khan and asking how it could violate his rights, but the court found the content could damage the actor's reputation and ordered its takedown. The case centres on Khan's personality rights rather than defamation, treating his identity and life story as something he can legally control the commercial use of.
key_points: The film **'Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy'** is reportedly modeled on Salman Khan's **1998 blackbuck poaching case** and his alleged rivalry with gangster **Lawrence Bishnoi**
The court ordered the producer to remove all related links from **X and YouTube within 24 hours**
The judge told the producer bluntly: **'You seem to think you are above the law'**
The producer argued it was **only a teaser** and that Khan was never named directly

depth.background: Salman Khan has been legally entangled for over two decades in a real blackbuck poaching case dating to 1998, which — combined with his alleged links to organised crime figure Lawrence Bishnoi, whose gang has publicly threatened Khan's life over the case — has made his life story a magnet for unauthorised dramatisations. 'Personality rights' is a legal doctrine, increasingly tested in Indian courts, that lets a well-known individual stop others from commercially using their name, likeness or life story without consent, distinct from defamation law. Khan filed suit against the makers of 'Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy' arguing the film improperly trades on his identity and the real, ongoing threat to his safety tied to the Bishnoi rivalry.

stories.title: Red Bull turns down a $3 billion bid for its junior F1 team, Racing Bulls
stories.what_happened: A consortium led by Dean Attew — a former adviser to ex-F1 chief executive Bernie Ecclestone — and financier Andrew Harriot, backed by Abu Dhabi investment funds, made an approach to buy Racing Bulls for a reported **$3 billion**. Red Bull rejected the offer almost immediately, according to multiple F1 outlets, choosing to keep its two-team development pipeline intact rather than cash out. Paddock analysts noted the scale of the bid is striking: when a consortium bought a 24% stake in Alpine in 2023, it valued that entire team at roughly $900 million, while Alpine's valuation is now estimated near $3 billion — meaning Racing Bulls, a smaller and less prominent team, drew a bid in the same range.
key_points: Red Bull rejected a reported **$3 billion (£2.2bn) bid** for its sister team, **Racing Bulls**, almost as soon as it was made.
The offer was led by **Dean Attew**, a former investigator for ex-F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone, backed by **Abu Dhabi-based investment funds**.
$3 billion would be one of the **largest bids ever linked to an F1 team** — roughly matching paddock estimates for Alpine's entire valuation.
Racing Bulls is Red Bull's **driver-development team**, the pipeline that produced champions **Max Verstappen and Sebastian Vettel**.
The rejection reaffirms Red Bull's **long-term commitment to its two-team structure** even as speculation swirls around Verstappen's own future at the senior team.

depth.background: Formula 1 team valuations have exploded in recent years as the sport's global popularity and TV/streaming rights have grown, turning even mid-grid teams into billion-dollar assets. Red Bull runs a **two-team system**: Red Bull Racing, its championship-winning senior outfit, and Racing Bulls (based in Faenza, Italy), a feeder team that lets promising young drivers get real Grand Prix experience before an eventual promotion. That pipeline is exactly how both **Max Verstappen** and **Sebastian Vettel** — multiple world champions — entered Red Bull's senior ranks, making the junior team strategically valuable to Red Bull far beyond its market price.

stories.title: Supreme Court: 'peaceful protest is a constitutional right, mere agitation can't justify a lathi-charge'
stories.what_happened: A Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice **Surya Kant**, Justice **Joymalya Bagchi**, and Justice **V. Mohana** orally observed, while hearing a batch of petitions over police action against student protesters, that **peaceful and lawful protest is constitutionally protected** and that **'mere agitation cannot justify a lathi-charge.'** The bench was responding to petitions alleging excessive police force during protests over exam paper leaks, including the **July 20 lathi-charge** on a student march toward Parliament in New Delhi. The Court said allegations of police excess should be **independently examined** and stressed the need for **uniform protocols** across states for how police handle demonstrations, rather than each state force setting its own rules.
key_points: Chief Justice **Surya Kant**, with two other judges, made the oral observations while hearing petitions on police force against student protesters.
The Court said the **right to peaceful protest is constitutionally protected** and can't be answered with a lathi-charge.
It specifically referenced the **July 20 lathi-charge on students marching toward Parliament**.
The bench called for allegations of police excess to be **independently examined** and for **uniform police protocols** on handling protests nationwide.

depth.background: Since a National Testing Agency (NTA) paper-leak scandal hit India's NEET medical entrance exam, student protests have spread to more than a dozen cities under the banner of the 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), a satirical youth protest movement. On **July 20**, a student march toward Parliament in Delhi was met with a police lathi-charge — a baton charge used to disperse crowds — leaving several protesters injured, including one woman who was critically hurt and put on a ventilator. The crackdown became a flashpoint in its own right, drawing opposition demands in Parliament for Home Minister Amit Shah to explain the police response, separate from the original exam-leak grievance.

stories.title: Ashok Gehlot accuses Rajasthan's BJP government of cancelling over 300 land allotments made under his Congress government
stories.what_happened: Gehlot said on Monday that the BJP-led state government has cancelled **more than 300 land allotments** that his Congress government had granted, arguing the reversals have disrupted social institutions and public welfare projects that depended on that land. He framed the move as part of a broader BJP pattern of unwinding his government's decisions rather than a genuine anti-corruption or irregularity review.
key_points: Former Rajasthan CM **Ashok Gehlot** accused the state's BJP government of cancelling **over 300 land allotments** made during his Congress tenure
He alleges the cancellations have hurt **social institutions and public welfare initiatives** that relied on that land
The claim adds to an ongoing pattern of the BJP state government **reversing decisions** made under the previous Congress administration
It escalates the state-level political fight between Gehlot's Congress and Rajasthan's ruling BJP

depth.background: Ashok Gehlot led Rajasthan's Congress government for three terms before the BJP, under Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma, took power after the December 2023 state election. Since then, the BJP administration has systematically rolled back several Gehlot-era decisions — including dissolving nine districts Gehlot had created and scrapping or scaling back welfare schemes — moves Gehlot has repeatedly criticised as politically motivated rather than driven by genuine public interest. Land allotments to trusts, cooperatives, and social institutions are a recurring flashpoint in this fight, since incoming state governments in India often review or cancel allotments made by their predecessors, alleging irregularities or favouritism.

stories.title: Amit Shah defends the 'Vande Mataram Bill' in Parliament as opposition accuses the government of 'manufacturing patriotism'
stories.what_happened: Union Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai tabled the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 -- popularly called the Vande Mataram Bill -- in the Rajya Sabha on behalf of Home Minister Amit Shah. It would extend the same legal protection given to the national anthem to Vande Mataram, with penalties of up to three years in prison for deliberately insulting, obstructing, or disrupting its singing. Left party MPs, including CPI's P Sandosh Kumar and CPI(M)'s John Brittas, objected loudly to its introduction, and the House was adjourned till Monday amid the disruption. On Monday, Amit Shah himself is expected to address the Rajya Sabha as debate resumes.
key_points: Bill would give India's national song the same legal protection as the national anthem
Disrespecting or disrupting Vande Mataram could carry up to 3 years in prison
Left MPs call it an attempt to distract from the NEET paper-leak protests
Rajya Sabha was adjourned last Friday amid sloganeering; Amit Shah addresses the House Monday

depth.background: Vande Mataram is India's national song -- distinct from the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana -- written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and long tied to the independence movement. But it's also politically loaded, since some see it as tied to a specific religious and nationalist reading of Indian identity that not everyone is comfortable being compelled to sing. The government has been trying to push several bills through a Monsoon Session already dominated by anger over the NEET exam paper-leak scandal and student protests.

stories.title: England's Jacob Bethell ruled out of the Hundred with a knee injury, now a doubt for the Pakistan Tests
stories.what_happened: England all-rounder **Jacob Bethell** has withdrawn from **The Hundred Men's 2026** after suffering a **right knee injury** during England's recent ODI series win over India. He underwent an **MRI scan on Monday morning**, with the England medical team now awaiting results to determine the extent of the injury and how long recovery will take. Bethell had been set to **captain Birmingham Phoenix** in the tournament. The injury also puts him in doubt for England's home Test series against Pakistan, which begins **August 19 at Headingley**.
key_points: **Jacob Bethell** has been ruled out of The Hundred 2026 with a **right knee injury**.
He was injured during England's recent **ODI series win over India**.
An **MRI scan on Monday** (today) will determine the injury's severity and recovery time.
He was set to **captain Birmingham Phoenix**, and is now a doubt for England's Test series against Pakistan starting **August 19** at Headingley.

depth.background: Jacob Bethell is a 22-year-old England all-rounder who has been fast-tracked into the national side across formats, including a maiden ODI century against South Africa earlier this year. He was named captain of Birmingham Phoenix for this year's Hundred, a significant vote of confidence in a young player. England's next big assignment is a home Test series against Pakistan, opening at Headingley on August 19 — less than a month away.

stories.title: Red Bull poaches Mercedes' driver-development chief Gwen Lagrue to replace Helmut Marko
stories.what_happened: **Mercedes officially confirmed** that **Gwen Lagrue**, its driver-development chief for the past decade, is leaving the team after being approached by **Red Bull**. Lagrue will join Red Bull's leadership team in **2027** as **director of its junior driver programme**, taking over the role long held by **Helmut Marko**, who departed at the end of the 2025 season. During his time at Mercedes, Lagrue was credited with guiding drivers including **George Russell, Kimi Antonelli, and Esteban Ocon** into Formula 1.
key_points: **Mercedes confirmed** that **Gwen Lagrue** is leaving after a decade with the team, following a **Red Bull approach**.
Lagrue will become **director of Red Bull's junior driver programme** starting in **2027**.
He succeeds **Helmut Marko**, the influential Austrian who ran Red Bull's junior programme for years before departing.
At Mercedes, Lagrue helped develop **George Russell, Kimi Antonelli, and Esteban Ocon** into F1 drivers.

depth.background: Helmut Marko was, for nearly two decades, one of the most powerful and controversial figures in Formula 1 — the gatekeeper of Red Bull's famed young-driver pipeline that produced stars like Max Verstappen. His departure left a major gap in how Red Bull identifies and develops future talent. Gwen Lagrue joined Mercedes in January 2016 as driver development chief and built a strong reputation for spotting and nurturing young talent, including current Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli.

stories.title: Sri Lankan Court Denies Bail to Jaffna Kings Co-Owner Manjot Kalra in Match-Fixing Probe
stories.what_happened: Kalra and co-accused Yuvraj Pushpa applied for bail on medical grounds, with their lawyers arguing both men were unwell. Prosecutors from Sri Lanka's Special Investigation Unit for the Prevention of Offences Relating to Sports opposed the application, telling the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court that their probe was still active and that they held recorded phone conversations and video evidence showing Kalra had offered a player upwards of $30,000 to fix a match outcome. The complaint that triggered the arrest was originally lodged by three capped Sri Lankan internationals — Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Avishka Fernando and Dunith Wellalage — after Kalra allegedly approached one of them. The magistrate sided with the prosecution and refused bail, meaning both men remain remanded in judicial custody at least until their next scheduled court date on July 31.
key_points: Colombo's Chief Magistrate **Asanga S. Bodaragama** rejected bail pleas from Jaffna Kings co-owner **Manjot Kalra** and fellow Indian national **Yuvraj Pushpa** on Monday
Investigators told the court Kalra allegedly offered players **more than $30,000** to influence match outcomes, backed by recorded calls and video evidence
Three Sri Lanka internationals — **Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Avishka Fernando and Dunith Wellalage** — are the players who reported the approach to authorities
Kalra, a **former India Under-19 World Cup-winning centurion**, was arrested on **July 17**, just hours before the 2026 LPL season began, and stays in custody until **July 31**
Kalra denies all wrongdoing and says he is cooperating fully with the investigation

depth.background: Manjot Kalra scored the century that won India the 2018 Under-19 World Cup final and later co-owned the Lanka Premier League franchise Jaffna Kings through his company Sports Commune. Days before this year's LPL began, he was arrested at a Colombo hotel over an alleged approach to a player; the resulting financial chaos (sponsors unpaid, players covering jersey logos with black tape) led Sri Lanka Cricket and tournament operator IPG to strip Sports Commune of the franchise entirely and take over Jaffna Kings' operations directly. Kalra has remained in custody since, and Monday's court appearance was his first bid for release.

stories.title: Ravindra Jadeja cleared fit for India's Sri Lanka Tests, removing one big selection doubt
stories.what_happened: The National Cricket Academy has cleared Jadeja as fit, meaning he'll be under consideration when India's Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee names the Test squad for Sri Lanka, expected imminently. Alongside Jadeja's clearance, selectors are also weighing the fitness of Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana, with Rana reportedly yet to recover from a hamstring injury picked up during the England T20I series. Jasprit Bumrah's own fitness call remains separate and ongoing, with the pace bowler resting until July 30 before a final assessment at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence.
key_points: Ravindra Jadeja has been **ruled fit** and is available for selection for India's two-Test tour of Sri Lanka
He'd been out since **May** with a tennis elbow injury from IPL 2026, last playing for India in January's ODIs against New Zealand
The squad is set to be **announced Monday**, with the series opening in **Galle on August 15**
Fitness questions remain for **Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana**, while Bumrah's knee is still being monitored separately
Jadeja's return strengthens India's spin options for conditions expected to favour turn in Sri Lanka

depth.background: India's selectors have spent recent days weighing a squad for the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka, opening in Galle on August 15, with the biggest question marks around senior pace bowler Jasprit Bumrah's fitness and all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja's availability after injury. Jadeja, one of India's most experienced spin-bowling all-rounders, has been sidelined since suffering a tennis elbow injury during the IPL in May and hadn't played for India since January's ODIs against New Zealand.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported the BCCI would name its Sri Lanka Test squad by Tuesday, July 28, with Jadeja "set to return" and Bumrah's left-knee fitness still the biggest open question, alongside fitness watches on Washington Sundar and Sai Sudharsan.
thread.changed: Jadeja has now been formally ruled fit and available by the NCA — moving him from "expected to return" to cleared — while Harshit Rana has also emerged as a fresh fitness concern; Bumrah's own assessment is still pending on July 30.

stories.title: German prosecutors confirm the Berlin Pride attack was Islamist terrorism and lay out the attacker's fuller radicalization timeline
stories.what_happened: German federal prosecutors on Monday laid out the fullest account yet of Ballout's path to the attack. He shared ISIS propaganda online in **2024**, then traveled to Lebanon in **2025** intending to cross into Syria and join the group; Lebanese authorities arrested him and a military court sentenced him to **three months in prison** there. Back in Germany, he was convicted of preparing a serious act of subversive violence but received a **suspended sentence of one year and ten months** — partly because of time already served in Lebanon and partly because he told the court he had distanced himself from ISIS. Prosecutors also confirmed a **2022 juvenile conviction** for assault and robbery, filling in a longer history of run-ins with the law before Saturday's attack.
key_points: Prosecutors formally confirmed the van-and-blade attack at Berlin's Pride festival was an **Islamist terror attack**, not just a suspected one
Attacker **Abdul Ballout, 21,** had tried to join ISIS in 2025 — he traveled to Lebanon, was arrested there, and served **three months** in a Lebanese military prison
Back in Germany, he received a suspended sentence of **1 year and 10 months** for preparing a serious act of violence — meaning he was free to carry out Saturday's attack
He also had a **2022 juvenile conviction** for assault and robbery, showing a longer pattern authorities had already flagged
The disclosures sharpen questions about why someone twice-convicted for violence-linked offenses was still free to act

depth.background: A van rammed a crowd near Berlin's Pride festival on Saturday night, killing one woman and injuring 29 people, before the driver fled and was shot dead by police roughly 20 hours later in a manhunt. Germany's interior minister called it a suspected Islamist terror attack within hours, and authorities quickly named the driver as **Abdul Ballout**, a German citizen of Lebanese descent — but the full picture of his background was still emerging. Germany has faced a string of vehicle-ramming and knife attacks tied to Islamist extremism in recent years, repeatedly raising the question of how radicalized individuals already known to police still manage to act.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported a van rammed a Pride festival crowd in Berlin, killing one woman and injuring 29; the suspect, Abdul Ballout, fled and was shot dead by police about 20 hours later, with Germany's interior minister calling it a suspected Islamist terror attack and noting Ballout had a prior suspended conviction tied to Islamic State propaganda.
thread.changed: Prosecutors have now formally confirmed the Islamist terror motive and released the fuller timeline: Ballout's 2025 attempt to join ISIS via Lebanon, his three months in a Lebanese military prison, the exact length of his suspended German sentence (1 year 10 months), and a previously-undisclosed 2022 juvenile conviction for assault and robbery.

stories.title: F1's driver market braces for chaos: 17 contracts expire after 2026, and Verstappen is the biggest unknown
stories.what_happened: **Seventeen drivers** on the current Formula 1 grid have contracts expiring at the end of the 2026 season -- effectively most of the field. Only **five drivers hold deals that run beyond 2026**: Max Verstappen, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Charles Leclerc and Pierre Gasly. That leaves stars including **Lewis Hamilton, Fernando Alonso, Carlos Sainz and Sergio Perez** all needing to sort out their futures. Analysts describe the situation as a powder keg, because Verstappen's own decision -- whether he stays at Red Bull using his newly active exit clause, or moves elsewhere -- is expected to trigger a chain reaction of moves across multiple teams. With the summer break approaching, the **next three weeks away from the track** are expected to produce the biggest driver-market news of the year.
key_points: **17 F1 drivers** are out of contract at the end of 2026 -- most of the entire grid
Only **5 drivers** -- Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Leclerc and Gasly -- have deals beyond this season
**Max Verstappen's** choice is seen as the single biggest domino for the whole market
The next **three weeks of the summer break** are expected to shape the 2027 grid

depth.background: Formula 1 contracts often run in multi-year cycles, and 2026 happens to be a year when an unusually large number expire at once -- including big names like Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso. Driver moves cascade: when one top team has an opening, it usually pulls a driver from another team, which then needs to fill that seat, and so on down the grid. Max Verstappen's situation is especially pivotal this year because his Red Bull contract now has an exit clause he can trigger, given the team's current form.

stories.title: Sensex jumps 550 points as oil prices tumble 5% on the US-Iran strike pause
stories.what_happened: Indian benchmark indices opened sharply higher on Monday, July 27, after Asian and global oil prices dropped roughly 5% following a weekend pause in US-Iran military strikes, which eased fears of a bigger disruption to Gulf oil supply. The Sensex jumped 549 points to open at 76,608.98, and the Nifty 50 rose about 161 points to open at 23,928.40; by mid-morning both were still climbing, with broader mid-cap and small-cap indices also in the green.
key_points: Sensex opened up 549 points (0.72%) at 76,609; Nifty opened above 23,928
By 9:35am, Sensex was up 0.79% at 76,663; Nifty up 0.72% at 23,938
Trigger: crude oil fell 5% after the US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend
Comes 3 days after both indices hit a one-month low on oil-driven selling

depth.background: India imports roughly 85% of the crude oil it uses, so when global oil prices rise, it directly pushes up the country's import bill, weakens the rupee, and squeezes companies that depend on fuel or oil-linked inputs — which is why Indian stock markets react so sharply to swings in crude prices, especially ones driven by Middle East tensions. On Friday, July 24, the Sensex and Nifty had fallen to one-month lows as fighting between the US and Iran pushed oil above $100 a barrel.

thread.previously: On Friday, July 24, the Sensex fell 332 points and the Nifty about 0.4% to one-month lows, as crude oil prices spiked on escalating Middle East tensions between the US and Iran.
thread.changed: The same oil-and-Iran dynamic reversed Monday morning: crude fell 5% after the US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend, and the Sensex and Nifty jumped over 500 points at the open.
