stories.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear pleas on police 'excesses' against NEET protesters, but rejects an urgent listing
stories.what_happened: A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is hearing two petitions today alleging that Delhi Police used disproportionate force — tear gas, lathi charges and other measures — against students protesting the NEET paper-leak issue on July 20. The court had initially declined a request for an urgent, out-of-turn hearing, with the Chief Justice reportedly telling the petitioners' lawyer not to waste the court's time, but agreed the matter would be taken up in the ordinary course today. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the petitioners, argued the police response amounted to 'police excess... going against students.'
key_points: CJI Surya Kant's bench will hear two pleas on the July 20 Delhi police crackdown today
Court had earlier declined to list the matter urgently, telling lawyers 'please don't waste our time'
Petitions allege tear gas and lathi-charge were used against NEET paper-leak protesters
Case is separate from the government's talks with protest leaders and the new anti-paper-leak bill

depth.background: Student protests over an alleged leak in this year's NEET-UG medical entrance exam have been building for weeks under the banner of the 'Cockroach Janta Party,' culminating in a 'Chalo Sansad' march toward Parliament on July 20 that Delhi Police broke up with tear gas and lathi charges — injuring, by some accounts, dozens of protesters and police alike. One young woman critically hurt in that crackdown was taken off ventilator support and is now stable, as we reported yesterday. Two separate petitions were then filed asking the Supreme Court to examine whether the police used excessive force.

stories.title: Government holds its first direct talks with NEET protest leaders — but makes no commitments
stories.what_happened: Union Health Minister JP Nadda met a CJP delegation at his residence — the first direct negotiation between the government and protest leaders since the crackdown. The delegation submitted a written memorandum and appealed to protesters to end their sit-in. Nadda said he would raise their concerns 'at the appropriate level' but offered no firm commitments. CJP leaders say the protest continues until remaining demands — ₹1 crore compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide amid the scandal, and the release of hospitalized activist Sonam Wangchuk — are met.
key_points: Union Health Minister JP Nadda met a CJP delegation for the first negotiation since the Chalo Sansad crackdown
The group submitted a written memorandum and asked protesters to end their sit-in
CJP says no real commitments were made; the protest continues
Remaining demands: ₹1 crore compensation for NEET-related suicide victims and activist Sonam Wangchuk's release from hospital

depth.background: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has led a weeks-long protest movement over alleged irregularities in India's NEET medical entrance exam, including a paper-leak scandal. Protesters tried to march on Parliament in a 'Chalo Sansad' demonstration; police used a lathi charge to disperse the crowd, critically injuring a woman who was later taken off ventilator support — a story we've covered. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, one of the protesters' original targets, has since resigned and been replaced by Pralhad Joshi.

thread.previously: We reported a woman critically injured in the police crackdown on the Chalo Sansad march had been taken off ventilator support and was conscious and stable.
thread.changed: The government held its first direct negotiation with CJP protest leaders since the crackdown, but made no firm commitments — the protest continues over compensation and Sonam Wangchuk's release.

stories.title: Netanyahu heads to the White House for a tense Trump meeting, with Iran splitting the two leaders
stories.what_happened: Netanyahu departs for Washington today ahead of a Tuesday meeting with Trump, his sixth Oval Office sit-down since Trump's return to office and his first since the Iran war escalated. The two leaders are expected to clash over next steps on Iran: Netanyahu is pushing for a renewed round of military strikes, while **Trump** — who ordered a halt to two weeks of nightly US bombing raids on Iran last week — is said to prefer giving diplomacy more room. Ahead of the trip, Netanyahu has made conciliatory gestures on Gaza and Lebanon that Israeli commentators read as an attempt to arrive in Washington looking like a cooperative partner rather than a source of friction. While in Washington, Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of **Senator Lindsey Graham**, a longtime Israel ally in Congress. The meeting lands at a delicate moment: the fragile US-Iran halt in hostilities is only days old, and how the two leaders align — or don't — could determine whether it holds.
key_points: Netanyahu meets Trump at the White House on **Tuesday**, his first visit since the Iran war began.
It will be his **sixth** Oval Office meeting with Trump in a year and a half — more than any other world leader.
Iran is the central divide: Netanyahu wants **renewed military action**, Trump leans toward **diplomacy**.
The visit comes days after the US paused its **two weeks of nightly airstrikes** on Iran.
Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of **Senator Lindsey Graham** while in Washington.

depth.background: Since the Iran conflict escalated, the US and Israel have coordinated closely but not always agreed on how far to push militarily. The US carried out nightly strikes on Iran for two weeks before pausing them last week as **Trump** signaled he wants room for diplomacy. Netanyahu has now visited the Trump White House **five times before** this trip, reflecting how central the US alliance is to Israel's wartime strategy — but this is his first visit since the Iran war intensified.

stories.title: China's Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, the largest open-weight AI model ever built
stories.what_happened: Beijing-based Moonshot AI released the open weights for **Kimi K3**, a **2.8-trillion-parameter** AI model, making it downloadable for free roughly **a day earlier** than the company's own July 27 target. The model uses a 'sparse mixture-of-experts' design, meaning it only activates a small slice of its total parameters for any given task, which keeps inference costs down compared to a dense model of the same size. It supports a **1-million-token context window**, letting it process entire codebases or large document sets in a single pass. On independent benchmarks, K3 ranked behind only Anthropic's and OpenAI's top models on general intelligence, while beating other rivals, including Anthropic's Opus-tier model, on coding and agentic tasks specifically. Moonshot priced API access at **$3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens** — the highest of any Chinese lab, but still roughly half the cost of Anthropic's premium model for comparable work.
key_points: Kimi K3 has **2.8 trillion parameters**, making it the largest open-weight AI model released to date.
Moonshot AI shipped the free download **a day early**, at roughly 7:30pm EDT on July 26.
It only activates a fraction of its parameters per request (a 'mixture-of-experts' design), keeping running costs down despite its size.
It ranks **fourth overall** on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, just behind Claude and GPT's top models but ahead of several others.
Moonshot is charging **roughly half** what Anthropic charges for its priciest model, undercutting Western rivals on price.

depth.background: 'Open-weight' models are AI systems whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and run, unlike 'closed' models such as those from OpenAI or Anthropic, which are only accessible through a paid API. Chinese AI labs, including Moonshot AI, have leaned into open-weight releases partly because **U.S. export controls limit their access to the most advanced computer chips**, making it harder to compete purely on raw compute — so they compete on giving the model away and letting the ecosystem build on it instead. Moonshot's prior model, Kimi K2.6, was already a well-regarded open-weight system; K3 is a major step up in scale.

stories.title: F1's summer-break report card: Antonelli's rookie masterclass, and a rough half-season for Verstappen
stories.what_happened: With Formula 1 entering its summer break after the Hungarian Grand Prix, mid-season assessments graded every team's performance under this year's new technical rules. Mercedes' 19-year-old rookie **Kimi Antonelli** has been the story of the season, winning six races and taking podiums in all but two starts to become the youngest driver ever to lead the championship at this stage. Mercedes as a team holds a commanding **78-point lead** over Ferrari in the constructors' standings. The bigger shock is at Red Bull, where four-time champion Max Verstappen sits 7th in the drivers' standings without a single win — reports point to Red Bull's car struggling with electrical deployment and its adaptation to the new active-aerodynamics rules, leaving Verstappen relying on pure driving skill to stay competitive. McLaren, which set the pace for much of last season, has also fallen short on both speed and reliability, with Lando Norris trailing Antonelli by 91 points.
key_points: Rookie **Kimi Antonelli**, 19, leads the drivers' championship at the summer break — the **youngest driver ever** to lead the standings, with **six wins** and podiums in all but two races.
**Mercedes** leads the constructors' championship by a wide margin, up **78 points** on second-placed Ferrari at the break.
**Max Verstappen sits 7th** in the standings with **zero wins** so far — a shock given his recent dominance — with Red Bull's new-rules car reportedly lagging Mercedes and Ferrari.
**McLaren**, last year's benchmark team, has lacked both pace and reliability to keep up, leaving Lando Norris **91 points** behind Antonelli.
The grades come at F1's annual **summer break**, the multi-week pause when teams and press traditionally take stock of the season so far.

depth.background: F1 introduced a major overhaul of its technical rules for the 2026 season — new engines and aerodynamics — the biggest regulatory shake-up since 2022, which reshuffled the competitive order and made this year's midpoint report card unusually consequential. The sport's summer break sits roughly at the season's halfway point and gives teams and commentators a natural pause to assess who has adapted best to the new rules before the run to the championship resumes.

stories.title: West Indies bowled out for 311 as Pakistan fight back to 60/1 at stumps on Day 2 in Trinidad
stories.what_happened: West Indies, who had reached a commanding 303/7 at lunch on Day 2, were eventually bowled out for 311 in the afternoon session — Shai Hope's unbeaten 89 was the only thing keeping the innings alive as Pakistan's bowlers, led by Abbas (3-63), got the old ball to talk. Pakistan then began their reply and closed the day at 60/1, still 251 runs behind but showing the first signs of fighting their way back into the match.
key_points: West Indies all out for 311 (Hope 89*, Hodge 84, Abbas 3-63)
Pakistan reach 60/1 at stumps, trailing by 251
Pakistan took 4 wickets before lunch bowling with the old ball
1st Test at Tarouba runs July 25-29

depth.background: This is the first Test of Pakistan's tour of the West Indies, played at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad — a five-day format where the side that scores more runs across two innings, or bowls the opposition out twice, wins.

thread.previously: West Indies had reached a commanding 303/7 at lunch on Day 2, built around Shai Hope and Hodge.
thread.changed: West Indies were bowled out for 311 in the afternoon, and Pakistan's openers fought back to 60/1 at the close, still trailing by 251 but showing early resistance.

stories.title: Ben Duckett powers Trent Rockets to a 4-wicket chase over London Spirit in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: London Spirit posted 159/9 batting first at Trent Bridge, Nottingham. Trent Rockets chased it down with 160/6, winning by 4 wickets with 2 balls to spare, powered by Ben Duckett's 75 off 47 balls, which earned him Player of the Match.
key_points: Trent Rockets chase down 160 with 2 balls to spare
Ben Duckett named Player of the Match: 75 off 47 balls
London Spirit had posted 159/9 batting first
Keeps Trent Rockets' early-season Hundred campaign on track

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-form, 100-balls-per-side franchise competition, now in its sixth summer, running alongside international cricket in a packed English summer.

stories.title: San Francisco Unicorns edge Perth Scorchers XI by 5 runs in a tight Global Super League thriller
stories.what_happened: San Francisco Unicorns scored 152 for 8 in their 20 overs, then bowled out — restricted — Perth Scorchers XI to 147 for 9, winning by 5 runs at Providence Stadium in Guyana on Sunday.
key_points: San Francisco Unicorns posted 152/8, then restricted Perth Scorchers XI to 147/9
The 5-run margin makes it one of the closest games of this GSL season
Played at Providence Stadium, Guyana, the tournament's single venue
Part of the fledgling Global Super League, running July 23-August 1

depth.background: The Global Super League is a young T20 franchise competition linking cricket boards and city-based teams across different domestic leagues — including Australia's Big Bash and new US-based sides — all played at one venue in Guyana over a short window.

stories.title: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee $250 billion for OpenAI's giant new Ohio data center
stories.what_happened: The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday that Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion financial guarantee to help OpenAI lease and finance a massive AI data center campus being built in southern Ohio by a SoftBank Energy subsidiary. The campus is designed to eventually draw 10 gigawatts of power, with an initial 800-megawatt phase due by 2028. Nvidia's guarantee would cover the lease and construction debt, not the chips that go inside; separately, Nvidia is discussing financing up to $350 billion of OpenAI's chip purchases for the same site. Including the chips, the full project could exceed $500 billion, making it the largest data center project ever announced. The power supply is controlled by the US government and funded by Japan under a recent trade agreement, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick involved in deciding who gets access to that power.
key_points: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee roughly **$250 billion** in financing so OpenAI can lease a giant new data center in **Ohio**.
The **10-gigawatt** campus is being built by SoftBank's energy arm and could cost more than **$500 billion** all-in, including chips.
It would be the **largest data center project ever announced**.
Nvidia is separately discussing financing up to **$350 billion** of the chip purchases for the same project.
Electricity for the site is controlled by the **US government** and funded by Japan under a recent trade deal.

depth.background: OpenAI has been racing to secure enormous amounts of computing power to train and run its AI models, and data centers at this scale — 10 gigawatts is roughly enough electricity for a small country — cost more than almost any lender will finance alone. SoftBank, the Japanese conglomerate and major OpenAI investor, is developing the site through its energy subsidiary. Nvidia's chips power nearly all major AI systems, and increasingly the company is acting less like a component supplier and more like a financier for its biggest customers' megaprojects.

stories.title: F1 stewards rule Sainz 'wholly responsible' for the Piastri crash -- but only fine him half the usual penalty
stories.what_happened: During Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix, Carlos Sainz's Williams collided with Oscar Piastri's McLaren as Sainz cut back in while battling Fernando Alonso, not realizing Piastri was attempting to pass him at the same moment. Stewards ruled Sainz 'wholly responsible' for the collision but issued only a 5-second penalty -- half the standard punishment -- because Piastri 'was not visible' in Sainz's mirrors and F1's blue-flag warning system had malfunctioned during the race, leaving Sainz without a signal that Piastri was closing in. Piastri, compromised in his fight for the win by the contact, retired from the race shortly after with a separate gearbox failure and said afterward that Sainz needed to 'look in the mirror.'
key_points: Sainz's Williams collided with Piastri's McLaren at Turn 2/3 in the Hungarian GP
Stewards ruled Sainz fully responsible, but gave a reduced 5-second penalty, not the usual 10
A broken blue-flag warning system meant Sainz wasn't told Piastri was coming past
Piastri called it 'one of the dumbest things' he's seen, and retired soon after with a gearbox failure

depth.background: Blue flags are shown to a slower car to tell its driver a faster car is about to lap or overtake, so they can move aside safely. Race stewards -- officials who police on-track incidents -- normally hand out a standard 10-second penalty to a driver judged fully at fault for causing a collision.

stories.title: Yorkshire crush Sussex by 184 runs in a One-Day Cup rout at Hove
stories.what_happened: At Hove, Yorkshire batted first after early rain reduced the match to 48 overs a side, and posted a commanding 325/7. Opener Adam Lyth hit a six off the very first short ball he faced en route to 21 from just seven balls before being caught. The innings was built around a dominant 160-run fourth-wicket partnership between Will Luxton, who scored a century, and Sam Whiteman, who made 74. In reply, Sussex collapsed to 140 all out in 27.5 overs, with seamer Ben Coad taking his maiden five-wicket haul in List A cricket. Yorkshire were awarded a 184-run win under the DLS method used to set fair targets in rain-affected matches.
key_points: Yorkshire posted **325/7** in a rain-shortened 48 overs, built on **Will Luxton's century**.
Luxton and **Sam Whiteman (74)** added **160 runs** together for the fourth wicket.
**Ben Coad** took a maiden List A **five-wicket haul** to help bowl Sussex out for just **140**.
Yorkshire won by **184 runs** on the DLS method, taking maximum points in the group.

depth.background: The One-Day Cup is English domestic cricket's 50-over county competition, running this summer alongside the more high-profile T20 Hundred tournament — it's where county players build List A credentials and it feeds England's broader domestic pathway. Yorkshire and Sussex are two of England's traditional first-class counties.

stories.title: Assam floods have now killed 66 people and affected 6.5 lakh more, as Union Minister Sonowal calls the situation 'extremely critical'
stories.what_happened: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal visited flood relief camps in Sivasagar district and described the situation as 'extremely critical,' as Assam's flood death toll for the season reached 66 and more than 6.5 lakh people across six districts remain affected. The state is running 274 relief camps and distribution centres, currently sheltering close to 19,000 displaced people, with the National and State Disaster Response Forces (NDRF/SDRF) continuing rescue and relief operations alongside the Centre.
key_points: Death toll from this year's Assam floods has reached 66
Over 6.5 lakh (650,000) people affected across six districts
Sivasagar is worst-hit, with roughly 3 lakh people impacted
274 relief camps are housing nearly 19,000 displaced people; NDRF/SDRF running rescues

depth.background: Assam faces destructive monsoon flooding most years, as the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell with heavy rain and overflow their banks across the state's low-lying districts. This year's flood season has been especially severe, compounding an already-active monsoon that has also triggered fresh IMD (India Meteorological Department) rain alerts elsewhere in the country this week.

stories.title: Chamika Karunaratne's 72* off 34 fires Galle Gallants to the top of the Lanka Premier League table
stories.what_happened: Galle Gallants posted 220 for 6, powered by an unbeaten 72 off 34 balls from Chamika Karunaratne, with useful contributions from Sam Harper, Nurul Hasan, Charith Asalanka and Sahan Arachchige. Dambulla Sixers got a promising start from Niroshan Dickwella in the chase but collapsed once wickets started falling, never mounting a serious threat beyond the powerplay, and Galle Gallants moved to the top of the table with eight points.
key_points: Galle Gallants posted 220/6, driven by Karunaratne's unbeaten 72 off just 34 balls
Dambulla Sixers fell well short in the chase after early wickets triggered a collapse
Win takes Galle Gallants clear at the top of the LPL points table with eight points
This is a separate, later match to the Jaffna-Kandy game already in the feed today

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise T20 tournament, now in its group stage with teams playing for a spot in the playoffs. Galle Gallants and Dambulla Sixers had already met once this LPL season, when Dambulla won comfortably — making this a rematch with the earlier result at stake.

stories.title: Surrey cruise past Northamptonshire by 6 wickets in the One-Day Cup
stories.what_happened: At Guildford, Northamptonshire batted first and posted 254/8 from their 50 overs. Surrey's batting lineup chased the target down with relative ease, reaching 258/4 in 43.1 overs to win by 6 wickets, with 41 balls to spare — a controlled run-chase rather than a nailbiter.
key_points: Northamptonshire posted **254/8** batting first at Guildford.
Surrey chased it down comfortably, reaching **258/4** in **43.1 overs**.
The win came by **6 wickets**, with **41 balls** still remaining.
It's another group-stage points boost for Surrey in the **2026 One-Day Cup**.

depth.background: This was a Group A fixture in the same 2026 One-Day Cup competition as the Yorkshire-Sussex match — English county cricket's 50-over format, running in parallel with The Hundred this summer.

stories.title: Championship leader Antonelli gets a triple penalty at the Hungarian GP and drops from pole pace to P7
stories.what_happened: During Saturday's qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Antonelli was investigated for not slowing sufficiently when yellow flags came out for Verstappen's spin — stewards found he lifted off the throttle only slightly and remained **faster through the corner than on his previous lap**, which is the definition of an unfair advantage under a caution. The standard penalty guideline for this offense is a five-place grid drop, but stewards reduced it to **three places**, noting Antonelli did make some reduction in speed and had limited time to react. He'd qualified fourth on raw pace but starts Sunday's race from **P7** as a result. A second, separate investigation was opened over Antonelli allegedly not following race-director instructions to drive at a reasonable pace during qualifying; that one resulted only in a formal warning, not a further grid penalty.
key_points: Stewards hit championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** with **three separate penalties** after Hungarian GP qualifying.
The main charge: failing to slow enough for **yellow flags** thrown when Max Verstappen spun in Q3.
He qualified 4th on raw pace but was dropped **three grid places to P7** for the race.
A second investigation added a **warning** for not following race-director instructions during qualifying.
Stewards said Antonelli did lift off the throttle, just **not enough** — sparing him the harsher 5-place penalty guideline.

depth.background: Yellow flags are shown at a track when there's a hazard ahead (here, Max Verstappen's Red Bull spinning off in Q3, the final and fastest qualifying segment) — drivers are required to slow down meaningfully when they see one, both for safety and to stop anyone gaining an unfair time advantage by racing through a caution zone. Kimi Antonelli has emerged as a genuine title contender this season, part of the storyline the reels covered yesterday about his 'rookie masterclass' during the summer-break report card.

stories.title: India name Sri Lanka Test squad: Jadeja returns, Bumrah in but fitness-watched, Gill captains
stories.what_happened: The BCCI announced India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour on Sunday, confirming **Shubman Gill** as captain and **KL Rahul** as his deputy. All-rounder **Ravindra Jadeja** is back in the squad after an extended absence from the format. **Jasprit Bumrah** has also been named, but his participation remains subject to a fitness call closer to the first Test — he's set to report to India's Centre of Excellence after resting his knee until July 30 — with **Mohammed Siraj** and **Prasidh Krishna** rounding out the pace options if Bumrah isn't ready. In the spin department, **Kuldeep Yadav** and uncapped left-armer **Manav Suthar** are the frontline picks. The two-Test series begins **August 15** in Sri Lanka.
key_points: **Shubman Gill** captains the squad with **KL Rahul** as vice-captain for the two-Test tour.
**Ravindra Jadeja** returns to the Test side after last featuring in an ODI back in January.
**Jasprit Bumrah** is included but remains fitness-watched, sharing the pace attack with **Mohammed Siraj** and **Prasidh Krishna**.
**Kuldeep Yadav** and **Manav Suthar** lead the spin options; the series starts **August 15**.

depth.background: India were due to name their Test squad for the upcoming two-match series in Sri Lanka, and the two names everyone was watching were **Ravindra Jadeja**, who hadn't played a Test in months, and **Jasprit Bumrah**, India's premier fast bowler, who picked up a left-knee injury while fielding during an ODI against England in Cardiff on July 17 and had been ruled out of full training until July 30.

thread.previously: As of Sunday, India's Test squad for Sri Lanka was still expected but not yet named, with Jadeja tipped to return and Bumrah's fitness still under review.
thread.changed: The squad has now actually been announced: Gill captains, Rahul is vice-captain, Jadeja is confirmed back in the squad, and Bumrah is named but still fitness-watched ahead of the August 15 series.

stories.title: Cadillac's brake trouble strikes again as both cars retire from the Hungarian Grand Prix
stories.what_happened: Cadillac suffered a double retirement at the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday, with both Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez failing to finish. Bottas retired on lap 15 after a fire broke out at his car's left front brake, which he said was caused by overheating that the team's cooling upgrades couldn't fully solve in Hungary's extreme conditions. Perez suffered a separate terminal mechanical issue and also failed to finish. The team had already started the race from the back of the grid — 21st and 22nd — after a difficult qualifying session the day before. This marks the second time this season brake failures have knocked out both Cadillac cars in the same race weekend, after a similar double failure at the Austrian Grand Prix. The team remains without a single championship point through more than half of its debut F1 season.
key_points: Both Cadillac cars — **Valtteri Bottas** and **Sergio Perez** — retired from the Hungarian Grand Prix with mechanical failures, after starting **dead last**.
Bottas retired on **lap 15** after a fire broke out at his car's **left front brake**, caused by overheating.
Bottas said the team's brake-cooling upgrades weren't enough to handle Hungary's extreme conditions.
It's the **second time this season** Cadillac cars have been knocked out by brake failures, after both retired early with the same issue at the **Austrian Grand Prix**.
Cadillac, F1's newest team, remains **without a single championship point** through more than half of its debut season.

depth.background: Cadillac is Formula 1's first new constructor since Haas joined in 2016, entering the 2026 season with backing from General Motors and Ferrari-supplied power units, with long-term plans to build its own engines. New teams typically endure a difficult first season as they learn to build and set up a competitive car from scratch, and Cadillac's rookie year has been rockier than most — reliability, not raw pace, has been the recurring problem, with brake failures already costing the team finishes at multiple races this year.

thread.previously: At Hungarian GP qualifying, Bottas and Perez lined up 21st and 22nd — dead last on the grid — continuing a rough rookie season marked by reliability issues, including brake failures that knocked both cars out early at the Austrian Grand Prix.
thread.changed: The bad qualifying became a bad race too: both cars retired from the Hungarian GP itself, with Bottas's retirement caused by another brake-related failure — a fire at his left-front brake — echoing the exact same problem that hit the team in Austria.

stories.title: Berlin's Pride attack suspect is shot dead by police after a 20-hour manhunt
stories.what_happened: On Saturday evening, a rented van drove into the crowd at Berlin's Christopher Street Day parade near Tiergarten park, killing one person and injuring 29 others. Police identified the driver as Abdul Ballout and launched a manhunt that lasted roughly 20 hours. He was found hiding in a garden in the western district of Spandau on Sunday evening, charged at emergency responders with a knife-like weapon, and was shot dead by police. Prosecutors confirmed his 2025 ISIS-related conviction and his more recent May 2026 arrest for allegedly preparing a violent attack, even though he had remained free. Germany's interior minister and prosecutors say all evidence points to Islamist extremism as the motive.
key_points: A rented van rammed into Berlin's Pride crowd near Tiergarten on **Saturday evening**, killing **one person** and injuring **29 others**.
The suspect, **21-year-old Abdul Ballout**, a German citizen of Lebanese descent, evaded police for **20 hours** before being cornered.
He was shot dead by police in Berlin's **Spandau** district on Sunday after charging at officers with a **bladed weapon**.
Prosecutors say Ballout was convicted in **2025** of trying to join ISIS and was arrested again in **May 2026** over an alleged plot to commit violence.
German officials have labeled it a likely **Islamist terror attack**.

depth.background: Christopher Street Day, Germany's version of a Pride parade, draws large crowds in cities across the country every summer. Prosecutors say Ballout traveled toward Syria in 2025 hoping to join ISIS, was caught and served under two years in prison, then returned to Germany in November 2025. He was arrested again in **May 2026** on suspicion of preparing a serious act of violence, but was not held in custody afterward — a gap that is now central to the fallout from this attack. Berlin has also seen a documented rise in anti-LGBT hate incidents in recent years.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants thrash Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: Manchester Super Giants posted 187 for 5 from their 100 balls and then bowled out Birmingham Phoenix for just 100, winning by 87 runs in the competition's 7th match of the men's season.
key_points: Manchester Super Giants posted 187/5 in their 100 balls
Birmingham Phoenix collapsed to just 100 all out in reply
87-run margin is one of the more lopsided results of this year's Hundred
Result strengthens Super Giants' position in the men's competition table

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-form, 100-balls-per-side cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments side by side each summer as a faster, more broadcast-friendly alternative to T20. Manchester Super Giants and Birmingham Phoenix are two of the eight men's franchises competing this season.

stories.title: 'How the hell did I end up here?' — Verstappen stunned by his own damaged-car podium as Red Bull says it never gave him a car to attack with
stories.what_happened: After qualifying poorly and picking up car damage during the Hungarian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen finished 2nd — a result he said left him baffled, telling reporters 'I don't understand how we are second' and 'How the hell did I end up here?' Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies backed up Verstappen's surprise, saying the team 'never managed to give Max... a car they could attack with' this weekend and that the car's behaviour was unlike stronger recent races such as Spa or Austria.
key_points: Verstappen said he was 'still shocked' by finishing 2nd after a poor qualifying and race damage
He called it 'a bit of an over-performance compared to what we expected'
Team boss Laurent Mekies said Red Bull 'never managed to give Max... a car he could attack with'
Mekies said this weekend's car behaviour was completely different from stronger races like Spa or Austria

depth.background: Red Bull has struggled with inconsistent car performance across the 2026 season, sometimes competitive and sometimes off the pace from one race to the next, making it hard for the team and Verstappen to predict results race to race. Laurent Mekies, who now leads Red Bull's F1 team, has been managing the team through this stretch of unpredictable form.

stories.title: Toto Wolff launches a 'Teletubbies' rant at rival teams over a blue-flag failure that nearly cost Antonelli the Hungarian GP podium
stories.what_happened: A system fault during the Hungarian Grand Prix meant the automatic blue-flag light panels stopped working, so backmarkers could only be warned manually — and several didn't react in time, holding up Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli as he tried to catch Max Verstappen for 2nd place in the closing laps while defending from Lewis Hamilton behind him. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff blasted rival teams afterwards, saying it was 'disgraceful' that 'some of the Teletubbies engineers... sitting on the pit walls' failed to tell their drivers what was happening, adding that lapped cars 'defending is just not acceptable.'
key_points: A light-panel system fault meant blue flags could only be shown manually to backmarkers
Antonelli was held up by slow lapped cars while chasing Verstappen for 2nd late in the race
Wolff called rival teams' pit-wall engineers 'Teletubbies' for not warning drivers in time
Antonelli still held on for 3rd, extending his championship lead to 50 points

depth.background: Blue flags are shown to backmarkers (cars a lap or more behind) to tell them to let faster, competing cars past without a fight. Normally this is triggered automatically by trackside light panels, which teams and drivers rely on to know when to yield.

stories.title: West Indies build a commanding 303/7 at lunch on Day 2 of the Pakistan Test
stories.what_happened: Resuming Day 2 from an overnight 194 for 3, West Indies added 109 runs in the first session to reach 303 for 7 by lunch, in 96 overs, despite losing four more wickets along the way. Shai Hope remained unbeaten on 89, anchoring the innings, while lower-order batter Shamar Joseph provided late fireworks with 23 not out off just 12 balls, hitting four boundaries and a six. Pakistan's Aamer Jamal was the most successful bowler in the session, taking a wicket for 81 runs.
key_points: West Indies resumed Day 2 at 194/3 and reached 303/7 by the lunch break
Shai Hope anchored the innings with an unbeaten 89
Shamar Joseph blazed 23 off just 12 balls with four fours and a six
It's a big recovery from a rain-hit 23/1 at the same stage on Day 1

depth.background: West Indies and Pakistan are playing the first Test of their series at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad — a brand-new Test venue. Day 1 was badly disrupted by rain and tight bowling from Pakistan's Mohammad Abbas, which restricted West Indies to just 23 for 1 at the close.

thread.previously: We reported that rain and disciplined bowling from Mohammad Abbas had restricted West Indies to just 23 for 1 at the close of a truncated Day 1.
thread.changed: West Indies have recovered strongly on Day 2, reaching 303 for 7 by lunch on the back of Shai Hope's unbeaten 89 and a late blitz from Shamar Joseph.

stories.title: Lando Norris wins a chaotic Hungarian GP for his first victory of his title-defense season
stories.what_happened: Norris took **pole position** but lost the lead at the start to teammate Oscar Piastri. Piastri then ran into trouble in the first sector when he made contact with Carlos Sainz's Williams, forcing Piastri to retire and triggering a Virtual Safety Car. Norris capitalized, reclaiming and then controlling the lead for the rest of the race, ultimately crossing the line roughly **15 seconds clear of Max Verstappen's Red Bull**, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli completing the podium in third. The Piastri-Sainz clash and a separate late pit-lane speeding penalty for Lewis Hamilton (which cost him a likely podium finish) were among the other major storylines of a dramatic afternoon.
key_points: Norris beat **Max Verstappen by around 15 seconds** and Mercedes' **Kimi Antonelli** for 3rd.
It's Norris's **first win of 2026** — his first as a reigning World Champion defending the title.
McLaren teammate **Oscar Piastri retired** after a first-sector clash with Williams' Carlos Sainz.
Norris lost the lead off the start from pole but reclaimed it after the Piastri-Sainz incident opened the door.

depth.background: Norris enters 2026 as the reigning **F1 World Champion**, having won last year's title with McLaren. The Hungarian Grand Prix is held at the **Hungaroring** near Budapest, a tight, twisty circuit that makes overtaking hard and rewards clean starts and strategy. Going into this race, Norris had yet to win in his title-defense season, while rivals including Verstappen, Antonelli and Ferrari's Hamilton had all been in podium contention across the year.

stories.title: Berlin Pride attack suspect shot dead by police after a daylong manhunt
stories.what_happened: Around 10pm on Saturday, July 25, a white van drove into a crowd of pedestrians in Berlin's Tiergarten park, near the closing concert of the city's Pride festival, before crashing into a tree. One woman was killed and 29 people were injured, several critically. The driver fled on foot; police named him as Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old German citizen of Lebanese descent, and launched a large-scale manhunt. On Sunday evening, officers cornered him at an allotment-garden site in the Spandau district; police say he charged at them with a stabbing weapon, and they shot him dead.
key_points: A van rammed a crowd at Berlin's Pride festival Saturday night, killing one woman and injuring 29
Suspect Abdul Ballout, 21, fled on foot; police launched a nationwide manhunt
He was shot dead Sunday evening in Berlin's Spandau district after charging officers with a blade
Germany's interior minister calls it a suspected Islamist terror attack

depth.background: Berlin's Christopher Street Day (CSD) — the city's biggest LGBTQ+ Pride celebration — draws hundreds of thousands of people every summer to march and celebrate near the Brandenburg Gate. Germany has been on edge about vehicle-ramming and knife attacks tied to Islamist extremism after a string of similar incidents at Christmas markets and other public gatherings in recent years, and security at large public events has been tightened accordingly.

stories.title: Hamilton fined five seconds for going 0.1 km/h over the pit-lane limit — and it cost him a place at the Hungarian GP
stories.what_happened: Hamilton pitted from second place on lap 56 under a virtual safety car triggered by Oscar Piastri's gearbox failure while leading. Ferrari has since explained that Hamilton pressed his pit-lane speed limiter button slightly too early, causing his car to register 80.1 km/h — 0.1 km/h over the legal limit — as he entered the pit lane. Stewards handed him a 5-second time penalty, added to his finishing time, which dropped him from an on-track 4th place to 5th, just 0.7 seconds behind teammate Charles Leclerc.
key_points: Hamilton was clocked at 80.1 km/h in an 80 km/h pit lane during the race
The 5-second penalty dropped him from 4th to 5th, behind teammate Charles Leclerc
Ferrari says Hamilton hit the pit-lane speed-limiter button too early, causing the tiny overspeed
It's his second penalty of the Hungarian GP weekend, after a grid penalty from qualifying

depth.background: F1 enforces a strict speed limit inside the pit lane at every circuit — at the Hungaroring it's 80 km/h — both for the safety of mechanics and to stop drivers gaining an unfair advantage. Cars are timed electronically, so even a fractional breach is caught and penalized automatically.

stories.title: Verstappen's stunning lap-16 divebomb on Hamilton headlines a wild Hungarian GP
stories.what_happened: On lap 16 of the Hungarian Grand Prix, Verstappen launched a daring dive down the inside of Hamilton into Turn 1, despite running the harder, theoretically slower tyre compound. Hamilton later said he didn't see Verstappen coming and admitted the Dutchman caught him out. The move was crucial to Verstappen's race, helping him climb the order to finish second behind race winner Lando Norris, after Oscar Piastri's late gearbox failure while leading reshuffled the podium.
key_points: Verstappen pulled off what many are calling the overtake of the 2026 F1 season on lap 16
He dived down the inside of Hamilton's Ferrari into Turn 1 despite running the harder tyre
Hamilton admitted he 'wasn't paying attention' and didn't see Verstappen coming
The move helped Verstappen climb from P4 on the grid to finish P2

depth.background: Max Verstappen started the Hungarian Grand Prix from fourth on the grid after a below-par qualifying, while Lewis Hamilton was running ahead of him in his Ferrari. Overtaking at the tight, twisty Hungaroring circuit is notoriously difficult — it's nicknamed 'Monaco without the walls' because cars struggle to pass each other there.

stories.title: Aston Martin's Hungary upgrade lifts Alonso into Q3 for the first time all year — with his stay-or-retire decision looming after the break
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin brought its first real upgrade package of the year to the Hungarian Grand Prix, and it showed: Alonso reached Q3 in qualifying for the first time all season and finished the race in P14, a clear step up from where the car has run most of the year. Team principal Adrian Newey said the goal now is "respectability" rather than results, while Alonso said he's hopeful of a "new start of the championship" in the second half, with a fresh engine arriving at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort.
key_points: Alonso reached Q3 for the first time this season and finished P14 on Sunday
Aston Martin brought its first major upgrade package of the year to Hungary
Team boss Adrian Newey is targeting "respectability", not wins, for now
Alonso, 44, says he'll decide his own future only after the summer break

depth.background: Aston Martin has struggled through a difficult 2026 season, prompting a long-planned upgrade push built around new technical boss Adrian Newey's designs. Alonso, now 44 and out of contract at the end of 2026, has repeatedly said he won't decide whether to continue racing or retire until after the summer break, keeping speculation about an Alpine return or retirement alive all year.

stories.title: Max Verstappen wins the Hungarian Grand Prix after starting only 10th on the grid
stories.what_happened: Verstappen carved through the field at the Hungaroring to win the Hungarian Grand Prix from 10th on the grid, his 8th win of the 2026 season and the 28th of his career. Lewis Hamilton brought his Ferrari home 2nd, with Mercedes' George Russell 3rd. Over team radio after the chequered flag, a stunned Verstappen said: "Amazing result. Who would have thought when we woke up that we were going to win the race."
key_points: Verstappen won from 10th on the grid — his 8th win of the season
Lando Norris had taken pole, with Hamilton and Antonelli both hit by grid penalties
Hamilton finished 2nd for Ferrari, Russell 3rd for Mercedes
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc lost a likely strong result to a strategy call

depth.background: Saturday's qualifying at the Hungaroring in Budapest was chaotic: Lando Norris took pole for McLaren by just 0.012 seconds over Lewis Hamilton, before stewards handed grid penalties to both Hamilton and championship leader Kimi Antonelli for separate incidents, reshuffling Sunday's starting order. Red Bull's Max Verstappen — this season's most successful driver by wins — had a poor qualifying and lined up well back in 10th, a rare off-day for the team.

stories.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now live after a below-top-2 Hungarian GP
stories.what_happened: Verstappen finished the Hungarian Grand Prix — the summer-break-defining race — well outside the championship's top two, confirming what had looked likely for weeks: he can now exercise his contractual release clause any time between August and October to leave Red Bull for 2027, rather than seeing out a long-term deal.
key_points: Verstappen sits P7, ~113 points off championship leader Antonelli
Hungarian GP was the exact reference race written into his contract
He can now activate the release clause between August and October
Aston Martin, boosted by Adrian Newey and a new Honda deal, is seen as the leading suitor

depth.background: Red Bull reportedly wrote a release clause into Verstappen's contract because of his long-running unease with F1's overhauled 2026 technical regulations, which he has compared unfavorably to 'Mario Kart' racing. The clause was designed as a pressure valve given that discomfort, with Aston Martin — now allied with car designer Adrian Newey and a new exclusive Honda engine deal — widely seen as his most likely destination if he leaves.

thread.previously: Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract includes a release clause letting him leave for 2027 if he isn't ranked in the championship's top two by the time F1 reaches its summer break, with the Hungarian Grand Prix serving as the key reference race.
thread.changed: The Hungarian GP — the actual reference race — has now been run. Verstappen sits seventh in the standings, roughly 113 points behind runaway leader Kimi Antonelli, comfortably outside the top two. That confirms the clause is now active, and he can formally choose to trigger it any time between August and October.

prev_ref.title: Verstappen can now trigger an exit clause to leave Red Bull for 2027 — if he's not top-2 by August

stories.title: London Spirit Women hand unbeaten Trent Rockets their first defeat of the season, as Kapp and de Klerk star in Nottingham
stories.what_happened: In a rematch at Nottingham, London Spirit Women beat Trent Rockets Women by 5 wickets, inflicting the Rockets' first defeat of the season and picking up Spirit's first win. South African all-rounders Marizanne Kapp and Nadine de Klerk were the standout performers: Kapp took a 3-wicket haul, including an opening spell where she didn't concede a run off the bat in her first 10 deliveries, while de Klerk struck the match-winning six on her way to an unbeaten 41, an innings that included two fours and three sixes.
key_points: London Spirit Women won by 5 wickets — their first win of this Hundred season
It's Trent Rockets Women's first loss of the season, ending their unbeaten run
Marizanne Kapp took 3 wickets, including an opening burst where she didn't concede a run off the bat in her first 10 balls
Nadine de Klerk hit the match-winning six, finishing unbeaten on 41 with two fours and three sixes

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format franchise cricket competition, played alongside separate men's and women's tournaments by the same eight city-based teams. Trent Rockets Women had been in strong form this season, while London Spirit Women had struggled to find a win — the two sides had already met once this season at Lord's, where Trent Rockets won convincingly.

stories.title: India complete a 3-0 T20I sweep of Zimbabwe as Sooryavanshi wins Player of the Series
stories.what_happened: India posted 192 for 5 batting first, with Sooryavanshi top-scoring with 81 off 49 balls, before bowling Zimbabwe out for 157 for 7 to win by 35 runs and complete a 3-0 series sweep. Sooryavanshi, who scored 151 runs across the series, was named Player of the Series as well as Player of the Match for the decider.
key_points: India beat Zimbabwe by 35 runs to win the 3rd T20I and the series 3-0
Teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit 81 off 49 balls, his best T20I score
Sooryavanshi finished with 151 series runs and won Player of the Series
It's Shreyas Iyer's first series win since taking over as India's T20I captain

depth.background: India toured Zimbabwe for a three-match T20I series under new captain Shreyas Iyer, with the series offering a testing ground for fringe players, including 18-year-old opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, before India's next major assignments. India had already won the first two matches of the series heading into this decider.

stories.title: Jaffna Kings crush Kandy Royals by 93 runs in the Lanka Premier League
stories.what_happened: Jaffna Kings beat Kandy Royals by 93 runs in Match 13 of the 2026 Lanka Premier League at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium. Jaffna posted 199/4 from their 20 overs before bowling Kandy out for 106 in 18.2 overs. Kamil Mishara was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Jaffna Kings posted 199/4 in their 20 overs at Rangiri Dambulla
Kandy Royals were bowled out for just 106 in 18.2 overs
Kamil Mishara named Player of the Match
Result keeps Jaffna Kings among the LPL 2026 pace-setters

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise Twenty20 tournament, running alongside similar leagues elsewhere (India's IPL, the Caribbean's CPL) that give international and local players a short, high-intensity domestic season outside their national team commitments.

stories.title: F1 heads into its summer break with 17 drivers out of contract and the Norris-Piastri title fight wide open
stories.what_happened: F1 heads into its summer break (starting July 27, with no race until the Dutch Grand Prix on August 23) with 17 of the grid's driver contracts expiring at the end of 2026 — all but five drivers are unsigned for 2027. Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract contains an exit clause that has now become active after the team failed to keep him inside the top two in the championship, adding fresh uncertainty to the sport's biggest storyline.
key_points: F1's summer break officially begins July 27, running until the Dutch GP on August 23
Only five drivers — Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Leclerc and Gasly — have deals beyond this season
Max Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active after a below-top-2 result run
The next month of driver-market speculation could reshape multiple teams' 2027 lineups

depth.background: Formula 1 contracts for the following season are typically negotiated and announced through the middle of the current year, and the summer break — a mandated shutdown of race-team factories — has traditionally been when driver moves get finalized, because there are no races to distract from the negotiations.

stories.title: George Russell's Mercedes suffers a mystery power failure on the Hungarian GP grid — and a grid penalty is now looming
stories.what_happened: During qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix, George Russell cracked the sump on his Mercedes power unit after running over a kerb at Turn 4, causing a water leak that forced the team to fit a brand-new engine ahead of the race. On the grid before the race start, that new unit developed an unrelated and previously unseen fault — the engine began revving unpredictably and the throttle stopped responding for several seconds, just before lights-out. Russell had to fight through an anti-stall situation as the rest of the field pulled away, but recovered through the field to finish seventh. Because this was his fourth power-unit change of the season — his full allowance — any further change this year will cost him a grid-position penalty at a future race. Mercedes has opened an investigation into the cause.
key_points: Russell's Mercedes had a **cracked power-unit sump** in qualifying, forcing an engine change before the race.
On the grid, the **replacement engine began revving erratically** and the throttle briefly stopped responding — a fault he says he'd never felt before.
Despite the scare, Russell recovered from near-last to finish **P7**.
He has now used his **full season allowance of four power units**, meaning his next change will trigger a **grid-position penalty**.
Mercedes has launched an internal investigation, with Russell publicly calling for the team to get to the bottom of it.

depth.background: In modern F1, each driver is allotted a limited number of power-unit components per season (typically around four full engines); using more than the allowance triggers automatic grid-penalty drops, since the rule is meant to control costs and discourage teams from treating engines as disposable. Mercedes has had a mixed 2026 season on power-unit reliability, and Russell has previously had to take a fresh unit after a failure earlier in the year, meaning Hungary's incident pushed him right to the edge of his seasonal limit.

stories.title: Mirabai Chanu scripts history with a third straight Commonwealth Games weightlifting gold
stories.what_happened: Chanu won India's first gold medal of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games in the women's 48kg weightlifting final, lifting a combined 190kg — a new Games record — to secure the title. She set a Commonwealth record of 85kg in the snatch and a Games record of 105kg in the clean and jerk. It is her third consecutive individual Commonwealth Games gold in the same weight category.
key_points: Chanu wins the women's 48kg gold with a Games-record 190kg total lift
She set a Commonwealth record 85kg snatch and a Games-record 105kg clean and jerk
It's her third consecutive individual Commonwealth Games gold medal
Only India's Vinesh Phogat has managed three straight individual CWG golds before her

depth.background: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, an Olympic medallist weightlifter from Manipur, carried India's flag at the Commonwealth Games 2026 opening ceremony in Glasgow. She had already won consecutive Commonwealth Games golds in the women's 48kg category at the two previous editions, making this event a bid for a rare 'three-peat' — winning the same individual event at three straight Games, something very few athletes from any country manage because of the toll repeated peak performances take across years.

stories.title: Piastri's Hungarian GP heartbreak: gearbox failure ends his race while leading, as Norris wins and Antonelli extends his F1 title lead
stories.what_happened: Oscar Piastri lost the race lead early after tangling with backmarker Carlos Sainz's Williams, then was forced to retire on lap 56 with a gearbox failure while running second — a bitter result after leading much of the race. Teammate Lando Norris held on to win from pole, 15 seconds clear of Max Verstappen, with Antonelli completing the podium in third. Lewis Hamilton crossed fourth but was demoted to fifth after a 5-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane.
key_points: Oscar Piastri retired on lap 56 with a gearbox failure while running second
An earlier clash with Carlos Sainz's Williams had already cost him the lead
Teammate Lando Norris converted pole into his first win of the season
Kimi Antonelli's podium stretches his championship lead to 50 points over Hamilton

depth.background: McLaren has been the class of the field for much of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but the Hungarian Grand Prix — the last race before F1's summer break — turned into a story of what could have been for one of its two drivers. Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes' rising star, arrived at Hungaroring already holding the championship lead, chasing a feat no driver has managed since 1950: winning the title on home soil.

stories.title: India chase a clean sweep as the series-deciding 3rd T20I in Harare gets underway
stories.what_happened: The third and final T20I between Zimbabwe and India begins today in Harare. With the series already won 2-0, India are playing for a clean sweep (3-0) rather than the series itself, while Zimbabwe look to avoid a whitewash and salvage some pride on home soil.
key_points: India already lead the 3-match T20I series 2-0
3rd and final T20I starts today in Harare
A win would complete a clean sweep of the series
India's 2nd T20I win came by 90 runs, with Ishan Kishan named Player of the Match

depth.background: India toured Zimbabwe with a fringe/second-string squad, giving newer players a chance to press their case for a fuller national recall. India won the first T20I by 7 wickets and the second by 90 runs, already sealing the series with a match to spare.

stories.title: F1 finds a workaround for its canceled Bahrain race: Malaysia will host it instead, in October
stories.what_happened: F1 and the FIA jointly confirmed that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit — a former F1 host that hasn't held a round since 2017 — will stage this year's Bahrain Grand Prix on **October 2-4**, under the unusual title 'Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.' Bahrain is covering much of the costs and keeping its naming rights and title sponsor, even though the race physically happens in Kuala Lumpur. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said the sport was delighted to confirm the arrangement. The race slots into a grueling stretch of the calendar, forming a triple-header with the Azerbaijan and Singapore Grands Prix that runs from September 26 through October 11 — three races in three different countries across just over two weeks. With this addition, the 2026 F1 calendar totals **23 races**, and this is the only one of the conflict-affected races that got relocated rather than simply canceled.
key_points: F1 and the FIA confirmed **Malaysia's Sepang circuit** will host this year's Bahrain Grand Prix.
The race is rebranded **'Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia'** and runs **October 2-4**.
It slots into a brutal **triple-header** with Azerbaijan and Singapore, running **September 26 to October 11**.
The original April Bahrain and Saudi Arabia races were scrapped outright due to the **escalating Middle East conflict**.
The 2026 calendar now sits at **23 races**, with this the only event that couldn't simply be rescheduled in-region.

depth.background: Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were both supposed to host Grands Prix earlier in the 2026 F1 season, but the sharp escalation in Middle East fighting this year (the same US-Iran conflict covered above) made racing in the region too risky, and both events were canceled rather than merely postponed. Bahrain still hoped to salvage its race by moving it later in the year, to October, but the continued conflict ruled that out too — so instead of losing the race entirely, F1 and Bahrain struck a deal to run it somewhere else while keeping Bahrain's name and sponsorship on it.

stories.title: Gunfire and vandalism hit two Jewish-owned Toronto bakeries in suspected hate crime
stories.what_happened: Toronto police were called shortly after 8am Sunday to a Kiva's Bagel Bakery location near Yonge Street and St. Clair Avenue West after reports of a shattered window; investigators found evidence a firearm had been discharged, though no one was injured. Less than 20 minutes later, officers responded to a second Kiva's location about 14km north, near Bathurst Street and Steeles Avenue West, after another window was broken. Police are examining whether the two incidents are connected and are treating both as suspected hate-motivated offences.
key_points: Two Kiva's Bagel Bakery locations in Toronto hit within 20 minutes on Sunday morning
One had a window struck by gunfire; no one was hurt
Toronto Police's Hate Crime Unit is treating both as suspected hate-motivated offences
Mayor Olivia Chow called them 'targeted attacks' on a Jewish-owned business

depth.background: Antisemitic incidents — vandalism, threats, and attacks on Jewish-owned businesses and institutions — have risen sharply across North America and Europe since the Israel-Hamas war began in 2023, and have stayed elevated through the on-and-off Gaza ceasefire that followed. Toronto, home to Canada's largest Jewish community, has recorded a string of such incidents at synagogues, schools, and shops over the past two years. Kiva's is a well-known local bagel chain with several locations across the city.

stories.title: Cadillac holds the cards on Perez and Bottas as F1's newest team plots its 2027 lineup
stories.what_happened: As Formula 1's driver market heats up ahead of the summer break, reports indicate that **both Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas hold options with Cadillac to continue into the 2027 season**, though neither has been officially confirmed yet. Perez returned to the grid in 2026 after sitting out 2025 following his Red Bull exit, while Bottas brings experience from his years at Mercedes and Sauber/Audi. Cadillac's decision matters beyond its own garage: if the team exercises its options and keeps both drivers, it would **close off two of the grid's most senior seats** to the wave of younger drivers -- including Red Bull juniors like Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad -- who are hoping to move up in 2027.
key_points: Both **Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas** are understood to have options to continue at Cadillac for 2027
Neither driver's **2027 seat is officially confirmed** yet
Cadillac is F1's **newest team**, having joined the grid in 2026
Junior drivers **Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad** are among those who could push for seats elsewhere if the pair are retained

depth.background: Cadillac became Formula 1's newest constructor when it joined the grid for the 2026 season, adding an 11th team to the championship. It signed Sergio Perez -- dropped by Red Bull after four seasons alongside Verstappen -- and veteran Valtteri Bottas to lead its debut campaign. As a new team, Cadillac's driver lineup decisions for 2027 carry extra weight, since they'll shape how the team builds its identity and competitiveness in only its second season.

stories.title: US and Iran quietly extend their strike pause for a second day as a Hormuz shipping compromise takes shape
stories.what_happened: The US paused attacks on Iran on Sunday for a second consecutive day, and Tehran said it had done so too. Deputy foreign ministers from Iran and Oman met in Tehran over the past two days specifically to discuss the Strait of Hormuz. A regional mediator called the mutual pause a "positive signal." The emerging compromise centers on Iran managing vessel transit through Hormuz with fewer restrictions on ships in exchange for the ceasefire holding.
key_points: US and Iran both held fire for a second straight day
Iran and Oman's deputy foreign ministers met in Tehran on the Strait
Compromise floated: Iran manages tanker transit, fewer restrictions on ships
Trump letting talks run "at every level" through the weekend

depth.background: A nearly two-week escalation began when Iran fired on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, prompting the US to strike Iranian coastal areas and infrastructure. An earlier interim ceasefire had been undermined by renewed exchanges of fire. Oman has long served as the back-channel mediator between the US and Iran, which have no direct diplomatic relations.

thread.previously: The US had just paused strikes for the first time as Oman-brokered talks began, with both sides testing whether de-escalation could hold.
thread.changed: The pause has now held for a second straight day, and negotiators are discussing a concrete compromise: Iran would manage tanker transit through Hormuz with fewer restrictions in exchange for the ceasefire sticking.

stories.title: India's Commonwealth Games Day 3: lawn bowls pair wins, boxer advances, but swimmers miss the final
stories.what_happened: On Day 3 (July 26), India's women's lawn bowls pair of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinky Singh won their sectional match against Namibia. In boxing, Sachin Siwach moved a step closer to a medal in the men's 60kg category. But in the pool, swimmers Dhakshan Shashikumar and Aryan Nehra failed to qualify for the men's 400m freestyle final, while the men's 4x200m freestyle relay team was still to swim its heats later in the day.
key_points: Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinky Singh win women's pairs lawn bowls vs Namibia
Boxer Sachin Siwach moves a step closer to a medal in men's 60kg
Dhakshan Shashikumar and Aryan Nehra fail to make the men's 400m freestyle final
Men's 4x200m freestyle relay heats still to come later in the day

depth.background: India arrived at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games with two bronze medals already banked — including one from Lovlina Borgohain's boxing bye into the semifinals — and is chasing a broader medal push across boxing, gymnastics, swimming and lawn bowls through the Games' first week.

stories.title: Estranged Thackeray cousins share a stage in Mumbai to celebrate the NEET protest movement's win
stories.what_happened: On Sunday, the two cousins jointly led a large rally at Shivaji Park in Dadar, Mumbai, that drew thousands of supporters, framing it as a celebration of the student protest movement that forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation a day earlier over the NEET-UG paper-leak scandal. They were joined on stage by Shiv Sena (UBT) figures including Aaditya Thackeray and Sanjay Raut, and NCP (Sharad Pawar faction) leader Rohit Pawar. Raj Thackeray told the crowd the protest's success 'proved that Gen Z can challenge the government,' and both leaders paid tribute to NEET aspirants who died by suicide during the crisis.
key_points: Uddhav and Raj Thackeray jointly led a rally at Mumbai's Shivaji Park on Sunday
Thousands gathered to celebrate Education Minister Pradhan's resignation as a student-movement victory
It's a rare public reunion for the two cousins, who lead rival Shiv Sena (UBT) and MNS parties
They paid tribute to NEET aspirants who died by suicide during the crisis

depth.background: Uddhav Thackeray (Shiv Sena UBT) and his cousin Raj Thackeray (MNS) lead rival breakaway factions of Maharashtra's once-united Thackeray political family and have mostly kept their distance politically for years, occasionally coming together only on specific shared causes such as opposition to Hindi-language mandates in schools.

thread.previously: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Education Minister on Saturday after weeks of protest pressure over the NEET-UG paper leak.
thread.changed: Maharashtra's rival Thackeray cousins jointly rallied thousands in Mumbai to celebrate the resignation as a win for the student movement — a rare political reunion.

stories.title: On Kargil Vijay Diwas, India's defence minister tells Pakistan: 'we design chips, you produce suicide bombers'
stories.what_happened: India marked the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas on Sunday. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to the soldiers who died in the 1999 war, calling their sacrifice a lasting source of national pride. In Drass, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh laid a wreath at the war memorial, inaugurated a virtual version of the memorial, and delivered a pointed message to Pakistan: "While India is manufacturing semiconductors, Pakistan is producing suicide bombers," contrasting India's start-up and tech ecosystem with what he called Pakistan's 'terror ecosystem.' He also warned that the enemy 'still resorts to proxy war and infiltration' and said India could respond to any Pakistani 'misadventure' far more harshly than Pakistan can imagine.
key_points: 27th anniversary of India's 1999 Kargil War victory over Pakistani intrusion
President Murmu and PM Modi led tributes to soldiers at war memorials nationwide
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, speaking in Drass, contrasted India's tech rise with Pakistan's militancy
Singh said India can hit back 'far harsher' at any future Pakistani provocation

depth.background: In summer 1999, Pakistani soldiers and militants secretly crossed the Line of Control (the de facto India-Pakistan border in disputed Kashmir) and occupied high mountain posts above the town of Kargil in Ladakh. India fought a two-month war, Operation Vijay, to reclaim those peaks at extreme altitude, losing over 500 soldiers before declaring victory on July 26, 1999. India has marked that date as Kargil Vijay Diwas ('Victory Day') every year since, with the main ceremony held at the Kargil War Memorial in Drass, near the old battlefield.

stories.title: UN chief Guterres demands the immediate removal of all remaining Syria sanctions
stories.what_happened: UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Sunday, wrapping up a two-day visit to Syria, that 'all these sanctions must be removed immediately,' while welcoming the steps already taken to ease them. He argued continued restrictions are choking off the economic recovery and reconstruction Syria needs after over a decade of war. The World Bank has estimated rebuilding Syria's shattered infrastructure and institutions could cost around $216 billion.
key_points: Guterres made the call at the end of a two-day visit to Damascus
Western countries, including the US, have already eased some sanctions since Assad's fall
World Bank estimates Syria's post-war reconstruction could cost $216 billion
Investors remain cautious despite the partial easing so far

depth.background: Syria's sanctions were imposed by the US, EU and others over decades of human-rights abuses under the Assad family's rule, which ended when Bashar al-Assad was toppled in December 2024. Syria's new authorities have spent the time since trying to rebuild a state shattered by more than 13 years of civil war and reconnect the country to a global financial system it was locked out of. Western governments have gradually eased — but not fully lifted — sanctions, wary of how the new government will govern.

stories.title: PM Modi marks 26th Kargil Vijay Diwas in his 136th Mann Ki Baat address
stories.what_happened: In the 136th episode of Mann Ki Baat, PM Modi paid tribute to the soldiers who fought in the 1999 Kargil War, calling their valour a lasting source of national pride, on the 26th anniversary of India's victory. He also used the address to spotlight the 'Catch The Rain' rainwater-harvesting campaign running since early July, the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' tree-plantation drive, a plastic-recycling 'Waste to Wealth' initiative from Sitamarhi in Bihar, and India's growing defence exports — citing a recent BrahMos and Astra missile agreement with Indonesia. Separately, a large tribute march with over a thousand participants — veterans, martyrs' families, and youth — was held in Drass, Ladakh, near the original Kargil battle sites.
key_points: July 26 marks 26 years since India's 1999 Kargil War victory
Modi paid tribute to soldiers in his monthly Mann Ki Baat radio address
He also highlighted rainwater harvesting, tree plantation, and a Bihar recycling project
A tribute march (Padyatra) was held in Drass, Ladakh, near the old battle sites

depth.background: Mann Ki Baat ('from the heart') is PM Modi's monthly radio address, running since 2014, where he talks directly to citizens about social initiatives and national moments — this was its 136th episode. Kargil Vijay Diwas marks India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War, fought in the high-altitude Kargil district of Ladakh after Pakistani forces and militants crossed the Line of Control; it's observed every July 26.

stories.title: A NASA astronaut and two Russian cosmonauts land back on Earth after 241 days on the space station
stories.what_happened: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev returned to Earth on Sunday, July 26, after **241 days** in space aboard the ISS. Their Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft undocked from the station at 2:03am and made a parachute-assisted landing in a remote area southeast of Zhezkazgan, Kazakhstan, at 5:27am CDT (3:27pm local Kazakhstan time). Over the mission, the crew circled the Earth **3,856 times** and travelled more than **102 million miles**. They had launched to the ISS on November 27, 2025. It was the first flight to space for both Williams and Mikaev, while Kud-Sverchkov was on his second mission.
key_points: NASA's Chris Williams and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev landed safely in Kazakhstan on Sunday after **241 days** aboard the International Space Station.
Their Soyuz MS-28 capsule made a parachute-assisted landing near **Zhezkazgan, Kazakhstan**, ending a mission that began on **November 27, 2025**.
The crew orbited Earth **3,856 times**, covering more than **102 million miles**.
It was the first spaceflight for both Williams and Mikaev, and the second for Kud-Sverchkov.
The mission is one of the routine crew rotations that keep the ISS staffed — a partnership that has kept running even as US-Russia relations have soured elsewhere.

depth.background: The International Space Station (ISS) has been continuously crewed by rotating teams of astronauts and cosmonauts since 2000, in a rare corner of US-Russia cooperation that has largely continued through wars and sanctions elsewhere. Crews typically fly up on Russia's Soyuz spacecraft or America's SpaceX Crew Dragon and stay for six months to a year, running science experiments in microgravity that can't be done on Earth. This mission, Soyuz MS-28, launched in late November 2025 and is one of many routine handovers that keep the station running.

stories.title: Sarnath, where Buddha gave his first sermon, becomes India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site
stories.what_happened: UNESCO's World Heritage Committee, at its 48th session in Busan, South Korea, voted on July 25 to inscribe the 'Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath' on the World Heritage List, citing its stupas, temples and monastic remains built up over centuries of royal and religious patronage. It becomes India's 45th World Heritage Site overall and the fourth in Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the news on Sunday, calling it a moment of pride for the country.
key_points: Inscribed July 25 by UNESCO's World Heritage Committee, meeting in Busan, South Korea
It's India's 45th World Heritage Site, and Uttar Pradesh's 4th
Sarnath is where Buddha delivered his first sermon after enlightenment
PM Modi called it 'a proud moment for every Indian'

depth.background: UNESCO's World Heritage List recognises sites of outstanding cultural or natural value to humanity, and inscription can bring conservation funding, tourism, and international prestige. Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, is one of Buddhism's four most important pilgrimage sites, marking the spot where Buddha first taught the Dharma (his core teachings) after attaining enlightenment — an event known as Dharmachakra Pravartan, or 'turning the wheel of Dharma.' India first put Sarnath forward for consideration in 1998, and formally submitted it for this year's nomination cycle in January 2025.

stories.title: Europe's wildfires claim their first confirmed civilian life as Spain and France evacuations pass 300,000
stories.what_happened: A 78-year-old man with reduced mobility died after being caught by flames near his orchard in Manises, a town northwest of Valencia — officials say it is the fires' first confirmed civilian death in Spain, after two firefighters died earlier in the week. Evacuations have now passed 300,000 across Spain and France, with Spain's Interior Ministry reporting nearly 30,000 evacuated from the Madrid region alone.
key_points: A 78-year-old man died in Manises, near Valencia — the fires' first confirmed civilian death
Two firefighters had already died fighting the blazes earlier this week
300,000+ people now evacuated across Spain and France
Temperatures set to climb again to abnormal highs by midweek

depth.background: Spain and France are in the grip of a wildfire outbreak that has burned roughly 10,000-15,000 hectares around Madrid and Ávila alone, driven by an intense summer heatwave. Spain declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency days ago as fires spread faster than crews could contain them.

thread.previously: Spain had just declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency as evacuations passed 300,000, driven by fires tearing through the Madrid and Ávila regions.
thread.changed: A 78-year-old man became the fires' first confirmed civilian fatality, caught near his orchard in Manises, and hotter, gustier weather is forecast to return by midweek.

stories.title: Spain declares its first-ever national wildfire emergency as evacuations pass 300,000
stories.what_happened: Spain's government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two large blazes near the capital merged into one and a third fire threatened to join them, burning roughly 15,000 hectares across the Madrid and Ávila regions. Regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso called it the worst fire in the region's history. Combined evacuations across France and Spain have now climbed past 300,000 people, up from about 250,000 a day earlier, with roughly 60,000 evacuated from villages west of Madrid alone. A separate, smaller blaze near Valencia killed one elderly man. High winds are fanning the flames in both countries.
key_points: Spain invokes a national emergency for a wildfire for the first time ever
Three blazes near Madrid have merged into one 'worst fire in the region's history'
Combined France-Spain evacuations now top 300,000, up from ~250,000 yesterday
Italy, Greece, Netherlands and Portugal are flying in extra water-bomber aircraft

depth.background: Southwestern Europe has been locked in a weeks-long, climate-change-intensified heatwave that has left forests around Madrid and southwestern France tinder-dry. Wildfires broke out over the weekend and, as of yesterday, had already forced roughly 250,000 people from their homes across France and Spain. A 'national emergency' in Spain is a rarely-used legal step: it lets the central government in Madrid take over powers that normally sit with Spain's semi-autonomous regions, and it has only been invoked once before (during a countrywide blackout in 2025).

thread.previously: We reported that wildfires fueled by a weeks-long heatwave had forced over 250,000 evacuations across southwestern France and central Spain.
thread.changed: The crisis has escalated sharply: Spain has now declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency after blazes merged near Madrid, and combined evacuations have passed 300,000.
