stories.title: Racing Bulls climb to 5th in the F1 constructors' standings as Lawson delivers a career-best first half
stories.what_happened: Both Racing Bulls cars scored points at the Hungarian Grand Prix, the last race before Formula 1's summer break. The result lifted the team to 5th in the constructors' championship on 66 points, five points clear of Alpine in 6th. Lawson has now surpassed his entire 2025 points total before the season is even half over.
key_points: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad both scored points at the Hungarian GP, Racing Bulls' final race before the summer break
The double-points finish moves Racing Bulls up to 5th in the constructors' championship, ahead of Alpine
Lawson has already beaten his entire 2025 points tally
F1 now enters a four-week break before the Dutch GP on August 24

depth.background: Racing Bulls is Red Bull's junior team, running alongside the main Red Bull outfit. New Zealander Liam Lawson had a difficult 2025, but has rebuilt his reputation in 2026 alongside rookie teammate Arvid Lindblad. We reported separately that Red Bull rejected a reported $3 billion offer for the team — a story about its ownership, not its on-track form.

stories.title: Mexican rookie Noel León wins his first Formula 2 Feature Race at the Hungaroring
stories.what_happened: León won Sunday's F2 Feature Race at the Hungaroring, the same Budapest circuit hosting the Hungarian Grand Prix. It's his first Feature Race win of the season, having already taken Sprint Race wins earlier this year in Montreal and Monaco — the Montreal win made him the first Mexican driver to win an F2 race in the modern era.
key_points: León, a 21-year-old rookie for Campos Racing, took his maiden F2 Feature Race win at Budapest's Hungaroring
It adds to two earlier Sprint Race wins this season, in Montreal and Monaco
A Feature Race is F2's longer, higher-points race — a bigger scalp than a Sprint win
Comes the same race weekend Lando Norris won the main Hungarian Grand Prix

depth.background: Formula 2 is the main feeder series directly below Formula 1 — most current F1 grid drivers competed in it (or its predecessor, GP2) before graduating up. Each F2 race weekend runs two races: a shorter Sprint Race and a longer, higher-points Feature Race. León, from Monterrey, Mexico, worked his way up through US and European junior single-seater categories before joining Campos Racing for his F2 rookie season this year.

stories.title: Berlin names 21-year-old Islamist extremist as suspect in fatal Pride attack, launches manhunt
stories.what_happened: Berlin police have identified the suspect as a 21-year-old man, named in reports as Abdul B., who is already known to authorities as part of the city's Islamist extremist scene and was released from a juvenile detention centre only in May 2026. Officers describe him as slim, about 1.9 metres tall, with black hair, wearing a black hoodie and white trousers at the time of the attack. Germany's elite counter-terrorism unit GSG 9, along with helicopters and other aerial surveillance, is now involved in the manhunt. Police have not confirmed a motive and are warning the public not to approach him.
key_points: Suspect named as a 21-year-old known to Berlin's Islamist extremist scene
He had been released from a juvenile detention centre only in May 2026
Elite counter-terrorism unit GSG 9 and aerial units are now hunting him
Motive still not officially confirmed; public warned not to approach him

depth.background: Christopher Street Day (CSD) is Germany's version of Pride, named after the New York street where the 1969 Stonewall uprising began; Berlin's is one of Europe's largest. On Saturday night a van drove into the crowd celebrating in the central Tiergarten park, killing a woman and injuring 16 people, eight seriously. The driver fled on foot, and for hours German authorities gave few details on who they were looking for.

thread.previously: A white van plowed into the crowd at Berlin's Christopher Street Day (Pride) celebration in Tiergarten park on Saturday night, killing one woman and injuring 16 people, eight seriously. The driver fled the scene and no motive was given.
thread.changed: Police have now named the suspect as a 21-year-old known to Berlin's Islamist extremist scene who was released from juvenile detention just two months earlier. He remains at large as GSG 9 and aerial units search for him; a motive is still not officially confirmed.

stories.title: A brutal heat dome traps over 100 million Americans under heat alerts as temperatures near 115°F
stories.what_happened: The National Weather Service has extreme heat warnings and heat advisories covering more than **100 million people**, spanning Illinois, Missouri, Iowa, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Tennessee, and reaching into the Northeast. In Mason City, Iowa, the heat index — how hot it actually feels once humidity is factored in — is forecast to hit **114°F**, among the most extreme readings in the country. At least **40 million people** are under the most serious tier, an Extreme Heat Warning, meaning conditions are dangerous even for healthy people without precautions. High humidity is compounding the heat, and forecasters say overnight lows aren't dropping enough for people — especially those without air conditioning — to get real relief before the next day's heat builds again. This is the second consecutive day of the most dangerous conditions, with cities as far apart as Las Vegas (112°F) and Rapid City, South Dakota (105°F) also seeing triple-digit highs.
key_points: Heat alerts now cover more than **100 million people** across the central and eastern US.
Heat index values are hitting **114°F in Iowa** and up to **112°F in Las Vegas**.
At least **40 million people** are under the most severe **Extreme Heat Warnings**.
This is the **second straight day** of dangerous heat, with overnight lows not dropping enough for relief.
A **'heat dome'** — trapped high pressure — is holding the hot, humid air in place over a huge swath of the country.

depth.background: A heat dome forms when a large area of high-pressure air gets stuck in place, acting like a lid that traps heat and humidity underneath it for days at a time. This one has parked itself over the central and eastern US, stretching from the Midwest through the Ohio Valley into the Northeast. Heat domes have become a recurring summer feature in North America in recent years, and this is one of the most widespread of **2026** so far, following an earlier bout of extreme heat around the July 4th holiday.

stories.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now officially active — and Red Bull is racing to stop him leaving
stories.what_happened: Sunday's **Hungarian Grand Prix**, won by Lando Norris, marked the start of F1's summer break — and with it, the trigger point for Verstappen's exit clause. Verstappen sits third in the championship, **78 points behind** second-placed George Russell, with too few points left on the table for him to have caught Russell before the break — meaning it's now mathematically certain he finished the first half of the season outside the top two. That makes his contractual escape clause active: he doesn't have to tell Red Bull his decision until **October**, but he can now walk away at the end of the season if he chooses. Red Bull, keen to avoid losing its four-time champion, has put a new contract on the table that would extend his deal to **2029** and strip out the exit-clause language altogether. Complicating his options, Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff said this past weekend he's sticking with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli for 2027, closing off what many saw as Verstappen's most likely alternative seat. That leaves **McLaren** as close to Verstappen's only realistic landing spot if he does decide to leave Red Bull.
key_points: Verstappen's Red Bull contract (through **2028**) has an exit clause tied to being **top-2** in the standings at the summer break.
That break arrived after **Sunday's Hungarian GP**, and Verstappen is **78 points behind** 2nd-placed George Russell — mathematically unable to catch him.
The clause is now **mathematically active**; Verstappen has until **October** to decide whether to use it.
Red Bull has offered a **new contract through 2029** that would **remove the exit clause** entirely.
**Mercedes** has ruled out signing him for 2027, leaving **McLaren** as his only realistic alternative seat.

depth.background: Max Verstappen signed his current Red Bull deal, running through 2028, at the height of his dominance, but it included a protective clause for him: if he ever fell outside the top two positions in the championship by the summer break, he'd be free to leave at the end of that season. Red Bull's car under the 2026 rules has not been as competitive as in Verstappen's title-winning years, and after a season of underperformance relative to McLaren, that clause has now become relevant rather than theoretical. This is the same 'ownership stake' saga already swirling around Verstappen's future — Red Bull has previously tried creative ways, including offering him an equity stake in the team, to keep him from bolting to a rival.

thread.previously: We reported Red Bull was offering Verstappen an ownership stake in the team as a way to keep him from leaving for a rival.
thread.changed: Verstappen's contractual exit clause is now mathematically active after the Hungarian GP confirmed he's outside the top two at the summer break — meaning he can actually leave. Red Bull has countered with a new contract offer through 2029 that removes the clause, while Mercedes has closed the door on a 2027 seat, leaving McLaren as his main alternative.

stories.title: Sudan's army seizes the town of Bara, easing pressure on a besieged regional capital, as a US-brokered truce push continues
stories.what_happened: Sudan's army captured the town of Bara, less than 50km from Al Obeid, loosening the RSF's grip on the besieged city — a notable battlefield gain given Kordofan is now the war's central front. At the same time, the army is demanding the RSF completely withdraw from the cities it holds as its price for accepting a US-proposed 90-day truce meant to open the door to a lasting ceasefire.
key_points: Army captured Bara, under 50km from besieged Al Obeid in North Kordofan
Kordofan is now the war's main front after the army lost all of Darfur last year
Army wants the rival RSF to fully withdraw from captured cities before any truce
The US has proposed a 90-day truce meant to lead toward a permanent ceasefire
War has displaced 13+ million people; ~5 million face emergency-level hunger

depth.background: Sudan's civil war, which began in 2023, pits the national army against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) for control of the country. The RSF swept through the western Darfur region last year, capturing its main city El Fasher, which pushed the fighting east into the Kordofan region — where the army has been trying to break an RSF siege of Al Obeid, North Kordofan's capital and a key army stronghold.

stories.title: France mobilizes the military and shortens the Tour de France finale as wildfires force 250,000+ evacuations
stories.what_happened: Wildfires burning across France and Spain have displaced more than 250,000 people combined, with France's government mobilizing the military to reinforce firefighters and emergency crews. Race organizers shortened the Tour de France's final stage from a 133km route starting in Thoiry to an 89km circuit confined to Paris, after officials reassigned part of the race's police security detail to wildfire response instead. The race itself continued, but with the shorter route and a smaller security footprint.
key_points: Nearly 200,000 evacuated in France, roughly 60,000 more near Madrid in Spain
France called in the military to help fight the fires and protect towns
Tour de France's final stage cut from 133km to 89km — about a third shorter
Race security officers were reassigned from the route to wildfire response instead

depth.background: A prolonged heatwave and weeks of dry conditions have turned much of France and Spain into a tinderbox this July, on top of the national wildfire emergency Spain already declared this week. The Tour de France, cycling's biggest race and one of the most-watched sporting events in the world, was in its final days, building to a traditional finish in Paris.

stories.title: F1's summer-break countdown: 17 drivers are out of contract for 2027 — and Alonso's own career decision is now due
stories.what_happened: Heading into F1's summer break (which follows the Hungarian Grand Prix), only five drivers — Max Verstappen, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Charles Leclerc and Pierre Gasly — have contracts confirmed into 2027. Seventeen others, including seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and veteran Fernando Alonso, are out of contract at the end of 2026, setting up a major reshuffling of the grid. Alonso is expected to make his own call — race on or retire — during the break, based partly on whether Aston Martin's new upgrades (unveiled this weekend in Hungary) close the gap to the front. Mercedes, meanwhile, still hasn't decided between George Russell and Kimi Antonelli for its two 2027 seats.
key_points: Only 5 drivers (Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Leclerc, Gasly) have deals confirmed into 2027
17 drivers, including Hamilton and Alonso, are out of contract after 2026
Fernando Alonso, 45, is expected to decide his future during the upcoming summer break
Mercedes still hasn't confirmed either seat for 2027, with Russell and Antonelli competing for both

depth.background: Formula 1 drivers typically sign multi-year deals, and clusters of contracts expiring at the same time create what the paddock calls 'silly season' — a scramble of rumours, moves and announcements as teams and drivers sort out who races where next. 2026 is one of those years: new technical rules reshuffled which teams are competitive, which in turn has reshuffled who wants to move. Fernando Alonso, a two-time world champion now in the twilight of a 25-year career, has said his Aston Martin future — and possibly his F1 career — hinges on whether the team's 2026 upgrades finally make the car competitive.

stories.title: Ferrari admits it was 'our mistake' as Hamilton apologises for his reaction to a costly Hungarian GP penalty
stories.what_happened: During Saturday's Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying, Hamilton was on a slow in-lap when McLaren's Oscar Piastri came up behind him on a quick lap. Ferrari's radio warning came late, and Hamilton unintentionally blocked Piastri at Turn 1. The stewards handed Hamilton a three-place grid penalty, dropping him from a provisional 2nd to 5th on the grid. Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur publicly took the blame, saying the team warned Hamilton 'far too late.' Hamilton, visibly frustrated after qualifying, later apologised to the team during the pre-race drivers' parade for his reaction in the moment.
key_points: Hamilton impeded McLaren's Piastri in Q3 after a delayed radio warning from Ferrari
The FIA dropped Hamilton three places on the grid, from 2nd to 5th
Team boss Fred Vasseur says Ferrari told Hamilton 'far too late' that Piastri was coming
Hamilton apologised during the drivers' parade for his post-qualifying 'attitude'

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton joined Ferrari for the 2026 season as a seven-time world champion looking to add a first title with the Italian team. In qualifying, drivers must stay out of the way of rivals on a fast 'push lap' — if a driver is spotted by their team on a slow lap, the radio is supposed to warn them in time to move aside. A driver who blocks another gets penalised by race stewards even if it wasn't intentional, because F1's rules hold the team responsible for keeping their driver informed.

stories.title: Russia bombards Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, killing at least 7 across Ukraine
stories.what_happened: Russia struck Ukraine overnight with one guided X-59/69 missile, seven Iskander ballistic missiles and 136 long-range attack drones. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted the guided missile, five of the seven ballistic missiles, and 104 of the drones — but a residential building in Kyiv was hit, igniting fires. Regional authorities reported at least 7 civilians killed and 58 injured nationwide over the past 24 hours, including one person killed and twelve hurt in a separate daytime drone strike on Kharkiv. Russia also reported casualties from Ukrainian strikes, including on a Russian-held area.
key_points: Russia fired ballistic missiles and over 130 drones at Ukraine overnight
At least 7 civilians killed and 58 wounded across the country in the past day
A residential building in Kyiv was struck; a Kharkiv drone strike killed one more
Kazakhstan's president calls for the war to be frozen and talks to resume

depth.background: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched in February 2022, has continued despite periodic diplomatic efforts, including talks based on the original 2022 Istanbul framework. Overnight long-range strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities — mixing ballistic missiles with cheap, mass-produced Shahed-type drones — have become Russia's routine tactic to wear down Ukrainian air defenses and civilian morale, even as both sides periodically report troop and civilian losses from ongoing frontline and drone warfare.

stories.title: Drone strike kills civilians, including children, at a Sea of Azov holiday camp — each side blames the other
stories.what_happened: An overnight drone attack hit a holiday-camp area of Kyrylivka, a resort town on the Sea of Azov in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia region. Russian-appointed regional governor Yevgeny Balitsky said 11 to 12 people were killed, including four or five children, with about 19 more wounded. Russian authorities and state media blamed Ukraine for the strike. Ukraine had not issued a public response to the accusation as of publication.
key_points: Overnight strike hit a resort area in Kyrylivka, a Russian-occupied town on the Sea of Azov
Russian-installed officials say 11-12 dead including 4-5 children, ~19 wounded
Russia blames Ukraine; Kyiv has not yet responded to the accusation
Comes the same week Russia struck a Kyiv arms exhibition, killing 10

depth.background: This stretch of Ukraine's Azov Sea coast, near the city of Melitopol, has been under Russian occupation since 2022. Russia has resettled and marketed it as a domestic beach holiday destination, so it is often full of civilian tourists rather than military personnel. Both sides in this war now regularly use long-range drones and missiles to hit targets far from the front line, and both have been accused of strikes that killed civilians.

stories.title: Verstappen fitted with a fresh Honda engine for the Hungarian GP after a hidden crack turns up
stories.what_happened: A closer physical inspection on Saturday evening found a crack in a structural area of the engine that Honda said it hadn't seen before, prompting an overnight swap to a new power unit for Sunday's race. Because this is only the third engine Verstappen has used this season — within F1's per-driver allocation before penalties apply — he faces no grid penalty and keeps his third-place starting spot.
key_points: Honda found a crack while re-checking the engine from Verstappen's Silverstone crash
Red Bull swapped in a new power unit on Saturday night
No grid penalty — it's only his third engine this season, within the allowed limit
A fourth unit later this year would trigger a 10-place grid drop

depth.background: Verstappen wrecked his car in a heavy, high-speed crash with Lewis Hamilton at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone. Honda sent that power unit back to its Sakura facility in Japan for inspection, and initial checks said it was fine — Verstappen used it again through Hungarian GP qualifying.

stories.title: West Indies claw back from 23/1 to 194/3 as Hodge's unbeaten 83 steadies a rain-hit Day 1 vs Pakistan
stories.what_happened: West Indies slipped to 23/1 early in the day as Pakistan's bowlers, led by Mohammad Abbas, made early inroads, with rain repeatedly stopping play. Kavem Hodge and Shai Hope then put together an unbroken partnership to steady the innings, with Hodge finishing the rain-shortened day unbeaten on 83 off 181 balls. West Indies closed play at 194 for 3.
key_points: West Indies were reduced to 23/1 early after choosing to bat first
Kavem Hodge (83 not out) and Shai Hope (37 not out) rebuilt with an unbroken stand
Rain repeatedly interrupted play at the new-look Brian Lara Stadium, Tarouba
West Indies closed Day 1 on 194/3 in the series-opening Test

depth.background: This is the first of a multi-match Test series between West Indies and Pakistan, being played at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad — a venue that has recently been redeveloped. West Indies won the toss and chose to bat first, but early results were shaky.

thread.previously: We reported West Indies slipped to 23/1 early on Day 1, with rain and Mohammad Abbas causing early trouble at the redeveloped Tarouba venue.
thread.changed: West Indies recovered through an unbroken Hodge-Hope partnership to close the rain-hit day at a much healthier 194/3, with Hodge unbeaten on 83.

stories.title: Van rams into crowd at Berlin's Pride celebration, killing one and injuring 16
stories.what_happened: On Saturday night, a van drove into a crowd gathered for Berlin's Pride festival, killing one person and injuring at least 16 others. Police called off the celebration, including a concert that was underway on stage, around 10:15pm local time. Investigators identified a suspect, a 21-year-old man referred to as Abdul B., whom police describe as known to them through Islamist circles in the city. Authorities are also examining reports that some victims suffered stab wounds in addition to being struck by the vehicle, though they say it is too early to say for certain.
key_points: A van drove into people gathered near Brandenburg Gate for Berlin Pride
1 person killed, at least 16 injured; some victims may have stab wounds too
Police name a 21-year-old suspect with alleged ties to Islamist circles in Berlin
The celebration and a concert were called off mid-event around 10:15pm

depth.background: Berlin's Pride march is one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ celebrations, drawing hundreds of thousands each year to the streets around the Brandenburg Gate and Tiergarten park. Germany has dealt with a string of vehicle-ramming attacks at public gatherings in recent years, which is why cities now use concrete barriers and route closures at big events — protections that, in this case, did not stop the vehicle from reaching the crowd.

stories.title: President Murmu wraps up India's first-ever presidential visit to Moldova and North Macedonia, signs trade and defence pacts in Romania
stories.what_happened: President Droupadi Murmu completed her three-nation European tour on Saturday, concluding in Romania where India and Romania signed three memorandums of understanding: a science and technology cooperation programme, a sports-cooperation pact, and an agreement to establish a Chair of Indian Studies at the University of Bucharest. The two countries agreed to double bilateral trade within three years, discussed deepening defence-manufacturing cooperation, and designated 2028 as the 'India-Romania Year of Innovation' to mark 80 years of diplomatic ties. On her final day, Murmu met the Indian diaspora and Romanian-Indian friendship groups, received an honorary doctorate from the Bucharest University of Economic Studies, and departed for New Delhi.
key_points: Murmu became the first Indian head of state to visit Moldova and North Macedonia, and the first Indian president to visit Romania in over 30 years
India and Romania signed three agreements — on science cooperation, sports, and a new Chair of Indian Studies at the University of Bucharest
The two countries agreed to double bilateral trade within three years and deepen defence-manufacturing talks
Murmu met the Indian diaspora and received an honorary doctorate before departing for New Delhi

depth.background: India has historically had limited high-level diplomatic engagement with Eastern Europe and the Balkans. Murmu's nine-day tour — Moldova (July 19-20), North Macedonia (July 21-22), and Romania (July 23-25) — is part of a deliberate push by India's foreign ministry to build ties in a region it has largely overlooked, at a time when India is also navigating friction with the US over trade tariffs.

stories.title: Ferrari breaks F1's overnight work curfew to fine-tune its car before Hungarian GP qualifying
stories.what_happened: The FIA confirmed Ferrari broke the Friday-night curfew at the Hungarian Grand Prix, using extra hours to adjust its SF-26 car's setup ahead of final practice and qualifying. Because it was Ferrari's first curfew exception of the 2026 season, one of four it is allowed, no fine or penalty followed. The move came even though Ferrari had already topped both Friday practice sessions.
key_points: FIA confirms Ferrari used one of its 4 allowed curfew exceptions this season
No fine or penalty follows — teams get 4 free passes per year
Comes despite Ferrari topping both Friday practice sessions
Shows how seriously the team is chasing a rare shot at pole

depth.background: F1's rules ban teams from working on their cars overnight between Friday and Saturday practice, to control costs and protect crew rest. But every team gets four 'curfew exceptions' per season it can use without punishment, usually for exactly this kind of late setup tweak.

stories.title: Typhoon Noul — the strongest to hit China this year — forces 715,000 people from their homes in Guangdong
stories.what_happened: Typhoon Noul made landfall on the coast of Huidong county in Huizhou, southern Guangdong province, at approximately 3:50am local time on Sunday, with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h (68 mph) near its center. More than 715,000 people had been relocated for safety in Guangdong province by early Sunday. China's state Xinhua news agency said Noul was the strongest typhoon to make landfall in the country so far this year. The storm was moving inland and weakening progressively, but still brought strong winds and heavy rain further into the region.
key_points: Noul made landfall in Huidong county, Huizhou, Guangdong province at 3:50am local time Sunday
Winds reached 110 km/h (68 mph) near its center
More than 715,000 people were relocated for safety in Guangdong alone
China's Xinhua news agency says it's the strongest typhoon to make landfall in the country so far this year

depth.background: China's southern coast, especially Guangdong province, is hit by multiple typhoons every summer as warm Pacific and South China Sea waters fuel powerful storms. China has invested heavily in early-warning systems and mass-evacuation drills precisely because storms like this are a near-annual occurrence — the scale of evacuation here (over 700,000 people) reflects a well-drilled system responding to a genuine top-tier threat, not a one-off.

stories.title: Jemimah Rodrigues fires Southern Brave to a 5-wicket win over Sunrisers Leeds in her first Hundred game for her new team
stories.what_happened: In Saturday's match at Headingley, Leeds, Sunrisers Leeds posted 116, and Southern Brave chased it down for a 5-wicket win with 4 balls remaining. Jemimah Rodrigues top-scored with an unbeaten 42 off 34 balls and was named Player of the Match, in her first appearance for Southern Brave against her former team.
key_points: Southern Brave chased down Sunrisers Leeds' 116 with 4 balls to spare
Jemimah Rodrigues scored an unbeaten 42 off 34 balls and won Player of the Match
She switched from Sunrisers Leeds (formerly Northern Superchargers) to Southern Brave for this Hundred season
She said the bowlers were 'outstanding under pressure' despite calling her own innings 'not the most pleasing'

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format franchise cricket tournament (100 balls per side instead of cricket's usual 120 in a T20), designed to be fast-paced and easy for newer fans to follow. It draws top international players, including several from India's women's team such as Rodrigues, who moved between English franchises this season — she previously played for the team now known as Sunrisers Leeds and switched to rival Southern Brave for 2026.

stories.title: Bangladesh's bowling crisis deepens for the Australia Tests — Shoriful and Litton ruled out, Ebadot opts out too
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh's cricket board confirmed that seamer Shoriful Islam (hamstring) and wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das (calf) will miss the series opener against Australia through injury, while all-rounder Ebadot Hossain has opted out of the tour for the birth of his first child. All three absences come on top of Nahid Rana, who was already ruled out of the two-match series with a Grade 2 side strain expected to sideline him for six to eight weeks.
key_points: Seamer Shoriful Islam and keeper-batter Litton Das ruled out injured for the series opener
All-rounder pace bowler Ebadot Hossain has opted out for the birth of his first child
Comes on top of strike bowler Nahid Rana's side strain, already confirmed out
Leaves Bangladesh's pace attack severely short-handed for a tough away tour

depth.background: Bangladesh are touring Australia for a two-match Test series as part of the World Test Championship (WTC) — a league that ranks Test-playing nations by results over a multi-year cycle. Bangladesh's attack has been led this year by fast bowler Nahid Rana, who has taken 44 international wickets in 2026 alone, the most of any bowler worldwide, making his earlier injury already a significant blow before these further absences.

thread.previously: We reported Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker Nahid Rana was ruled out of the Australia Tests with a side strain.
thread.changed: The squad crisis has deepened: seamer Shoriful Islam and keeper-batter Litton Das are also out injured, and Ebadot Hossain has opted out for the birth of his first child — leaving Bangladesh's pace attack severely short-handed.

prev_ref.title: Bangladesh loses fast bowler Nahid Rana for the Australia Tests to a side strain

stories.title: Bangladesh loses fast bowler Nahid Rana for the Australia Tests to a side strain
stories.what_happened: The Bangladesh Cricket Board confirmed on Saturday that Rana has been ruled out of the two-match Test series against Australia after medical scans confirmed a Grade 2 strain on his left side, picked up during a T20I against Zimbabwe on July 17. The board expects a six-to-eight-week recovery, which also rules him out of the associated World Test Championship points on offer.
key_points: Rana, 23, suffered a Grade 2 left side strain during the second T20I against Zimbabwe on July 17
The Bangladesh Cricket Board estimates a six-to-eight-week recovery
That rules him out of the upcoming two-match World Test Championship series in Australia
News lands less than a week before the squad is due to fly out, forcing a scramble for replacements

depth.background: Nahid Rana is Bangladesh's premier fast bowler, valued especially for the extra pace and bounce he offers on bouncier pitches like those in Australia — conditions where Bangladesh has historically struggled. His fitness had already been in question heading into this high-stakes tour.

stories.title: Netherlands beat Namibia by 58 runs to boost 2027 World Cup qualifying hopes
stories.what_happened: The Netherlands set Namibia a target of 252 after being asked to bat first, then bowled Namibia out for 193 to win by 58 runs. The match was the 117th fixture of the long-running League 2 competition and the fourth match of a week-long tri-series between the Netherlands, Namibia and Nepal in Utrecht.
key_points: Netherlands posted 251/6, Namibia bowled out for 193
Namibia won the toss and chose to field first
Played at Kampong, Utrecht, in ICC Cricket World Cup League 2
Result affects both teams' race for the 2027 World Cup Qualifier

depth.background: Cricket World Cup League 2 is a multi-year one-day league where eight non-Test-playing nations (like Netherlands, Namibia, Nepal, Oman and UAE) play each other repeatedly over several years. It exists purely so these teams can earn ODI status and a shot at qualifying for the 50-over Cricket World Cup, since they don't get automatic entry the way India, Australia or England do. This match was part of a tri-nation series in Utrecht also involving Nepal, hosted by the Netherlands.

stories.title: Desert Vipers chase their first Global Super League win today against unbeaten defending champions Guyana
stories.what_happened: Guyana Amazon Warriors face Desert Vipers today in Providence. Guyana have won both their games so far, including a 3-wicket win over San Francisco Unicorns decided on DLS method; Desert Vipers lost their tournament opener to Lahore Qalandars and need a win to keep their qualification hopes alive.
key_points: Guyana Amazon Warriors, the defending GSL champions, are unbeaten through their first two games
Desert Vipers lost their opener to Lahore Qalandars and need a win to stay in contention
The five-team, Guyana-hosted league runs through August 1; only the top team goes straight to the final
Everyone else fights through a knockout qualifier for the second final spot

depth.background: The Global Super League is a T20 franchise tournament played entirely at Providence Stadium in Guyana, running from July 23 to August 1, 2026, with five teams: Lahore Qalandars, Perth Scorchers XI, Guyana Amazon Warriors, San Francisco Unicorns and Desert Vipers. Guyana enter as defending champions after winning the previous edition.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russia is trying to bring in 30,000 more North Korean troops for the Ukraine war
stories.what_happened: In his Saturday night address, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia wants to bring in 30,000 additional North Korean troops, with preparations to house them in Russia's Voronezh region underway since June. He said North Korea is also preparing to send new ballistic missile launchers to Russia. He did not name his source. Separately, Russia bombarded Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, part of an exchange that has killed civilians on both sides in recent days.
key_points: Zelensky says Russia has asked North Korea for 30,000 additional troops
Intel points to Russia's Voronezh region prepping to house them since June
Pyongyang is also readying new ballistic missile launchers for Russia, he says
Comes as Russia pounds Kyiv with a fresh wave of missiles, killing civilians

depth.background: North Korea has been quietly bankrolling Russia's war effort since late 2024, when it first sent roughly 20,000 troops to help push Ukrainian forces out of Russia's Kursk region. In exchange, Russia has reportedly shared missile and satellite technology with Pyongyang — a partnership that worries the US, South Korea, and Japan because it makes North Korea's own weapons more dangerous. About 14,000 North Korean soldiers are currently believed to be serving on the front lines.

stories.title: IDFC FIRST Bank posts record ₹1,075 crore quarterly profit, crossing ₹1,000 crore for the first time
stories.what_happened: IDFC FIRST Bank reported its highest-ever quarterly net profit of ₹1,075 crore for the April-June 2026 quarter (Q1 FY27), up 132.4% from ₹463 crore a year earlier — the first time it has crossed ₹1,000 crore in a single quarter. Its loan book grew 20.6% year-on-year to ₹3,05,488 crore, net interest income rose 21.1% to ₹5,972 crore, and its share of low-cost current and savings account deposits (CASA ratio) hit a multi-quarter high of 50.8%. Gross bad loans fell to 1.51% of the loan book from 1.97% a year ago, and provisions for bad loans dropped 31%, helped by a ₹514.82 crore insurance claim payout.
key_points: Q1 FY27 profit up 132% year-on-year to ₹1,075 crore
Loan book grew 20.6% to over ₹3 lakh crore
Bad loans (gross NPA) fell to 1.51% from 1.97% a year ago
Provisions (money set aside for bad loans) dropped 31%

depth.background: IDFC FIRST Bank was formed in 2018 from the merger of IDFC Bank and Capital First, and spent its early years absorbing heavy loan losses as it built out a retail banking business from scratch. Under CEO V. Vaidyanathan, it has been shifting from riskier infrastructure and wholesale lending toward retail loans and deposits, a slower but usually steadier path to profitability. As recently as early 2025 the bank posted a quarterly loss, so this result marks a sharp turnaround.

stories.title: CJP formally ends its 37-day Jantar Mantar sit-in after Education Minister Pradhan's resignation
stories.what_happened: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the Council of Ministers today; Prahlad Joshi has been named to take over the ministry. Hours later, CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka announced at a joint press conference with Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh that the CJP was withdrawing its 37-day agitation 'in good faith,' on the understanding that the government's other commitments — compensation and dropped cases — are honoured within the agreed timelines.
key_points: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the student group leading the protest, announced the withdrawal at ~6:05pm today
Comes hours after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, the protesters' central demand
Government also agreed to ₹1 crore compensation for NEET victims' families and to drop FIRs against protesters by Tuesday
Security cover has already been withdrawn from the Jantar Mantar protest site

depth.background: The CJP has held a sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar since June 20, demanding accountability for this year's NEET-UG medical entrance exam paper leak and irregularities in CBSE's on-screen answer-marking process. It grew into one of India's largest youth-led protests in recent years, spreading to solidarity actions like today's Bihar Bandh. As of yesterday, the government had offered compensation and dropped some FIRs but had refused the protesters' central demand: removing Pradhan.

thread.previously: Yesterday the government offered NEET protesters compensation for victims' families and agreed to drop FIRs against protesters, but held the line on removing Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan even as a Saturday deadline the protesters had set arrived.
thread.changed: Pradhan resigned today, and the CJP formally called off its 37-day Jantar Mantar sit-in in response — ending Delhi's biggest student-led protest in years.

stories.title: Pralhad Joshi named interim Education Minister after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
stories.what_happened: President Droupadi Murmu has formally accepted Pradhan's resignation from the Union Cabinet. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has named Pralhad Joshi as interim Education Minister, meaning Joshi will run the ministry in addition to the portfolios he already holds. Joshi said he was thankful to the PM and would carry out the responsibility 'with complete humility.'
key_points: President Murmu accepted Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as Education Minister
Pralhad Joshi has been named interim Education Minister
He'll hold the education portfolio alongside his existing ministries
The move follows weeks of protest over NEET exam paper leaks

depth.background: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned amid a nearly seven-week protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar by a Gen-Z-led group calling itself the 'Cockroach' movement, demanding accountability over leaked NEET (medical entrance exam) papers. We previously reported that his resignation and government assurances — including compensation and FIR withdrawals for protesters — led the group to formally call off its sit-in.

thread.previously: We reported that the government accepted Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper-leak protests, and the CJP formally ended its Jantar Mantar sit-in as a result.
thread.changed: Prime Minister Modi has now named Pralhad Joshi as interim Education Minister to take charge of the ministry alongside his existing portfolios.
