stories.title: Sri Lanka Women level the ODI series 1-1, chasing down 274 with an unbeaten Samarawickrama century
stories.what_happened: At Hambantota's Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium, Pakistan Women batted first and posted 273 for 5. Sri Lanka Women chased the target down comfortably, reaching 275 for 2 with 19 balls remaining, powered by an unbeaten century from Harshitha Samarawickrama.
key_points: Pakistan Women set 273/5; Sri Lanka Women chased it down for the loss of just 2 wickets
Harshitha Samarawickrama hit an unbeaten century to anchor the chase
Sri Lanka won by 8 wickets with 19 balls to spare
Series now tied 1-1 with the decider on July 28

depth.background: Pakistan Women's cricket team is touring Sri Lanka for a three-match ODI and three-match T20I series. Pakistan won the first ODI by 5 wickets in a close finish two days ago, taking a 1-0 lead in the series.

stories.title: 'Useless': Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari needs to change driver after shock Q2 exit at his best track
stories.what_happened: Hamilton was knocked out in Q2 of Hungarian GP qualifying and will start Sunday's race from 12th place — missing the cut for the top-ten shootout, Q3, by just 0.015 seconds according to Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur. Visibly frustrated, Hamilton told reporters afterward 'I just drove terribly,' called himself 'useless,' and said the team needs to 'change driver.' His teammate Charles Leclerc, by contrast, took pole position in the same session.
key_points: Hamilton was eliminated in Q2 and will start Sunday's race from P12
He missed the cut for Q3 by just 0.015 seconds, per Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur
Hamilton called himself 'useless' and said the team needs to 'change driver'
The Hungaroring is historically his best track: 9 poles and 8 wins there

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton is a seven-time world champion widely regarded as one of F1's greatest ever drivers, and the Hungarian Grand Prix has historically been his best track — he has won it eight times and taken pole nine times, more than at any other circuit on the calendar. Since joining Ferrari, however, he has struggled to find the same form he had at his previous team, making a poor result at his most successful track especially jarring.

stories.title: Charles Leclerc converts practice pace into a shock Hungarian GP pole, beating championship leader Piastri
stories.what_happened: Charles Leclerc took pole position for Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix, setting a lap of 1 minute 15.372 seconds — just 0.026 seconds quicker than championship leader Oscar Piastri. McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell were within half a tenth of that time. It caps a strong weekend for Leclerc, who had topped Friday's practice session despite a mechanical scare on his car. His Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton endured the opposite: eliminated in Q2, missing the pole-sitter's time by just 15 thousandths of a second, and will start Sunday's race down in 12th.
key_points: Leclerc took pole with a 1:15.372, just 0.026 seconds ahead of championship leader Oscar Piastri
McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell were within half a tenth of pole too
Lewis Hamilton, Leclerc's own teammate, was knocked out in Q2 and starts P12
It's Leclerc's first pole since Friday's practice scare, when he said 'something broke' on his Ferrari

depth.background: Qualifying in Formula 1 sets Sunday's starting grid: whoever sets the fastest single lap across three knockout rounds (Q1, Q2, Q3) starts at the front, which matters enormously at a tight, overtaking-unfriendly track like the Hungaroring. Leclerc had topped Friday's practice session despite a mechanical scare, hinting Ferrari had genuine pace this weekend — but practice speed doesn't always survive into a clean qualifying lap under pressure.

thread.previously: Leclerc topped Friday's practice session for the Hungarian GP despite reporting a mechanical scare mid-session.
thread.changed: He's turned that practice pace into pole position for Sunday's race, beating championship leader Piastri by 0.026 seconds.

prev_ref.title: Charles Leclerc tops Hungarian GP practice despite a scary mechanical scare — 'something broke'

stories.title: George Russell's Mercedes sprang a mystery water leak in Q3 — but he dodges a grid penalty
stories.what_happened: During Q3 of Hungarian GP qualifying, a crack in George Russell's Mercedes power unit sprayed water onto his rear tyres just as he began his final lap, instantly cooling the rubber and ruining his lap time; his car came to a stop at Turn 1 with water pooling underneath. He ended up qualifying 7th. Mercedes confirmed it will change his internal combustion engine before Sunday's race — his fourth of the season — which comes without a grid penalty because it's within his permitted allocation.
key_points: A cracked engine part sprayed water onto Russell's rear tyres mid-lap in Q3
He described it as 'a water pistol being sprayed at the tyres'
Mercedes will fit a new engine before Sunday's race
No grid penalty — it's only his 4th engine of the season, within the allowed limit

depth.background: F1 teams are only allowed a limited number of engine (power unit) components per driver each season; going over that limit brings an automatic grid penalty. So a mid-season engine swap doesn't always cost grid places — only once a driver exceeds their season's allowance.

stories.title: Hamilton and Antonelli handed grid penalties, reshuffling the Hungarian GP front row
stories.what_happened: In Saturday's Hungarian GP qualifying at the Hungaroring, Lando Norris (McLaren) took pole position with a last-gasp lap. Stewards then penalized two rivals: Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) received a 3-place grid drop for impeding Oscar Piastri at Turn 1 during Piastri's final flying lap, and championship leader Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) received a 3-place drop plus a penalty point for not slowing enough for yellow flags caused by a Max Verstappen spin at the final corner. The reshuffled grid for Sunday: Norris pole, Charles Leclerc 2nd, Oscar Piastri 3rd, Verstappen 4th, Hamilton 5th, George Russell 6th, and Antonelli 7th.
key_points: Lando Norris took pole with a last-gasp lap in Q3
Hamilton dropped 3 grid places for impeding Piastri
Championship leader Antonelli dropped 3 places (plus a penalty point) for not slowing for yellow flags
Leclerc is promoted onto the front row alongside Norris for Sunday's race

depth.background: F1 stewards can penalize a driver after qualifying even if their lap time was legitimate — common offences include 'impeding' a rival (blocking their run) or not slowing enough under yellow flags, which warn drivers of a hazard like a spun car ahead. Drivers also accumulate penalty points on their super-licence for infractions; reaching 12 points within 12 months triggers an automatic one-race ban. Kimi Antonelli, a rookie sensation, currently leads the drivers' championship.

stories.title: Charles Leclerc snatches a shock Hungarian GP pole, upsetting the McLarens of Piastri and Norris
stories.what_happened: In Saturday qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Charles Leclerc set a lap of 1 minute 15.372 seconds to take pole position, beating Piastri by 0.026 seconds and Norris by a further 0.015 seconds. Norris had actually set the fastest lap of anyone in Q2, but cloud cover and dropping track temperature in Q3 meant he couldn't match it when it counted. Leclerc's own team radio caught his reaction: "What? Ahahahaha. Mamma Mia! My God!"
key_points: Leclerc: 1:15.372, beats championship leader Piastri by 0.026s, Norris by 0.041s
It's Ferrari's first pole of the entire 2026 season
Comes a week after Ferrari fitted upgraded suspension at the Belgian GP
Norris was actually fastest in Q2, but couldn't repeat it as conditions cooled in Q3

depth.background: McLaren has been the dominant team in 2026, with Piastri leading the drivers' championship and Norris close behind — Ferrari, by contrast, hadn't taken a single pole position all year heading into this weekend. Leclerc himself said before qualifying that he expected nothing better than third place. Ferrari introduced an upgraded suspension package at the previous race in Belgium, and Hungary's Hungaroring circuit — tight, twisty, low on long straights — has traditionally rewarded cars with strong aerodynamic grip rather than raw engine power.

stories.title: US finalizes 10% 'forced labour' tariff on India; government says it will keep pushing for a trade pact
stories.what_happened: The US Trade Representative finalized Section 301 duties of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trading partners on July 23, replacing an expiring temporary tariff; the new India-specific 10% duty took effect July 24. India moved from the 12.5% bracket to the lower 10% one after amending its Foreign Trade Policy on June 14 to explicitly bar imports made with forced labour. India's commerce ministry said on Saturday, July 25, that roughly 45% of its exports to the US remain outside this duty, and it will continue talks with Washington, including on textiles, to conclude the pending trade agreement.
key_points: New US Section 301 duty of 10% on Indian goods took effect July 24
Lower than the 12.5% first proposed, after India tightened import rules
About 45% of India's US-bound exports are exempt, government says
Pharma, smartphones, steel, aluminium, auto parts excluded from the duty

depth.background: Washington has spent months investigating whether trading partners were importing goods made with forced labour, using 'Section 301' of the US Trade Act — a law that lets the US impose tariffs to punish what it considers unfair foreign trade practices. India has separately been negotiating a Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) with the US for over a year to lower tariffs on both sides.

stories.title: Netherlands crush Namibia by 123 runs in World Cup League 2, boosting their push for a 2027 World Cup qualifying spot
stories.what_happened: At Sportpark Maarschalkerweerd in Utrecht, the Netherlands batted first and posted 251 for 6 in their 50 overs. Namibia's reply fell well short — they were bowled out for 128, handing the Netherlands a 123-run win in the 117th match of the League 2 cycle.
key_points: Netherlands posted 251/6 in their 50 overs at Utrecht
Namibia were bowled out for just 128 in reply, falling 123 runs short
The result is the 117th match of the ongoing ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2
League 2 is a qualification ladder that decides which associate nations advance toward the next 50-over World Cup

depth.background: The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 is a multi-year one-day international (ODI) league for cricket's 'associate' nations — countries like the Netherlands and Namibia that aren't part of the sport's traditional Test-playing elite. Results here matter directly: they build the points table that decides who advances toward qualifying for cricket's 50-over World Cup, one of the sport's biggest tournaments.

stories.title: India completes a 90-run rout of Zimbabwe to seal the T20I series, with Ishan Kishan named Player of the Match
stories.what_happened: Batting first at Harare Sports Club, India posted 219 for 5. Zimbabwe were bowled out for 129 in reply, handing India a 90-run win and a 2-0 series sweep. Ishan Kishan's 50 not out in India's innings earned him the Player of the Match award.
key_points: India posted 219/5, Zimbabwe were bowled out for 129 in reply
India wins the 2-match series 2-0 after Sooryavanshi's record fifty carried the 1st T20I
Ishan Kishan named Player of the Match for his 50* in the chase-setting innings
Series win ends a rough recent patch for India's T20I side

depth.background: India came into this two-match tour of Zimbabwe on the back of a rough run of T20I results. The tour opener was headlined by 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who smashed an 18-ball fifty to become the youngest player ever to score a half-century in international cricket, powering India to a 7-wicket win in the first match.

stories.title: Irish police intercept a fully built car bomb heading for Northern Ireland, charge a man
stories.what_happened: During an intelligence-led operation, Irish police stopped a car on a highway south of Carrickmacross and found a fully constructed, portable car bomb — Semtex plastic explosive plus a detonator — in a bag inside. Investigators believe it was destined to be fitted to a vehicle in Northern Ireland with police as the intended target. A 25-year-old was initially detained; a man in his 40s has since been charged in connection with the device and is due before Dublin's Special Criminal Court, which handles paramilitary and terrorism-linked cases.
key_points: Gardaí (Irish police) stopped a car near Carrickmacross, Co Monaghan, about 6 miles from the border
A bag inside held Semtex explosive and a detonator — a portable, ready-to-use bomb
Police believe it was meant to be attached to a vehicle in Northern Ireland, targeting police
A man in his 40s has been charged and is due before the Special Criminal Court in Dublin

depth.background: Northern Ireland's decades-long sectarian conflict, 'the Troubles', formally ended with the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, but small 'dissident republican' groups who reject that peace deal have kept carrying out sporadic bomb and gun attacks aimed at police and security forces, mostly along the Irish border where the old conflict was centred.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton stuns the Hungaroring, beating Verstappen and Norris to Hungarian GP pole
stories.what_happened: Charles Leclerc was fastest in Saturday morning's FP1, before Hamilton topped the afternoon FP2 nearly half a second clear of Norris. Norris then hit back to top FP3, the final practice session, ahead of Hamilton. But when qualifying itself ran later on Saturday, Hamilton produced the fastest lap to take pole position, with Verstappen second and Norris third — pushing Antonelli off the front row.
key_points: Hamilton tops qualifying at the Hungaroring, ahead of Max Verstappen and Lando Norris
Comes right after Norris had topped final practice (FP3) earlier the same day
Breaks Mercedes' perfect run — the team had taken all 10 poles so far this season
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli misses out on the front row

depth.background: Mercedes has been the class of the field in qualifying all season, with Kimi Antonelli and George Russell splitting all 10 poles so far in 2026. Antonelli leads the drivers' championship by 50 points, with Hamilton — now at Ferrari and chasing a record eighth world title — sitting between the two Mercedes drivers in the standings. Hungary is a track Hamilton has historically excelled at.

stories.title: India post 219/5 against Zimbabwe in Harare, closing in on a T20I series sweep
stories.what_happened: In the second T20I at Harare Sports Club, Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza won the toss and chose to field. India batted first and posted 219/5, driven by a 50 from Ishan Kishan and an unbeaten 60 from Tilak Varma. In reply, Zimbabwe slipped to 36/2 early in the chase, leaving them needing 184 runs from the remaining overs with a steep uphill task.
key_points: Zimbabwe won the toss and chose to bowl first at Harare Sports Club
India posted 219/5, with Ishan Kishan making 50 and Tilak Varma unbeaten on 60
India already lead the three-match series 1-0 after a seven-wicket win in the opener
Zimbabwe's chase started at 36/2, needing 184 from 93 balls, with a win probability under 6%

depth.background: India, captained by Shreyas Iyer, are on a three-match T20I tour of Zimbabwe and won the first match by seven wickets, a game that also featured 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 18-ball fifty. A series win here would be India's first T20I series victory under Iyer's captaincy.

stories.title: Cadillac's rookie F1 season hits a new low: Perez and Bottas start last at Hungary
stories.what_happened: At Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying, Bottas and Perez lined up 21st and 22nd — dead last on the grid — continuing a rough rookie season in which the team is still searching for its first championship points and has struggled with reliability, including brake failures that knocked both cars out early at the Austrian Grand Prix.
key_points: Bottas and Perez qualify 21st and 22nd — dead last — at the Hungarian GP
Team still has zero championship points through 11 rounds
Both cars retired early from the Austrian GP with brake failures
Debut season raises questions about how fast a new team can close the gap

depth.background: Cadillac joined Formula 1 for 2026 as the sport's 11th team and first new entrant in years, hiring experienced drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez — who between them have over 500 Grand Prix starts and 100-plus podiums — to lead its debut campaign.

stories.title: Pakistan's Babar Azam era faces its first real test as the West Indies series opens in Trinidad
stories.what_happened: The first Test between West Indies and Pakistan began Saturday at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad, the opening match of a two-Test series. It's Babar Azam's first Test in charge since Pakistan reinstated him as captain, dropping Shan Masood. Babar arrives in good form, having scored an unbeaten century in Pakistan's warm-up match against a West Indies Select XI. Pakistan's predicted XI includes Abdullah Shafique, Imam-ul-Haq, Shan Masood, Babar Azam (c), Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Aamir Jamal, Sajid Khan, Mohammad Ali and Abrar Ahmed. West Indies are rated slight favourites given home conditions.
key_points: The first of two Tests between West Indies and Pakistan starts today at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy, Trinidad
It's Babar Azam's first competitive Test as Pakistan captain since his reinstatement
Babar scored an unbeaten century in the warm-up match, signalling good early form
West Indies are slight favourites on home conditions, per pre-series analysis

depth.background: Pakistan reinstated Babar Azam as Test captain this week, replacing Shan Masood after a poor run of results. This two-match series in the Caribbean is his first assignment back in charge, and a chance for Pakistan to show the change was the right call.

stories.title: Piastri edges Norris in final Hungary practice as Verstappen complains of a 'locked and stiff' rear axle
stories.what_happened: In final practice, Oscar Piastri turned the pecking order around, edging out teammate Lando Norris for the fastest time, while Max Verstappen could only manage fourth and complained that the rear axle of his Red Bull felt locked and stiff — a handling issue right before qualifying. The session ran just before Saturday afternoon's qualifying hour, with Mercedes — unbeaten in poles so far this season — also expected to be competitive.
key_points: Piastri fastest in FP3, just ahead of teammate Norris — reversing Friday's pecking order
Verstappen only fourth, reporting the rear of his Red Bull feels 'locked' and stiff
Session comes right before Saturday afternoon qualifying at the Hungaroring
Mercedes had won 10 poles already this season and were expected to be in the mix again

depth.background: Friday practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix had been led by Ferrari (Hamilton ahead of Leclerc), with McLaren's Norris close behind and Piastri struggling on limited track time. FP3 (final practice) on Saturday morning is the last chance for teams to fine-tune the car before a low-fuel qualifying run decides Sunday's starting grid.

stories.title: Tainted cooking-oil scandal triggers a 200,000-strong protest in Taipei
stories.what_happened: Tens of thousands of protesters — organizers claimed more than 200,000 — rallied on Taipei's Ketagalan Boulevard, outside the Presidential Office, on July 25 under the slogan 'I'm against poisoning Taiwan.' KMT chairperson Cheng Li-wun, Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu, and TPP chairman Huang Kuo-chang addressed the crowd, accusing the government of a 'collapsed' food-safety system and demanding President Lai Ching-te apologize.
key_points: Taichung firm sold soy oil with 4x the legal limit of a cancer-causing chemical
Contaminated oil reached major food processors between April and June
Organizers say 200,000+ rallied outside Taiwan's Presidential Office
Opposition demands President Lai apologize and overhaul food-safety oversight

depth.background: Since mid-July, Taiwan's opposition Kuomintang (KMT) and Taiwan People's Party (TPP) have escalated pressure on the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) government after Taichung-based Central Union Oil Corp. was found to have manufactured roughly 1,300 metric tons of soy-based cooking oil contaminated with benzo[a]pyrene, supplying it to major food processors for months before it was caught.

stories.title: Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi Aramco's Jazan and Yanbu oil sites, opening a new Red Sea front in the Iran war
stories.what_happened: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group struck Aramco's Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast and its Yanbu export terminal further north with a barrage of missiles and drones. The strikes could not be independently verified by international media, but satellite imagery analyzed by NASA's FIRMS fire-tracking system showed thermal anomalies consistent with fires at Jazan. The attack came about a day after a Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi military positions in the Yemeni port city of Hodeidah — the first time Riyadh has taken direct military action in the broader Iran conflict.
key_points: Yemen's Houthi rebels say they fired 'dozens' of ballistic missiles and drones at Aramco facilities in Jazan and Yanbu overnight
Satellite fire-detection data showed active blazes and heat signatures at the Jazan complex
Comes ~24 hours after a Saudi-led coalition bombed Houthi positions in the port of Hodeidah
Houthis have vowed 'escalation with escalation' as the wider US-Iran war grinds into a third week

depth.background: Saudi Arabia has stayed mostly on the sidelines of the US-Israel-Iran war that began roughly two weeks ago, worried that taking sides could make its own oil infrastructure a target. Yemen's Houthi movement, which controls the country's northwest and is backed by Iran, has fought a Saudi-led coalition for a decade and separately declared solidarity with Iran once the US started bombing it. Aramco is the Saudi state oil company and the single biggest supplier of crude to the world market — any disruption to its refineries moves prices instantly.

stories.title: Sergio Perez's Cadillac catches fire risk and locks up in a scary FP3 failure, leaving his qualifying spot in doubt
stories.what_happened: In final practice (FP3) for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Sergio Perez's Cadillac suffered a sudden failure just after leaving the pit lane, stopping near Turn 2. Smoke was visible from the rear of the car; Perez reported an engine problem and a possible fire risk around the rear brakes, and replays suggested the rear axle had locked up before he stopped. The session was red-flagged (halted) while the car was recovered. The failure cost Perez a representative practice lap and left his participation in Saturday's qualifying uncertain while the team investigates.
key_points: Perez stopped near Turn 2 moments after leaving the pits in final practice
Smoke was seen from the rear of the car, with a possible brake fire and an engine problem reported
Replays suggested the rear axle had locked before he came to a stop
The stoppage triggered a red flag, and Cadillac now must assess the damage before qualifying

depth.background: Cadillac is a brand-new team on the 2026 F1 grid, and new teams often struggle with reliability as they iron out problems real racing conditions expose that testing doesn't catch. Cadillac has already had recurring issues with brake temperatures this season, a common headache for teams still learning how their car behaves under race-level stress.

stories.title: Government introduces tougher anti-paper-leak bill in Lok Sabha — up to 10 years' jail and fast-track courts for exam fraud
stories.what_happened: The Union Cabinet approved a new amendment bill on July 24, and the government introduced it in the Lok Sabha (parliament's lower house) on July 25. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, raises individual penalties to 5–10 years in jail and fines up to ₹50 lakh, and for organised crime rings to 7+ years and fines up to ₹10 crore. It requires investigations to finish within two months, lets states designate fast-track sessions courts for these cases with trials completed within three months of the chargesheet, and lets the central government set up a special task force to investigate leaks.
key_points: Bill amends India's 2-year-old anti-paper-leak law, introduced in the Lok Sabha today
Individuals face 5–10 years jail and fines up to ₹50 lakh; organised gangs face 7+ years and up to ₹10 crore
Every state must set up a fast-track court to try these cases within 3 months of chargesheet
Comes a day after Cabinet approval, and days after the NEET paper-leak protests forced a minister's resignation

depth.background: India's competitive exams — for medical college (NEET), government jobs, and more — have been repeatedly hit by leaked question papers, sometimes sold for lakhs of rupees before the exam even starts, derailing the futures of lakhs of honest students who prepared for years. Parliament passed a first anti-paper-leak law in 2024, but leaks kept happening, including the recent NEET leak that triggered weeks of protests, a Bihar-wide shutdown, and this week's resignation of the Education Minister.

stories.title: Parliament moves to lock in a bigger Supreme Court: bill raising judge count from 33 to 37 comes up in the Lok Sabha
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 came up in the Lok Sabha (the lower house of Parliament) during the ongoing Monsoon Session, seeking Parliament's formal approval to raise the Supreme Court's judge strength from 33 to 37 (excluding the Chief Justice of India). Because Article 124 of the Constitution lets Parliament change the court's size through an ordinary law, the bill needs only a simple majority to pass — not the two-thirds majority a constitutional amendment would require. Opposition MPs, including Sougata Ray, N.K. Premachandran and Dean Kuriakose, moved a statutory resolution objecting to the government's earlier use of the ordinance route.
key_points: Bill amends a 1956 law to raise Supreme Court judges (excluding the Chief Justice) from 33 to 37
It replaces an ordinance the government had already issued in May to make the change immediately
Needs only a simple majority — the Constitution lets Parliament set the court's size by ordinary law
Opposition MPs moved a resolution objecting to the government's use of the ordinance route

depth.background: India's Supreme Court has grown its sanctioned strength several times over the decades as its caseload swelled — the court alone handles tens of thousands of pending cases at any time, on top of matters that flow up from High Courts across the country. In May, the government used its ordinance power — the ability to make a law when Parliament isn't in session, subject to later approval — to raise the judge count. Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal introduced the formal bill to replace that ordinance on July 20.

stories.title: Left-wing student groups enforce a statewide Bihar Bandh over the NEET paper leak, clashing with police as RJD's Tej Pratap Yadav is detained
stories.what_happened: On Saturday, left-wing student organisations called a statewide bandh (shutdown) across Bihar, with heavy security deployed as demonstrations turned confrontational in several districts. Police used tear gas and a lathi charge to disperse crowds after stone-pelting broke out; protesters blocked a key road by burning tyres. RJD leader Tej Pratap Yadav was detained after joining the protest in solidarity.
key_points: AISA- and RYA-led shutdown hits several Bihar districts; around 70,000 police personnel deployed
Protesters demand a fair, independent probe into the alleged NEET-UG paper leak — not just a resignation
Stone-pelting, tear gas and a lathi charge reported; the Samastipur–Patna road blocked by burning tyres
RJD leader Tej Pratap Yadav detained after joining protesters, says he's 'ready to die' for the cause

depth.background: NEET-UG is the single national entrance exam that decides admission to nearly every medical college seat in India, making it high-stakes for lakhs of students every year. Weeks of protests broke out after a Bihar police report alleged the exam paper had been leaked for money, and the movement escalated into a hunger strike and sustained demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation — which he ultimately gave.

stories.title: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, handing NEET protesters the win they demanded for weeks
stories.what_happened: Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, July 25, sending his resignation letter to Prime Minister Modi. The move came after weeks of the government insisting he would not step down, even as it made other concessions (compensation, dropped FIRs, an NTA shake-up). Abhijeet Dipke, the Cockroach Janta Party founder who led the protests, told cheering crowds at Jantar Mantar 'We have done it.'
key_points: Pradhan sent his resignation letter to PM Modi on Saturday
Protesters at Delhi's Jantar Mantar erupted in celebration
He is only the second minister to resign over a scandal since Modi took power in 2014
Sonam Wangchuk, who fasted 26 days over the issue, called it 'a victory of peace, patience & perseverance'

depth.background: For weeks, students and youth activists — organized under a group calling itself the 'Cockroach Janta Party' — have been protesting over leaked NEET-UG papers (India's national medical-entrance exam), accusing the government of failing to secure the exam and protect students' futures. The protests grew into one of India's biggest youth street movements in recent years, drawing in opposition politicians and putting real political pressure on PM Modi's government. Activist Sonam Wangchuk went on a 26-day hunger strike in support, ending it earlier this week after the government agreed to compensate paper-leak victims' families — but at that point still refused to remove Pradhan.

thread.previously: The government had offered compensation to NEET-leak victims' families and dropped FIRs against protesters, but held firm that Education Minister Pradhan would not be removed, even as protesters' Saturday deadline arrived.
thread.changed: Pradhan resigned on Saturday — the outcome the government had refused for weeks — handing protesters the win they had been demanding.

prev_ref.title: NEET protests: government offers compensation and drops FIRs, but still won't remove minister Pradhan as Saturday deadline arrives

stories.title: Babar Azam leads Pakistan out for his first Test since being reinstated as captain, as a new venue gets its Test debut
stories.what_happened: Pakistan's two-match Test series against the West Indies began today at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad — the ground's first-ever Test match. It's the first Test Babar Azam has led as captain since Pakistan's board reinstated him in that role, replacing Shan Masood after a run of poor results. West Indies go in as slight favourites on home soil, with forecasters warning that passing showers, typical for Trinidad in July, could interrupt play at points across the five days.
key_points: Pakistan's two-match Test series in the West Indies got underway today in Tarouba, Trinidad
It's Babar Azam's first Test in official charge since Pakistan reinstated him as captain over Shan Masood
The Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba is hosting its first-ever Test match
Rain is forecast to interrupt play at points during the five-day match

depth.background: Pakistan's Test team has struggled for consistency in recent years, prompting the board to swap captains between Babar Azam and Shan Masood more than once. After a brutal run under Masood, Pakistan's board recently reinstated Babar as Test captain, hoping his experience can steady a team searching for a settled identity in the format's toughest arena.

thread.previously: Pakistan's board reinstated Babar Azam as Test captain, dropping Shan Masood after a brutal run of results.
thread.changed: Babar has now led the team out for his first Test in charge, as the series against West Indies gets underway at a brand-new venue in Trinidad.

prev_ref.title: Pakistan reinstates Babar Azam as Test captain, dumping Shan Masood after a brutal run

stories.title: Iran signs 25 deals with China, Russia and Central Asia at an SCO summit, rejecting US 'bullying' as its war grinds on
stories.what_happened: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters at the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan on July 24-25 that Tehran will not bow to US 'bullying and coercion,' and said the real obstacle to US-Iran talks is not a lack of communication channels but Washington's pressure tactics. SCO foreign ministers, including Araghchi, signed 25 cooperation documents covering security, trade, transport connectivity, energy and digital cooperation, and made progress toward setting up an SCO development bank. Araghchi held bilateral meetings with Russia's Sergey Lavrov and Pakistan's Ishaq Dar on the sidelines.
key_points: Iran's FM Araghchi says Tehran won't bow to US pressure at Shanghai Cooperation Organisation talks
SCO foreign ministers signed 25 cooperation documents in Kyrgyzstan
Deals span security, trade, transit, energy and a proposed SCO development bank
Comes as Iran remains under sustained US strikes elsewhere in the war

depth.background: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) is a China- and Russia-led political and security bloc that also includes Pakistan, India, and several Central Asian states — built partly as a counterweight to Western-led institutions. Iran formally joined in 2023. With the US and its allies maintaining sanctions and now conducting military strikes against it, Iran has leaned harder on the SCO and its members as an alternative source of trade, investment and diplomatic cover.

stories.title: Five drivers take grid penalties for Sunday's Hungarian GP after engine and parts changes
stories.what_happened: Carlos Sainz, Lando Norris, Lance Stroll, Isack Hadjar and Fernando Alonso will all take grid penalties for Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix after their teams fitted new engine components or other parts that exceed each driver's allocation for the season. The penalties apply regardless of where each driver qualifies.
key_points: Sainz, Norris, Stroll, Hadjar and Alonso all take penalties
Penalties come from engine and component changes ahead of the race
It scrambles the grid regardless of Sunday's qualifying result
Comes in the same weekend Antonelli extends his championship lead from Spa

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli arrives in Hungary leading the championship by 45 points after winning from pole at Spa-Francorchamps, with Mercedes teammate George Russell out of that race after a first-lap crash. Several teams are using the Budapest weekend to fit upgraded engines and parts before F1's summer break.

stories.title: Red Bull rejects a reported $3 billion offer for its Racing Bulls junior team
stories.what_happened: Red Bull has reportedly rejected an approach worth around $3 billion (about £2.2bn) for its Racing Bulls team, led by US-based investor Dean Attew — a former adviser to ex-F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone — together with financier Andrew Herriot and backing from Abu Dhabi-based investment funds. Neither Red Bull nor the bidders have officially confirmed the approach or its rejection. It follows earlier reported offers of just over $2 billion that Red Bull also turned down in the past year.
key_points: Red Bull reportedly turned down a ~$3bn Abu Dhabi-backed bid for Racing Bulls
Bid was fronted by ex-Ecclestone adviser Dean Attew and financier Andrew Herriot
It's at least the second big offer Red Bull has rejected in the past year
Keeping Racing Bulls preserves Red Bull's young-driver pipeline into F1

depth.background: Red Bull runs a two-team F1 structure: the main Red Bull Racing team, and Racing Bulls (formerly Toro Rosso/AlphaTauri), a junior team used to develop young drivers before they graduate to the senior team or move elsewhere on the grid. F1 team valuations have surged in recent years as the sport's global popularity and Liberty Media's commercial push have made even smaller teams attractive, unconfirmed-bid targets for outside investors.

stories.title: Malaysia's PM says a formal Sepang F1 return announcement is coming this Sunday
stories.what_happened: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said his government will make an announcement on Sunday, July 27, about a possible Sepang return to the F1 calendar this year — most likely as a stand-in race around early October, replacing one of the cancelled Middle East rounds. Malaysia's Ministry of Youth and Sports has been in active discussions with F1 about the logistics.
key_points: PM Anwar Ibrahim says an update on Malaysia's F1 return comes Sunday, July 27
Sepang hosted F1 from 1999–2017 and still holds F1-grade certification
Race would fill a slot left by cancelled Bahrain and Saudi Arabia races
Talks had been rumor-stage until this confirmation

depth.background: The Sepang International Circuit hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix on F1's calendar from 1999 to 2017, before being dropped over rising hosting costs. It has stayed in competitive shape since, still hosting MotoGP, and retains the FIA Grade 1 certification required to host F1 again. Earlier this year, escalating conflict in the Middle East forced F1 to cancel the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, leaving holes in the 2026 calendar that organizers have been scrambling to fill.

thread.previously: Malaysia and F1 were reported to be in early talks about a stand-in Sepang race this year, floated as a replacement after the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix were thrown into doubt by the regional conflict.
thread.changed: Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim confirmed a formal announcement on the Sepang return is coming this Sunday, July 27 — moving it from rumor to an imminent official call.

prev_ref.title: F1 eyes a surprise Sepang return this year as a stand-in race, with Middle East races in doubt

stories.title: Centre and NEET protesters head into a third round of talks today, with minister Pradhan's exit still the sticking point
stories.what_happened: The Centre and CJP are set for a third round of talks today, after two earlier rounds with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh produced no breakthrough. CJP's central demand — Pradhan's resignation — remains unresolved; the group calls it non-negotiable. The government has given in-principle approval to two lesser demands (compensating families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and withdrawing FIRs against protesting students) but CJP wants those commitments in writing before today's meeting. The government separately dismissed 47 officials at the National Testing Agency (NTA), the body that conducts NEET, as an administrative response to the leak.
key_points: Third round of Centre-CJP talks set for 3:30-4pm today, after two earlier rounds broke down
CJP calls Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation 'non-negotiable'
Government has given in-principle approval on compensation and dropping FIRs, but wants it in writing
Centre has so far given no sign it will consider removing Pradhan

depth.background: The protests began after the NEET-UG (India's national medical entrance exam) paper leak, which student groups say the government mishandled — including the suicide of an aspirant, Riya Thapa, that became a rallying point. The protest group, calling itself the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), has been camped at Delhi's Jantar Mantar for weeks, and Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk's 26-day hunger strike (which ended Friday after the government agreed to compensate victims' families) turned the movement into one of India's largest youth protests in years.

thread.previously: We reported the government had offered compensation to victims' families and agreed to drop FIRs against protesting students, but was still refusing to remove Minister Pradhan, with a Saturday deadline looming.
thread.changed: That Saturday deadline is today: a third round of talks is scheduled for this afternoon, CJP wants the earlier concessions in writing, and the government has still given no indication it will act on Pradhan's resignation.

prev_ref.title: NEET protests: government offers compensation and drops FIRs, but still won't remove minister Pradhan as Saturday deadline arrives

stories.title: Europe's wildfires turn deadly: three firefighters killed as blazes reach Sicily, Bordeaux orders new evacuations
stories.what_happened: Two firefighters were killed battling a blaze near Bordeaux airport in southwest France, and a third died fighting fires in Sicily. French authorities ordered fresh evacuations in three Bordeaux suburbs as an 'unprecedented' fire that has already burned roughly 19,000 hectares of the Gironde region keeps spreading; around 40,000 people have been moved out of the area this week. In Spain, the largest active fire is still burning in Guadalajara province near Madrid, having scorched about 32,000 hectares. French President Emmanuel Macron activated the EU's civil-protection mechanism, bringing in water-bombing planes from other member states.
key_points: Two firefighters die near Bordeaux, France; one dies fighting fires in Sicily, Italy
France has now burned over 50,000 hectares this year — nearly 3x last year's pace
Bordeaux suburbs Le Haillan, Eysines and Mérignac ordered to evacuate as the 'largest fire of the season' spreads
Macron activates the EU's cross-border firefighting mechanism for the first time this summer

depth.background: A brutal heatwave and months of drought have primed southern Europe's forests to burn. Spain, France and Italy fight wildfires most summers, but this year's blazes started earlier and have already scorched more land than the 20-year average — even after 2025 set the modern record. Spain declared a national emergency on Friday as fires threatened towns near Madrid.

thread.previously: We reported over 200,000 people had fled fires in France and Spain, with Madrid's regional government declaring its first-ever national emergency as blazes closed in on towns near the capital.
thread.changed: The fires have now killed three firefighters for the first time this summer, spread into Sicily (Italy), forced fresh evacuations in Bordeaux's suburbs, and pushed Macron to activate the EU's cross-border firefighting mechanism.

prev_ref.title: Europe's wildfires explode: 200,000+ flee France and Spain as Madrid declares its first national emergency

stories.title: Kimi Antonelli could pull off a feat no F1 driver has managed since 1950 — winning the title on home soil
stories.what_happened: With Antonelli 45 points clear at the top of the standings after his Belgian GP win, attention has turned to whether the 2026 calendar will end at Imola — which would hand him a shot at clinching the title in front of his home crowd, something achieved only once in F1's 76-year history. The final calendar slot is tied up with talks over Sepang, Malaysia's push to rejoin the calendar for the first time since 2017.
key_points: Antonelli, 19, leads the 2026 championship by 45 points after his Belgian GP win
If Imola hosts the season finale, he could clinch the title at his home race
Only Giuseppe Farina — F1's very first champion, in 1950 — has ever won a title on home turf
Whether Imola gets the finale hinges on a wider calendar shuffle, including a possible Sepang, Malaysia return

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli is an Italian rookie who became the youngest championship leader in F1 history this season with Mercedes. His home race is the Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix at Imola, near Bologna. F1 calendars are finalized late and reshuffled often — races get added, dropped or moved for political, financial and logistical reasons — so which race closes out a season isn't locked in until relatively close to the year itself.

stories.title: Namibia and Netherlands clash today in a World Cup qualifying tri-series with 2027 spots on the line
stories.what_happened: Namibia opened the tri-series by bowling Nepal out for just 157, with JJ Smit taking 6 for 27, then chasing the total down with 8 wickets to spare. Namibia now plays host Netherlands today in Utrecht — the tri-series' 117th match overall in the wider League 2 competition — in a fixture that matters directly for 2027 World Cup qualification math, with Netherlands looking to tighten its grip on third place in the standings.
key_points: Namibia already beat Nepal, bowling them out for 157 behind JJ Smit's 6-27
Namibia faces the Netherlands today in Utrecht in a must-not-lose fixture
Top four in the League 2 table advance to the 2027 World Cup Qualifier
Bottom four are pushed into a tougher Qualifier Play-off route

depth.background: Outside the sport's biggest nations, Nepal, Netherlands and Namibia are locked in a tri-series of one-day internationals at Utrecht's Sportpark Maarschalkerweerd, part of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 — the qualification pathway that decides who reaches the 2027 Cricket World Cup Qualifier tournament, a step below the World Cup itself.

stories.title: Zelensky warns of a new 'massive' Russian strike, as Ukraine hits back at a Russian refinery 2,000km from the front
stories.what_happened: Following Friday's strike on the Kyiv-area arms exhibition, President Zelensky said Saturday that Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia has 'readied missiles' for a further 'massive' attack within 48 hours. In response, Ukraine's special forces struck the Tyumen oil refinery deep inside Russia, roughly 2,000km from the front line — a sign Ukraine's long-range strike capability keeps expanding. Russia's defense ministry said it downed 571 Ukrainian drones overnight, and Kyiv region declared July 25 a day of mourning for Friday's strike victims.
key_points: Zelensky says intel shows Russia has 'readied missiles' for a massive strike within 48 hours
Comes a day after a Russian missile killed 10 at a Ukrainian arms exhibition near Kyiv
Ukraine struck Russia's Tyumen oil refinery deep inside Russian territory in response
Russia says it downed 571 Ukrainian drones overnight

depth.background: Russia has been at war with Ukraine since its 2022 invasion; despite periodic US-brokered diplomatic efforts to end the fighting, both sides continue trading long-range strikes deep behind the front lines. On Friday, July 24, a Russian ballistic missile struck an arms exhibition near Kyiv, killing at least 10 people including senior Ukrainian security officials — one of the deadliest single strikes on Ukrainian soil in months.

thread.previously: A Russian ballistic missile struck an arms exhibition near Kyiv on July 24, killing at least 10 people including senior Ukrainian security officials — one of the deadliest single strikes on Ukrainian soil in months.
thread.changed: Zelensky now warns Russia has 'readied missiles' for a further massive strike within 48 hours, and Ukraine has retaliated by striking a Russian oil refinery 2,000km from the front line.

stories.title: Fernando Alonso's Aston Martin future in doubt again, with retirement and an Alpine return both back on the table
stories.what_happened: With no contract in place for 2027, Alonso says he won't decide his future until after F1's summer break. Paddock reporting this weekend has revived speculation that he could return to Alpine, now being rebranded as Gucci Racing Alpine under Flavio Briatore, someone Alonso has a long working relationship with — though Alonso has publicly denied any such move. At the same time, some in the paddock believe Aston Martin's 'deep crisis' (just one point from the first 10 races of 2026) could see him retire outright rather than change teams.
key_points: Alonso, 44 and out of contract for 2027, says he'll decide his future only after the August summer break
His options: retire at the end of 2026, stay at Aston Martin, or leave for a seat elsewhere
Alpine — being rebranded as Gucci Racing Alpine under Alonso's longtime ally Flavio Briatore — is the 'hottest' rumoured destination, though Alonso has denied it
Some in the paddock reportedly believe Aston Martin's dire 2026 form (one point from 10 races) could push him to simply walk away

depth.background: Alonso is a two-time world champion in his 40s, widely regarded as one of the grid's most complete drivers even this late in his career, and previously drove for Alpine (then Renault) earlier in his career. He joined Aston Martin on a multi-year deal but the team has struggled badly this season.

stories.title: US strikes on Iran pause for the first time in two weeks as Saudi Arabia opens a new front, hitting Houthi-held Hodeidah
stories.what_happened: For the first time since the bombing campaign began, US Central Command made no announcement of new strikes on Iran on Friday, and Iranian state media reported no strikes or explosions overnight into Saturday. Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan — the three countries Iran has struck hardest — also reported no new attacks. Separately, Saudi Arabia launched strikes on the Houthi-held Yemeni port city of Hodeidah, its most direct military action of the war so far, responding to the Houthi attacks on its oil tankers earlier in the week. President Trump said the US remains 'locked and loaded' while pursuing talks, and that he believes Iran is 'getting more serious' about reaching a deal.
key_points: US Central Command reported no new strikes on Iran overnight for the first time in ~13 days
Iranian state media has not reported explosions inside the country since Friday
Saudi Arabia struck Yemen's Houthi-held port city of Hodeidah — its most direct entry into the war yet
Trump says the US is 'locked and loaded' but Tehran is 'getting more serious' about a deal

depth.background: A ceasefire between the US/Israel and Iran collapsed earlier this month, and the US has bombed Iranian targets nearly every night since — 13 consecutive nights by Friday. Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in Yemen have used the chaos to attack shipping and, this week, two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, dragging Saudi Arabia toward direct involvement in a war it had mostly stayed out of.

thread.previously: We reported Trump saying a larger, 'massive' US attack on Iran might not be necessary because Tehran was showing signs of getting serious about a negotiated deal.
thread.changed: Overnight strikes on Iran actually paused for the first time in nearly two weeks, while Saudi Arabia opened a new front by striking Houthi-held Hodeidah in Yemen — so the war widened even as the US-Iran track went quiet.

prev_ref.title: Trump says a 'massive' Iran attack 'may not be necessary' as Tehran gets 'serious' about a deal

stories.title: Hungaroring gets emergency overnight repairs after F1 drivers say the resurfaced track is breaking apart
stories.what_happened: During Friday's practice sessions for the Hungarian Grand Prix, multiple drivers reported that the newly resurfaced sections of track were bumpy, inconsistent, and in places visibly opening up under load — worst at Turn 1, a major overtaking spot, and around the final corners, where drivers said they had to avoid the apex (the inside racing line) entirely to stay on stable tarmac. The FIA and Hungaroring confirmed they carried out emergency repairs to two problem areas overnight ahead of Saturday's qualifying.
key_points: Drivers complained during Friday practice that newly resurfaced sections were bumpy and breaking up
Worst spots were Turn 1 (a key overtaking zone) and the final corners
FIA and Hungaroring carried out emergency repairs overnight before Saturday running
Track was resurfaced in spring as part of a wider circuit upgrade programme

depth.background: Race tracks get resurfaced periodically to fix wear and improve grip, but new tarmac needs time and the right conditions to bond properly — done badly, it can crumble under the extreme loads Formula 1 cars put through corners at 200mph+. The Hungaroring redid several turns, including Turn 1, this spring as part of a broader circuit upgrade.

stories.title: Assam's flood toll jumps to 61 — 14 people died in a single day as 700,000+ are now affected
stories.what_happened: Assam's disaster management authority said Saturday that the flood death toll had jumped to 61, with 14 of those deaths occurring in just the preceding 24 hours — a sharp acceleration. Charaideo district alone reported 7 new deaths, Sivasagar 6, and Jorhat 1. More than 7.05 lakh people are now affected across nine districts, with Sivasagar (roughly 3.5 lakh affected), Charaideo (1.9 lakh) and Jorhat (1.3 lakh) hit hardest. Relief has reportedly not yet reached over 80,000 people stranded in cut-off areas. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the situation "remains critical," and a central government assessment team was scheduled to visit Saturday.
key_points: Assam's flood death toll rose sharply to 61, with 14 of those deaths in just the last 24 hours
Charaideo and Sivasagar districts saw the sharpest jump — 7 and 6 new deaths respectively
More than 7 lakh (700,000) people are now affected across nine districts; relief hasn't reached over 80,000 people in cut-off areas
A central government team was due to assess the damage in Assam on Saturday

depth.background: Assam floods almost every monsoon season (June-September) because the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell with rain from across the region, including Nagaland and the Himalayan foothills. Earlier this week the state's flood toll stood at 47 dead with 40 missing, part of a wider wave of cloudbursts and floods that had already killed dozens across India's Himalayan and west-coast states. Assam's Chief Minister has pointed to heavy rain spillover from neighbouring Nagaland as a factor behind the latest surge.

thread.previously: We reported that cloudbursts, flash floods and landslides had battered a wide swathe of India — from the Himalayan states to the west coast — killing dozens and displacing thousands, with nearly a third of India's states getting 60% more rain than normal on July 23.
thread.changed: The crisis has now concentrated and sharply worsened in Assam specifically: the death toll has climbed to 61 (from 'dozens' reported across the whole country), with 14 deaths in a single day, and over 700,000 people affected in Assam alone — far more specific and severe than the nationwide picture we had before.

stories.title: Assam's flood death toll jumps to 61 — 14 people died in a single day
stories.what_happened: The Assam State Disaster Management Authority said the death toll rose to 61 after 14 more people died in the past 24 hours — seven in Charaideo district, six in Sivasagar, and one in Jorhat, among them 11 men and three women. More than 7.05 lakh people are now affected across 12 districts, with Sivasagar (about 3.48 lakh affected), Charaideo (1.88 lakh) and Jorhat (1.27 lakh) hit hardest. Over 3.15 lakh people have taken shelter in 363 relief camps, and NDRF and SDRF teams evacuated nearly 1,000 people from marooned areas on Friday.
key_points: 14 more deaths in the last 24 hours push the toll to 61
Over 7.05 lakh (705,000) people affected across 12 districts
Sivasagar is worst-hit with over 3.48 lakh people affected
Over 3.15 lakh people are sheltering in 363 relief camps

depth.background: Assam's monsoon floods, driven by an overflowing Brahmaputra river, had already turned catastrophic — the toll stood at roughly 50 dead and 700,000 displaced as of yesterday's count, with the Centre sending a team to assess the damage.

thread.previously: We reported Assam's monsoon floods had turned catastrophic, with at least 50 dead and 700,000 displaced as the Brahmaputra overflowed.
thread.changed: The toll has climbed to 61 after 14 deaths in a single day, with over 705,000 now affected across 12 districts.

stories.title: Trump quietly halts nightly US strikes on Iran, breaking a 13-day streak
stories.what_happened: US Central Command did not announce any new overnight strikes on Iran for the first time since the campaign began nearly two weeks ago. Trump directed the military not to conduct new strikes on Friday, breaking the daily-attack pattern. Iran also reported no new strikes on American targets overnight.
key_points: US skipped a night of strikes on Iran for the first time in nearly two weeks
Trump personally ordered the pause on Friday, officials say
No new Iranian strikes on US targets were reported either
Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites kept a separate front open

depth.background: On June 27, a US-brokered ceasefire between Israel/the US and Iran collapsed, and the US began nightly bombing runs on Iranian targets that ran for 13 straight days. At least four US service members and dozens of Iranians have been killed since. Trump had recently floated a 'massive attack' but also said negotiations might make it unnecessary.

thread.previously: We reported Trump was floating that a bigger attack on Iran might not be necessary and was considering negotiations, even as US strikes hit a 13th consecutive night.
thread.changed: That talk turned into action: the US skipped a night of strikes entirely for the first time since the campaign began, and Iran didn't retaliate either — though officials caution it may not last.

stories.title: Houthis hit back at two Saudi Aramco oil sites, setting a refinery ablaze as Brent tops $100
stories.what_happened: In the early hours of Saturday, Houthi forces fired a barrage of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco-linked sites in the Red Sea towns of Jazan and Yanbu. A Houthi military spokesperson said it was retaliation for the Saudi strike on Hodeidah and Kamaran Island. NASA's satellite fire-monitoring system detected an abnormal temperature spike at Jazan around 4:17am local time, and residents filmed a fire burning at the refinery. At least five explosions were reported in Jazan; nearby commercial flights were diverted.
key_points: Dozens of missiles and drones hit Aramco facilities in Jazan and Yanbu
Fire breaks out at the Jazan refinery, one of Saudi's newest, 400,000 barrels/day
Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's main working oil-export route now that Hormuz is blocked
Brent crude jumped back above $100 a barrel on the news

depth.background: Since a US-Israel campaign against Iran began earlier this year, Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in Yemen have been attacking ships and infrastructure to pressure the Gulf states that back the US position. Saudi Arabia struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in Yemen days ago, hitting back after Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping. The Strait of Hormuz — the narrow chokepoint at the mouth of the Gulf that a large share of the world's oil passes through — has already been effectively closed by the fighting, so Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export terminal, has become one of the last ways Saudi oil reaches world markets.

thread.previously: We reported Saudi Arabia struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in Yemen, retaliating for Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping.
thread.changed: The Houthis have now hit back directly at Saudi soil, striking Aramco facilities in Jazan and Yanbu, setting a refinery on fire and pushing Brent crude back above $100 a barrel.

prev_ref.title: Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi-held Hodeidah, opening a new front as it hits back for Red Sea attacks

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's claim it's 'getting more serious' about talks — a general says Tehran would welcome a US ground invasion
stories.what_happened: Speaking Friday, Trump said the US and Iran remain in contact and that he believes Iran is 'getting more serious' about a negotiated end to the war. An Iranian military official identified by state media as General Asadi publicly rejected that characterization, saying Iran's fight is a 'war of attrition' with no end date, and adding Iran hopes American ground forces put themselves in a position where Iran 'can engage them on the ground.' Trump separately told reporters the US military is 'locked and loaded' for a heavier attack if Iran doesn't return to serious talks.
key_points: Trump said Friday the US and Iran are still talking and Tehran is 'getting more serious'
An Iranian general publicly dismissed that, saying Iran's war is 'one that will not end'
The same general said Iran wants US ground troops to 'find themselves in a position where we can engage them'
No new US strikes were reported Friday night, after 13 consecutive nights of bombing

depth.background: The US, Israel and Iran agreed a memorandum of understanding weeks ago meant to open 60 days of talks toward a wider peace deal covering Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz. That truce collapsed, and the US has since bombed targets inside Iran for 13 straight nights. Trump has said he could end the war either 'diplomatically or militarily,' and has floated both continued talks and a bigger strike.

stories.title: Rohit Sharma answers retirement talk the only way that matters — with a Lord's century
stories.what_happened: India lost the deciding 3rd ODI to England at Lord's by 27 runs, with England posting a List A-record 387/3 (Ben Duckett 141) and India replying with 360/7. Rohit Sharma scored 138 — his 34th ODI century and the first-ever men's ODI hundred by an Indian batter at Lord's — but it wasn't enough to prevent England winning the series 2-1, their first series win over India since 2018. Days later, BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla said in Agra that there was 'no question' of Rohit's retirement and that he remains part of the team.
key_points: Rohit scored 138 at Lord's, his 34th ODI century, in a losing cause
England won the 3rd ODI by 27 runs and the series 2-1
BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla publicly shut down retirement rumours
Rohit, 39, has already retired from Tests and T20Is; ODIs are his last format

depth.background: Rohit Sharma retired from Test cricket in 2025 and from T20Is earlier, keeping ODIs as his only remaining international format with an eye on playing the 2027 ODI World Cup. A poor run of ODI form on India's England tour had fuelled speculation that Lord's might be his farewell series.

stories.title: Big Tech's 'open-weight AI' letter doubles to 50 signatories overnight, as Washington weighs curbing Chinese AI models
stories.what_happened: More than two dozen companies — including Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, IBM, Dell, CrowdStrike, Palantir, Hugging Face, Perplexity, Mistral and the Linux Foundation — signed an open letter urging US policymakers not to impose broad "premature restrictions" on open-weight AI models. Within a single day the signature count nearly doubled to 50, with OpenAI and Google joining. Amazon and Anthropic have not signed.
key_points: Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and ~20 others signed a letter defending open-weight AI models
Signatures nearly doubled to 50 in a single day, adding OpenAI and Google
Comes as Washington debates restricting Chinese open-weight models like DeepSeek
Amazon and Anthropic are notably still not on the list

depth.background: "Open-weight" AI models are ones where the company publishes the actual trained parameters, so anyone can download, run, and modify them for free — unlike closed models such as flagship GPT or Claude versions, which you can only use through the company's paid service. Open-weight models, like Meta's Llama or China's DeepSeek, have become central to a US-China rivalry: they spread fast and get built into products everywhere, and Washington has grown worried that letting Chinese open-weight models dominate could hand China long-term influence over global AI infrastructure — so some policymakers now want to restrict them.

stories.title: F1 lines up Imola and Sepang as backup venues in case Iran tensions force Qatar and Abu Dhabi off the calendar
stories.what_happened: With the US and Iran locked in an escalating standoff that has already put fuel-shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz at risk, F1 organizers have quietly lined up backup plans for the season's Middle East finale. Imola is the leading candidate to replace Qatar's race on the same November 29 weekend if it's scrapped, which would mark F1's first European season finale in nearly 30 years, since Jerez in 1997. Sepang is separately being considered as an alternative for an early-October date. The tension has also ended any chance of Bahrain returning to the calendar this year.
key_points: F1's 2026 season is due to finish in Qatar (Nov 29) and Abu Dhabi (Dec 6)
Escalating US-Iran tensions have put both Gulf races in doubt
Imola (Italy) is the leading contingency to host the season finale instead
Sepang (Malaysia) is also on standby for an early-October slot

depth.background: Formula 1's calendar has leaned heavily on the Gulf region in recent years, with Qatar and Abu Dhabi hosting the season's final two races. That only works if the region is stable enough for teams, sponsors and fans to travel safely. Imola, officially the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari, is one of F1's classic European circuits and hosted a round as recently as 2025; Sepang, in Malaysia, held F1 races from 1999 to 2017 before dropping off the calendar.

stories.title: DRC's Ebola outbreak becomes the fastest-spreading ever recorded — deaths pass 1,300
stories.what_happened: The death toll from DRC's current Ebola outbreak has surged past 1,300, with confirmed cases topping 3,000 as of this weekend — a more than 40% jump in just five days, according to Al Jazeera and UN reporting. A public health official described the virus as 'spreading like a wildfire.' Neighboring Uganda has also confirmed cases, and isolated imported cases have turned up as far away as France and the United States.
key_points: Confirmed cases have climbed past 3,000; deaths have surpassed 1,300
Cases rose more than 40% in just five days
WHO says the virus is 'spreading like a wildfire'
Most new infections can't be traced to a known source, making containment harder

depth.background: Ebola is a severe viral disease first identified near the Ebola River in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 1976; it causes fever, severe bleeding, and organ failure, and has killed a large share of those infected in past outbreaks. The DRC has battled more Ebola outbreaks than any other country, but health officials say this one — declared earlier this year — is spreading faster than any previous outbreak on record.

stories.title: Anahat Singh, 18, becomes the first Indian ever to win the World Junior Squash title
stories.what_happened: Anahat Singh won the girls' singles final at the 2026 World Squash Junior Championships in Niagara-on-the-Lake, Canada, beating Egypt's Ruqayya Salem in straight games (11-3, 11-7, 11-9) on July 25, 2026. It's the first time a non-Egyptian player has won the title since 2010, ending a 15-year run of Egyptian champions. Singh dropped just two games across her entire six-match run to the title. Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly congratulated her.
key_points: Beat Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 11-3, 11-7, 11-9 in the final in Canada
Ends Egypt's 15-year grip on the girls' singles title
First non-Egyptian champion since an American won it in 2010
Dropped only two games across her whole six-match campaign

depth.background: Squash is a fast indoor racket sport played in a four-walled court; the World Junior Championships are the sport's top under-19 event, and Egypt has dominated the girls' singles title for the better part of two decades thanks to its deep youth squash pipeline. Anahat Singh is an 18-year-old Indian player who has been rising through junior and senior ranks for several years and was already a national talking point after past regional junior titles.

stories.title: Sarnath, where the Buddha gave his first sermon, is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site
stories.what_happened: UNESCO's World Heritage Committee formally inscribed the 'Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath' on the World Heritage List during its 48th session in Busan, South Korea, on July 25, 2026. The listing covers the Deer Park area, including the Dhamek Stupa (a large dome-shaped Buddhist shrine) and the Dharmarajika and Chaukhandi Stupas. It is India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly welcomed the news.
key_points: UNESCO's World Heritage Committee inscribed Sarnath on July 25 at its Busan, South Korea session
It's India's 45th World Heritage site
The nomination had waited 28 years for approval
Site includes the Dhamek Stupa, Dharmarajika Stupa, and Chaukhandi Stupa near Varanasi

depth.background: Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, is one of Buddhism's four holiest sites — it's where, over 2,500 years ago, the Buddha is believed to have delivered his first sermon after attaining enlightenment, setting out the core teachings that became Buddhism. UNESCO's World Heritage List recognizes places of outstanding cultural or natural value to humanity; getting on it brings global recognition, tourism potential, and stronger legal protection against damage or unchecked development. India first nominated Sarnath decades ago.

sources.name: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

stories.title: Verstappen can now trigger an exit clause to leave Red Bull for 2027 — if he's not top-2 by August
stories.what_happened: Verstappen's contract includes an exit clause letting him leave Red Bull for another team in 2027, but only if he's outside the top two positions in the Drivers' Championship when the sport's summer break begins in August. Kimi Antonelli currently leads the championship with 204 points, with Lewis Hamilton second and George Russell third — meaning Verstappen, who has struggled with Red Bull's 2026 car, is not currently inside the top two and would be eligible to trigger the clause. He would have a three-month window, from August to October, to make the move official. His manager says the Verstappen camp wants to decide quickly, possibly before the break even starts.
key_points: Verstappen is signed through 2028, but his contract has a release clause
It activates if he's outside the top 2 in the championship at the start of August's summer break
He'd get a 3-month window (August–October) to use it
His manager says a decision could come 'possibly even before the summer break'

depth.background: Verstappen signed a seven-season extension with Red Bull running to 2028 — an unusually long deal in F1, where top drivers typically sign 2-3 year contracts. He reportedly had 'longstanding apprehension' about the sweeping new technical rules introduced for 2026, and got Red Bull to agree to a specific escape route in case the new-rules car wasn't competitive.

stories.title: OpenAI fully launches GPT-5.6 Sol after a month-long US government security review
stories.what_happened: OpenAI said this weekend it has now fully released GPT-5.6 Sol, its most capable model yet, after the US government's review pushed the launch back about a month from its original July 9 preview. Access is still limited to roughly 20 vetted organizations while a broader public rollout is prepared 'in the coming weeks.' On the 'Agents' Last Exam' benchmark, a test of long, professional, multi-step tasks across 55 fields, Sol scored 53.6, more than 13 points ahead of the closest rival model from Anthropic.
key_points: OpenAI's most advanced model, delayed a month at Washington's request
A new executive order lets the government preview 'frontier' AI models first
Sol beats rival models on complex reasoning and coding benchmarks
Public rollout still limited to about 20 vetted partners for now

depth.background: OpenAI first previewed the GPT-5.6 family on July 9, 2026 - three tiers called Sol (flagship), Terra (mid-tier), and Luna (fast and cheap). Weeks earlier, on June 2, President Trump signed an executive order letting AI companies voluntarily give the US government up to 30 days of early access to any 'frontier' model before it reaches the public, so officials can check for national-security risks like cyberattack or bioweapon misuse. OpenAI ran Sol through that window before releasing it more widely.

stories.title: Israel locks down northern West Bank and raids a village after a deadly settler-Palestinian shootout
stories.what_happened: On Friday, a group of Israeli settlers entered a restricted area near the Palestinian village of Tal, close to Nablus, for what officials called an unauthorized, uncoordinated hike. Clashes broke out with local residents, and in the gunfire that followed, four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers were killed. Accounts differ: Palestinian officials say settlers provoked the confrontation by trying to attack villagers; Israel's military first described the civilians involved as unarmed hikers, then acknowledged some were armed and said both sides had opened fire before troops intervened. In response, Israel reinforced troops, imposed a curfew across large parts of the northern West Bank, postponed soldiers' leave, and on Saturday carried out a large-scale raid on a village near Nablus, capturing two people linked to the shooting. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also ordered military demolitions, new movement restrictions on Palestinians in the area, and moves to legalize outposts that are currently illegal even under Israeli law.
key_points: 4 Palestinians and 2 Israeli soldiers killed Friday near the village of Tal, close to Nablus
Israeli settlers were on an 'unauthorized' hike into a restricted area when clashes broke out
Israel imposed a curfew, reinforced troops, and raided a nearby village, capturing two suspects
Netanyahu ordered demolitions, new movement restrictions on Palestinians, and moved to legalize illegal outposts

depth.background: The West Bank is Palestinian territory that Israel has militarily occupied since 1967; roughly 500,000 Israeli settlers now live there in communities most of the world considers illegal under international law, alongside about 3 million Palestinians. Friction between settlers and Palestinian villagers over land and access is constant, and 'unauthorized hikes' by settlers into Palestinian-controlled or restricted areas have repeatedly been the spark for deadly clashes in recent years.

stories.title: Critical, unpatched security flaw in Alibaba's Fastjson is being actively exploited — no fix exists yet
stories.what_happened: Security researchers at FearsOff discovered a critical vulnerability in Fastjson, tracked as CVE-2026-16723, that lets an attacker send a specially crafted piece of JSON data to a vulnerable application and run their own code on it — no password or login required. Fastjson's maintainers published an advisory on July 21. Security firm ThreatBook confirmed real-world attacks starting July 22. As of the latest reporting on July 25, Alibaba had not released a fix, and the attack works even when standard safety settings that normally block similar bugs are turned on.
key_points: CVE-2026-16723, severity 9.0 out of 10 — critical
Affects Fastjson 1.2.68 through 1.2.83, widely used in enterprise Java apps
Attackers can run code with no login needed, no patch available yet
Active attacks confirmed since July 22, mostly against US firms

depth.background: Fastjson is a free code library, maintained by Chinese tech giant Alibaba, that lets Java programs read and write JSON data (a common format for exchanging information between computer systems). Because it's fast and free, it got embedded into huge numbers of enterprise applications built on Java and Spring Boot — the same programming stack used by banks, hospitals, retailers and many other large organizations worldwide.

stories.title: First death confirmed as Spain and France wildfires grow to 25,000 hectares; Germany sends aid
stories.what_happened: Authorities in Manises, Spain confirmed the fires' first fatality. Fire officials say roughly 30 separate blazes are burning simultaneously across southwestern France's Gironde and Landes regions, with the total burned area now near 25,000 hectares. Around 50,000 people remain affected in the wider Madrid region alone. Germany has sent an A400 military transport plane, helicopters and rescue personnel to reinforce French firefighting crews.
key_points: One person confirmed dead in Manises, Spain
Fires have burned roughly 25,000 hectares so far — nearly the size of a mid-sized city
About 30 separate fires are still burning across southwestern France
Germany is sending helicopters, a military transport plane and rescuers to help French firefighters

depth.background: Spain and France are in the grip of an unusually intense, record-breaking wildfire season, driven by a prolonged heatwave and tinder-dry vegetation across southern Europe. Officials in both countries had already evacuated more than 250,000 people, and Spain had declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency. Fires like this spread fastest when high heat, low humidity, and strong wind combine — exactly the conditions much of the Iberian Peninsula and southwestern France have seen this month.

thread.previously: Wildfires had forced over 250,000 evacuations across southwestern France and central Spain, and Spain declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency as the fire season hit a record.
thread.changed: The fires have now claimed their first confirmed death, grown to roughly 25,000 hectares, and Germany has sent military aircraft and rescue crews to reinforce French firefighters.
