stories.title: A record US parasite outbreak has topped 11,000 cases this year — and the FDA just found a second, unexplained cluster
stories.what_happened: Of the 11,000-plus total US cases this year, 1,644 have been directly linked to Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia, with 94 hospitalizations and no deaths. An FDA lab test that had flagged the lettuce was later retracted as a false positive — but the agency says the lettuce is still considered linked to the outbreak based on the broader pattern of illness. Separately, on July 23 the FDA said it had identified an entirely new cluster of 72 Cyclospora cases tied to a different, as-yet-unidentified food product.
key_points: Over 11,000 Cyclospora cases confirmed in the US in 2026 — more than four times a typical year
1,644 cases traced to Taco Bell's shredded iceberg lettuce, supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico
The FDA just identified a brand-new 72-case outbreak from a food source it hasn't pinned down yet
No deaths reported; the illness causes days of watery diarrhea, cramping, and severe fatigue

depth.background: Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that spreads through food or water contaminated with human feces — most US outbreaks are traced to imported fresh produce, especially leafy greens and herbs, because the parasite survives washing and is hard to detect with routine food-safety testing. A typical year sees only 200 to 1,000 US cases. 2026 has already blown past 11,000, making it one of the worst years on record. On July 17, Taylor Farms de Mexico recalled all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico after investigators traced illnesses at Taco Bell locations across five states back to it.

stories.title: The EU fines Google $1 billion for rigging its own search results and app store — the first fine of its kind
stories.what_happened: The European Commission fined Google €890 million (about $1 billion): €460 million for giving its own services more prominent placement in search results (bigger visuals, top-of-page positioning) than competitors get, and €430 million for 'anti-steering' — blocking app developers on the Play Store from telling their own users about cheaper ways to pay outside the app. Google now has 60 days to change these practices or face further daily penalties that can reach 5% of its total worldwide revenue.
key_points: Brussels says Google favored its own services over rivals in search results and the Play Store
€890 million ($1B) fine — the first-ever penalty under the EU's Digital Markets Act
Google has 60 days to change its practices, or face fines of up to 5% of its global revenue
Google says the ruling is unjustified and plans to appeal

depth.background: In 2023 the EU brought in the Digital Markets Act (DMA), a tougher law aimed squarely at a handful of giant tech platforms it calls 'gatekeepers' — companies so dominant that smaller rivals can't realistically compete on a level playing field. Unlike older antitrust cases, which could take a decade of litigation before any real consequence landed, the DMA is designed to issue findings and penalties fast, with escalating fines if a company doesn't comply. Google has been fined by the EU before — including a record €4.3 billion in 2018 over its Android practices — but this is the first time it has been punished specifically under the new DMA regime.

stories.title: HAL signs a long-term deal with France's Safran to build parts for the world's best-selling jet engine
stories.what_happened: HAL and Safran Aircraft Engines signed a multi-year agreement at the Farnborough International Airshow in the UK for HAL to produce near-net-shape superalloy ring forgings for the LEAP engine at its Ring Rolling facility in Bengaluru. These ring forgings sit in the hottest, most stressed rotating section of the engine, so they are made to extremely tight tolerances — even small defects can be catastrophic.
key_points: Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) will manufacture superalloy turbine ring forgings for the CFM LEAP engine
Deal signed at the Farnborough Airshow, to be made at HAL's Ring Rolling facility in Bengaluru
The LEAP engine powers most new Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX jets worldwide
It's India's entry into the global commercial supply chain for the world's most-produced jet engine

depth.background: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) is India's state-run aerospace manufacturer, historically focused on building and maintaining military aircraft for the Indian armed forces. The CFM LEAP is a joint venture engine built by America's GE Aerospace and France's Safran, and it's the single most common engine powering new narrow-body airliners globally — the workhorse behind most new Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX deliveries. Landing a role in its supply chain is different from HAL's usual defence work: it's a commercial, globally competitive contract judged purely on manufacturing quality and reliability.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton says he 'really believes' he can still win the title — but admits he must 'step it up' after his Spa crash
stories.what_happened: Ahead of the Hungarian GP, Hamilton said he 'really believes' Ferrari can put him in title contention, but that he needs to 'step it up' and 'come correct' after a crash compromised his recent Belgian Grand Prix weekend at Spa. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella separately said he expects Ferrari to be 'extremely competitive' at the Hungaroring, a circuit that rewards chassis and cornering strength over raw engine power.
key_points: Hamilton sits 2nd in the standings, 45 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli
He says he 'can't afford' to repeat the mistake that wrecked his Belgian GP weekend
Ferrari's chassis is expected to suit Hungary's twisty circuit better than recent tracks
Hungary is the last race before F1's four-week summer break

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton, F1's most decorated driver, moved to Ferrari after more than a decade at Mercedes, chasing a record-extending world title with the sport's most storied team. His first seasons at Ferrari have been a mixed bag as he and the team adjust to each other. Going into the Hungarian Grand Prix — the final race before F1's mandatory summer shutdown — he trails 18-year-old championship leader Kimi Antonelli by 45 points.

stories.title: Trump says the US-Saudi nuclear deal is off unless Saudi Arabia normalizes ties with Israel
stories.what_happened: On Wednesday, the US and Saudi Arabia signed a civilian nuclear deal that bars uranium enrichment and is limited to non-military use. But on Thursday, Trump said publicly that the deal is "totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining" the Abraham Accords — a condition that was not part of the agreement as announced a day earlier. The White House press secretary backed him up, saying the deal is "off" unless Saudi Arabia normalizes relations with Israel. An unnamed Saudi source pushed back, saying the deal was already signed and there's "nothing to renegotiate."
key_points: Trump adds a brand-new condition to a US-Saudi civil nuclear deal signed just a day earlier
Says Saudi Arabia must join the Abraham Accords — the US-brokered pacts normalizing Arab-Israel ties
Saudi Arabia has long said it won't normalize with Israel without a path to Palestinian statehood
A Saudi source says the deal is signed and "nothing to renegotiate" — a standoff neither side has resolved

depth.background: The Abraham Accords, launched in Trump's first term in 2020, got several Arab states — including the UAE and Bahrain — to formally normalize relations with Israel for the first time, breaking with the traditional Arab League position that recognition should wait until Palestinians get their own state. Saudi Arabia, the region's most influential power, has held out: it has said for years that it will only normalize ties with Israel once there's a genuine, "irreversible and time-bound" path to Palestinian statehood — a step the current Israeli government has strongly resisted. Washington and Riyadh had separately been negotiating a civil nuclear cooperation deal, letting Saudi Arabia build nuclear power plants under US supervision.

stories.title: Infosys beats Q1 estimates as AI deals convert into real revenue, but margins stay tight
stories.what_happened: Infosys reported Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) revenue of $5,082 million, up 2.4% year-on-year and 1% sequentially in constant currency, alongside an operating margin of 21.1%. Earnings per share grew nearly 15% year-on-year in rupee terms. The company signed large deals worth a combined $3.6 billion in total contract value, 61% of which was net-new business rather than renewals. CEO Salil Parekh highlighted that AI-related work, powered by the company's 'Topaz' AI platform, is increasingly turning into paid revenue rather than staying in pilot mode.
key_points: Infosys Q1 FY27 revenue: $5,082 million, up 2.4% year-on-year
Operating margin held near 21.1%, EPS up nearly 15% in rupee terms
Large deal wins worth $3.6 billion, 61% of it genuinely new business
CEO says 'AI momentum is now rapidly converting into revenue'

depth.background: Infosys is India's second-largest IT services company and a bellwether for the broader Indian IT sector, whose revenue depends heavily on corporate spending decisions in the US and Europe. For the last couple of years, big IT firms like Infosys have been under pressure to show that all the money clients are pouring into AI projects is actually turning into billable revenue for them — not just internal experimentation that never becomes a paid contract.

stories.title: A US judge sets a June 2027 trial date for Venezuela's captured ex-leader Nicolás Maduro
stories.what_happened: A federal judge in New York, Alvin Hellerstein, set June 1, 2027, as the start date for Maduro and Flores's trial on federal drug-trafficking, narco-terrorism conspiracy, and firearms charges, which could carry a life sentence if he's convicted. The date was set at the request of lawyers on both sides at a Wednesday hearing. Maduro's defense lawyer said he will first try to get the case dismissed by arguing Maduro has sovereign immunity as a former head of state.
key_points: Judge Alvin Hellerstein set June 1, 2027 as the trial date for Maduro and his wife
Both face US drug-trafficking and narco-terrorism charges, and have pleaded not guilty
Maduro was seized from Venezuela by US commandos in a January raid, jailed in Brooklyn since
His lawyers plan to argue the case should be thrown out on sovereign-immunity grounds

depth.background: Nicolás Maduro led Venezuela as president from 2013 until January 2026, when US forces carried out a military operation that captured him and his wife Cilia Flores at their compound in Caracas and flew them to the US to face charges. Washington had accused Maduro for years of running Venezuela as a narco-state; his removal ended over a decade of rule marked by economic collapse, mass emigration, and disputed elections. Since then, his vice-president Delcy Rodríguez has led the country as acting president.

stories.title: Oil just crossed $100 a barrel for the first time since May — Goldman says $120 could be next
stories.what_happened: Brent futures surged about 7% to settle at $100.69 a barrel on Thursday, crossing the $100 mark for the first time in two months, after reports that Yemen's Houthi rebels struck two oil tankers off Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia had been routing more oil through the Red Sea via a pipeline to avoid the Strait of Hormuz — but the new attacks show that route isn't safe either.
key_points: Brent crude jumped about 7% in a day, closing above $100.69 a barrel
First time above the $100 psychological line since late May
Triggered by fresh attacks on tankers off Saudi Arabia amid the Iran war
Goldman Sachs says Brent could top $120 next quarter if the disruption continues

depth.background: Brent crude is the global benchmark price for oil pumped from the North Sea — traders use it to price roughly two-thirds of the world's oil. Its price has been climbing for weeks as the US-Israel war with Iran drags on, threatening the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb strait near Yemen — two narrow shipping lanes that together carry a huge share of the world's seaborne oil.

thread.previously: We covered the Houthi strikes on two Saudi tankers as a new dangerous front opening up alongside the collapsing Iran ceasefire.
thread.changed: That attack has now shown up directly in oil prices — Brent crossed $100 a barrel for the first time since May, and Goldman Sachs is now warning of $120 next quarter if the disruption continues.

stories.title: Pakistan's U19 women level their series 2-2 against South Africa — decider set for today in Karachi
stories.what_happened: Chasing South Africa's 109 for 8, Pakistan's U19 women were nearly derailed by leg-spinner Respect Mabasa's three wickets, but an unbeaten 70-run partnership between Zoofishan Ayyaz (44 not out) and captain Fizza Fiaz (28 not out) got them home by six wickets with four balls to spare, levelling the series at 2-2 heading into Friday's decider.
key_points: Pakistan's U19 women beat South Africa's U19 women by 6 wickets in the 4th match
That win levelled the five-match youth T20I series 2-2
Zoofishan Ayyaz (44 not out) and captain Fizza Fiaz (28 not out) shared an unbeaten 70-run stand
The series decider (5th T20I) is scheduled for today, July 24, in Karachi

depth.background: This is an unofficial five-match Youth T20I series between Pakistan's and South Africa's Under-19 women's teams, played in Karachi — part of the pipeline that develops future senior international players on both sides.

stories.title: US jobless claims crash to a level not seen since 1969 — even as Wall Street just had its worst day in weeks
stories.what_happened: Initial claims fell by 22,000 to 187,000 in the week ended July 18, well below the roughly 210,000 economists expected, and continuing claims also declined. The data landed the same day the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all sold off sharply — Tesla dropped 14% and Alphabet 7% on earnings, while oil prices jumped on Middle East tensions.
key_points: Weekly unemployment claims fell to 187,000, far below the 210,000 forecast
That's the lowest level since 1969
Signals employers still aren't cutting jobs, despite market turmoil
Landed the same day stocks fell hard on oil prices and AI-spending fears

depth.background: Initial jobless claims are a weekly US government count of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time — one of the fastest, most current reads on whether companies are laying people off, released every Thursday. The Federal Reserve watches this number closely because a weakening labor market is one of the main reasons it would cut interest rates.

stories.title: The US House votes again to stop Trump from expanding the Iran war — and it barely passes
stories.what_happened: The House voted 214-208 on Thursday to pass a resolution demanding an end to unauthorized US military action against Iran — the second such vote this year. Four Republicans (Tom Barrett, Warren Davidson, Thomas Massie and Brian Fitzpatrick) crossed over to join every Democrat in voting yes. The Senate was expected to vote on a similar resolution later the same day.
key_points: House passes a resolution 214-208 to limit Trump's Iran strikes
Four Republicans broke ranks to join all Democrats
Second time this year the House has passed the same warning
It's symbolic — the Senate is unlikely to send it to Trump's desk

depth.background: The War Powers Resolution is a 1973 US law passed after Vietnam, meant to stop presidents from waging war indefinitely without Congress's say-so. It lets Congress pass a resolution ordering troops to pull back — but a president can veto it, and overriding a veto needs two-thirds of both chambers, a bar Congress almost never clears. Trump has been trading strikes with Iran since a ceasefire collapsed, and has vowed to bomb an Iranian bridge or power plant every time Iran hits a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: India's wholesale prices post their sharpest jump in over a decade — and traders now bet the RBI has to raise rates
stories.what_happened: The RBI's own July bulletin described the economy as broadly resilient, even as it flagged rising WPI and elevated global oil prices as risks. Wholesale inflation has climbed to roughly 9.87% for June — its steepest rise outside the pandemic years — while the rupee trades near an all-time low against the dollar. Interest-rate swap markets are now pricing meaningfully higher odds of an RBI rate hike at its October meeting.
key_points: Wholesale price inflation (WPI) jumped to about 9.87% in June — the fastest pace outside the Covid years
Fuel, power and manufactured goods are the biggest drivers, as oil stays elevated on Middle East tensions
Swap markets now price roughly a 1-in-3 chance the RBI hikes rates as soon as October, up from near 1-in-10 a week ago
The rupee is trading near a record low, around ₹96.5 per dollar

depth.background: WPI (Wholesale Price Index) tracks how much prices change at the factory-gate/wholesale level — before goods reach a shop shelf — and is different from the CPI retail inflation number most people follow, though WPI moves tend to show up in retail prices with a lag. The RBI (Reserve Bank of India) is India's central bank; its main job is keeping inflation in check, mainly by setting the repo rate, the interest rate at which it lends to banks. Until recently, markets expected the RBI to keep cutting rates to support growth.

stories.title: F1's rulebook makers want a word — with Alonso and Newey, not Verstappen, at Hungary this time
stories.what_happened: The FIA confirmed its Hungarian Grand Prix press-conference lineup: Fernando Alonso, Franco Colapinto and Carlos Sainz in the drivers' session, with Adrian Newey representing Aston Martin as team rep. Max Verstappen was left off this weekend's list — the FIA rarely calls back the same drivers who attended the previous race, and Verstappen was on the panel last time out.
key_points: The FIA's official Thursday press conference features Fernando Alonso and Aston Martin design chief Adrian Newey
Max Verstappen is left out this weekend under the FIA's rotation practice
Alonso appears alongside Alpine's Colapinto and Williams' Sainz
Comes as drivers plan to confront the FIA this weekend over recent Hamilton and Leclerc penalties

depth.background: Every F1 race weekend, the FIA (the sport's governing body) picks a rotating panel of drivers plus one team representative for its mandatory Thursday press conference — part media duty, part a formal channel for teams to raise issues with regulators directly. Adrian Newey is regarded as F1's most decorated car designer; he left Red Bull for Aston Martin in 2025.

stories.title: Red Bull is bleeding senior staff before Hungary — and Verstappen's advice is blunt: just replace them
stories.what_happened: At Thursday's Hungary media day, Verstappen addressed the team's ongoing staff exodus directly, saying Red Bull should 'carry on' and focus on finding new talent rather than dwelling on who has left. Team principal Laurent Mekies separately acknowledged that uncertainty around Verstappen's own 2027 future is prompting other drivers to already inquire about a possible seat opening.
key_points: Red Bull has lost a wave of senior technical staff in recent months
Verstappen says the team should stop dwelling on it and 'find new talent'
Comes as Red Bull already faces questions over car form and Verstappen's own future
Team boss Laurent Mekies confirms other drivers are already asking about Verstappen's seat

depth.background: Red Bull won four straight drivers' and constructors' titles with Verstappen before rivals closed the gap. Since design chief Adrian Newey left for Aston Martin in 2025, the team has continued to lose senior engineers and strategists — the kind of staff turnover that doesn't show up in a single race result but compounds over a season of car development.

stories.title: Ukraine sends 223 drones deep into Russia overnight, hitting an oil refinery and 'Russia's Amazon'
stories.what_happened: Overnight into Thursday, Ukraine launched a large drone barrage across Russian territory. Russia's Defense Ministry said its air defenses intercepted 223 fixed-wing drones over regions including Belgorod, Bryansk, Rostov, Tatarstan and occupied Crimea. Despite the interceptions, a fire broke out at the NS-Oil refinery in Ulyanovsk Oblast (about 400 miles from the border), and explosions were reported near a Wildberries logistics hub — Wildberries being Russia's largest e-commerce company, commonly nicknamed 'Russia's Amazon'. A 3-year-old boy died and his parents were injured when a downed drone started a house fire in Voronezh.
key_points: Russia says it shot down 223 Ukrainian drones over 19 regions overnight
A refinery 400 miles inside Russian territory was hit and caught fire
Drones also struck a hub of Wildberries, Russia's biggest online retailer, dubbed 'Russia's Amazon'
A 3-year-old boy died in Voronezh when a downed drone sparked a house fire

depth.background: Ukraine has spent much of 2026 building up a long-range drone program to strike deep inside Russia — hitting oil refineries, pipelines and logistics networks that fund and supply Moscow's war effort, since Ukraine can't match Russia's conventional firepower. Russia, in turn, has been hitting Ukrainian civilian delivery and logistics networks. This exchange is widely read as Ukraine retaliating in kind: going after the Russian equivalent of the courier and retail infrastructure Russia has been targeting inside Ukraine.

stories.title: Tesla craters 14%, Magnificent Seven lose $767 billion in a day as the AI-spending trade cracks
stories.what_happened: Tesla and Alphabet both reported Q2 2026 earnings on Wednesday, and Wall Street didn't like either. Tesla's profit came in far below expectations and CEO Elon Musk warned 2026 would be 'a massive capex year' — the stock tumbled 14% on Thursday to an 11-month low. Alphabet beat estimates but raised its 2026 capex guidance to as much as $205 billion, and investors punished it anyway. Together, the sell-off wiped out roughly $767 billion from the Magnificent Seven's combined market value — their worst one-day drop since the tariff turmoil of April 2025 — while Brent crude pushing toward $100 a barrel added to the gloom.
key_points: Tesla plunged 14% to an 11-month low after missing profit estimates
Alphabet fell too, its earnings beat overshadowed by its $205bn spending plan
The 'Magnificent Seven' megacap tech stocks lost $767 billion in value in one session
Rising oil prices from the Iran war added to inflation worries dragging the Nasdaq down

depth.background: The 'Magnificent Seven' is the nickname for the seven US tech giants — Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Meta, Nvidia and Tesla — whose combined size has driven most of the US stock market's gains since 2023, largely on excitement about AI. For over a year, these companies have been locked in a spending race, pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into data centers and chips (known as 'capex', or capital expenditure) to build AI infrastructure, betting the returns will eventually justify the cost.

thread.previously: Yesterday, Alphabet beat earnings estimates on 82% cloud growth but still fell 3-6% after-hours because it raised its 2026 capex guidance to $205 billion — investors worried spending was outrunning proof of AI profits.
thread.changed: Today that worry spread across the whole sector: Tesla's own profit miss and capex warning joined Alphabet's, and together they dragged the full Magnificent Seven basket down $767 billion in its worst single-day drop since April 2025, with rising oil prices compounding the sell-off.

prev_ref.title: Alphabet's cloud business grew 82% — but Wall Street punished the stock anyway, over a $205 billion spending plan

stories.title: India-US trade deal comes down to the 'last one percent' — with a tariff deadline hours away
stories.what_happened: With a temporary US tariff arrangement on Indian goods set to expire Friday, July 24, negotiators describe the first phase of the deal's legal text as parked at its 'last one percent' — essentially finished but not yet signed. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar reinforced the push to close the interim agreement, even as Washington separately threatens new tariffs on pharmaceutical imports. The reciprocal tariff on Indian goods currently stands at 18%, already reduced from an earlier 25% threat.
key_points: A temporary US tariff arrangement on Indian goods expires Friday, July 24
Negotiators say the first phase of a trade deal is done except for the final 1% of legal text
Rubio and Jaishankar pushed to close the deal despite new US threats on pharma tariffs
The current US tariff on Indian goods sits at 18%, down from a threatened 25%

depth.background: In 2026, the Trump administration has been imposing 'reciprocal tariffs' — import taxes set to match what the US says other countries charge American goods — as leverage in trade talks. India and the US have spent months negotiating an interim Bilateral Trade Agreement, with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer haggling over market access, agriculture and non-tariff barriers, under a shared 'Mission 500' goal of doubling two-way trade to $500 billion by 2030.

stories.title: Commonwealth Games 2026 open in Glasgow — Mirabai Chanu carries India's flag, Lovlina Borgohain the baton
stories.what_happened: India's contingent, led by flag bearer Mirabai Chanu and baton bearer Lovlina Borgohain, marched in the opening ceremony at Glasgow's Hydro arena on Thursday, formally starting the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Indian athletes were already in action earlier the same day, with the lawn bowls pair opening India's campaign in Glasgow.
key_points: The Commonwealth Games officially open today at Glasgow's Hydro arena
Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu is India's flag bearer, boxer Lovlina Borgohain the baton bearer
Chanu is a two-time Commonwealth Games gold medallist; Borgohain is chasing her first CWG medal
India's contingent had already begun competing hours earlier in lawn bowls

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from Commonwealth nations (mostly former British territories, including India, the UK, Australia and dozens of others). Glasgow last hosted in 2014 and steps in again for 2026. Carrying the flag and baton at the opening ceremony is one of the highest honors a nation gives its athletes — Chanu is a Tokyo Olympics silver medallist and two-time CWG champion (2018, 2022), while Borgohain is a Tokyo bronze medallist still seeking her first Commonwealth Games medal.

stories.title: Nepal's World Cup qualifying hopes take a hit as Netherlands chase them down with 35 balls to spare
stories.what_happened: Netherlands beat Nepal by 6 wickets in Utrecht on Thursday, bowling Nepal out for 157 before chasing the target down with 35 balls unused. Netherlands captain and wicketkeeper Scott Edwards anchored the chase with an unbeaten 61 off 89 balls and was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Netherlands beat Nepal by 6 wickets in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 in Utrecht
Nepal were bowled out for 157; Netherlands chased it down with overs to spare
Wicketkeeper-captain Scott Edwards top-scored with 61 not out and won Player of the Match
The loss makes it harder for Nepal to break into League 2's automatic-qualifying top 4

depth.background: The ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 is a multi-year one-day-international competition for lower-ranked cricket nations like Nepal, Netherlands, Namibia, Oman and the USA, where the top four finishers earn a route toward qualifying for the 50-over Cricket World Cup. Nepal went into today's match sitting fifth in the table with 28 points from 28 games — just outside that top-four cutoff — as part of a tri-series with Netherlands and Namibia running through July 31.

thread.previously: Nepal went into today's match sitting fifth in the League 2 table with 28 points from 28 matches — just outside the top four needed for direct qualification to the 2027 World Cup Qualifier — calling it a near-must-win fixture.
thread.changed: Nepal lost, bowled out for 157 and chased down by Netherlands with 35 balls to spare, making their push into the top four measurably harder with the tri-series' remaining matches now more critical.

prev_ref.title: Nepal's World Cup qualification hopes are on the line as they face the Netherlands in a must-win tri-series match

stories.title: Aston Martin's biggest upgrade of the year arrives late for Hungary — with the summer break bearing down
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin's much-anticipated upgrade package for Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll did not arrive at the Hungaroring on schedule, with the new parts only expected late Thursday evening — leaving mechanics significantly less time to build and check the car before Friday's practice. Chief trackside officer Mike Krack admitted the team is racing against time on spare-parts availability, after months of delaying performance development specifically to solve reliability problems first.
key_points: Aston Martin's revamped 'B-spec' AMR26 missed its scheduled arrival at the Hungaroring
The team held back performance upgrades all season to fix reliability problems first
Team principal Adrian Newey hopes it delivers a 'large step' in performance
Mechanics now have less time than planned to fit it before Friday practice

depth.background: Aston Martin has struggled through the 2026 F1 season and made a deliberate trade-off: instead of chasing speed early, the team spent months fixing reliability issues on its AMR26 car, delaying the aerodynamic upgrades it hoped would make it competitive. A 'B-spec' car is essentially a major mid-season redesign — new parts across the car rather than small tweaks — and Hungary is the last race before F1's mandatory three-week summer shutdown, making it the team's final chance this half of the season to test whether the gamble paid off.

stories.title: England confirms its 2027 Ashes schedule — and for the first time in memory, none of it is in cricket-mad northern England
stories.what_happened: The England and Wales Cricket Board announced its full 2027 fixture list on Thursday. The men's five-Test Ashes series runs June 18 to August 2, starting at Trent Bridge (Nottingham) and moving through Lord's, Edgbaston, the Utilita Bowl (Rose Bowl) in Southampton — hosting its first-ever men's Ashes Test — before finishing at The Oval. Neither Headingley nor Old Trafford, the two traditional northern venues, is hosting a men's Test in this cycle; Nottingham is the northernmost stop. The women's multi-format Ashes series opens June 24 at Headingley, which will host its first women's Ashes Test since 2001. The ECB also confirmed a four-day warm-up match between a full-strength England Lions side and Australia at Old Trafford from June 7-10.
key_points: 5-Test men's Ashes runs June 18 to August 2, 2027: Trent Bridge, Lord's, Edgbaston, the Rose Bowl, The Oval
Neither Headingley (Leeds) nor Old Trafford (Manchester) hosts a men's Test
The Rose Bowl in Southampton gets its first-ever men's Ashes Test
Women's Ashes opens June 24 at Headingley — its first women's Ashes Test since 2001

depth.background: The Ashes, contested between England and Australia since 1882, is Test cricket's oldest and most storied rivalry. Traditionally, hosting duties rotate around England's largest Test grounds, and the northern venues Headingley and Old Trafford have long produced some of the series' most passionate crowds and dramatic matches. Which grounds get an Ashes Test is a major financial event for the host city, driving hotel bookings, hospitality spending and tourism for the days around the match.

stories.title: India's weightlifting quota at the Commonwealth Games is slashed after five Indian lifters test positive for doping, sending Dilbag Singh home
stories.what_happened: Five Indian weightlifters tested positive for doping violations in the period from June 1, 2025 to July 22, 2026, triggering a rule that cut India's weightlifting quota for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow from 16 places down to 11. As a result, weightlifter Dilbag Singh, who competes in the men's 94kg category, was withdrawn from India's squad, along with judoka Arun Kumar. Dilbag was not personally implicated in any doping case — reports note he had also been struggling with a back injury and had been unable to train fully during India's preparatory camp in Birmingham, making the call a difficult but practical one.
key_points: Five Indian weightlifters tested positive for doping between June 2025 and July 2026
The violations cut India's weightlifting quota at CWG 2026 from 16 places to 11
Dilbag Singh (men's 94kg) and judoka Arun Kumar are among those withdrawn
Dilbag himself was not among those who failed a test — he's a quota casualty

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games, a multi-sport event for athletes from Commonwealth nations, allocates each country a fixed number of competitor slots per sport based on qualification performances. Anti-doping violations by a country's athletes in the run-up to a Games can trigger quota reductions as a penalty, even for athletes who personally tested clean — a rule meant to hold national federations collectively accountable for doping culture.

stories.title: Lahore Qalandars beat Perth Scorchers XI by 16 runs in the opening match of the new Global Super League
stories.what_happened: In the opening match of the Global Super League 2026 at Providence Stadium, Guyana, Lahore Qalandars posted 171 for 7 in their 20 overs and defended it to beat Perth Scorchers XI, who fell short on 155 for 7, a margin of 16 runs.
key_points: Lahore Qalandars scored 171/7, Perth Scorchers XI replied with 155/7
Result came in the very first match of the new Global Super League
Played at Providence Stadium in Guyana
Tournament brings together champion franchise teams from around the world

depth.background: The Global Super League is a new T20 tournament that brings together the champion franchise teams from major domestic T20 leagues around the world — including Pakistan's PSL and Australia's Big Bash — to compete against each other, similplaying on the idea of European football's Champions League for franchise cricket. Lahore Qalandars are champions of Pakistan's PSL, while the Perth Scorchers are a leading Australian Big Bash franchise; the tournament kicked off today in Guyana.

stories.title: Ferrari finally debuts a high-downforce 'Macarena' rear wing at Hungary, months after Hamilton flagged the team was missing a trick
stories.what_happened: Ferrari introduced a high-downforce version of its 'Macarena' rear wing for the Hungarian Grand Prix, featuring three curved mini winglets stacked vertically in a triple-element design similar to one McLaren used at Monaco earlier this season. Lewis Hamilton had said earlier in the year that Ferrari missed a trick by not producing a high-downforce wing of this kind for Monaco, where several rivals used one; the Hungaroring, one of the highest-downforce circuits on the calendar, is now where Ferrari brings its own version.
key_points: Ferrari brings a triple-element 'Macarena' rear wing for Hungary
Design swaps mechanical actuators for stacked mini winglets for extra downforce
Rivals McLaren and Red Bull already used similar wings since Monaco
Hamilton had said earlier this year Ferrari missed a trick by not having one

depth.background: In modern F1, teams bring specialized 'high-downforce' rear wing packages to a handful of slow, twisty circuits each year — like Monaco and now Hungary — where cornering grip matters far more than top speed. A popular way to add extra downforce recently has been stacking multiple small curved winglets ('Macarena' wings, nicknamed for their layered look) instead of relying purely on moving parts, and several rival teams adopted this approach months ago.

stories.title: The FIA confirms four 'Active Aero' zones on a revised Hungaroring track map for this weekend's race
stories.what_happened: The FIA confirmed a revised track map for this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix showing four zones where Straight Mode will be active: the start/finish straight, the straight between Turns 1 and 2, a new zone on the uphill run to Turn 4, and the short straight between Turns 11 and 12. The point where cars detect they're close enough to trigger the separate Overtake Mode boost will be on the entry to the final corner, with the boost itself usable from the corner's exit.
key_points: A revised track map shows four Active Aero 'Straight Mode' zones at the Hungaroring
Two zones are on the start/finish straight and the Turn 1-2 straight
A new zone allows it on the uphill climb to Turn 4
Another covers the short straight between Turns 11 and 12

depth.background: Since 2026, F1 cars use 'Active Aero' — moveable front and rear wings that drivers can open on straights to cut drag and gain speed — instead of the old DRS (Drag Reduction System) button, which only ever affected the rear wing and could be used only when chasing a car ahead. Active Aero's 'Straight Mode' opens automatically in designated track zones for every car, while a separate 'Overtake Mode' still gives a following driver an extra energy boost only when they're close behind a rival, similar to the old DRS.

stories.title: Assam floods kill 10 more in a day, pushing the week's death toll to 36 as 650,000 people are hit across 11 districts
stories.what_happened: Assam recorded at least 10 more flood deaths in the 24 hours to Thursday, taking the state's death toll for the week to 36. More than 650,000 people have been affected by flooding across 11 districts, with authorities calling the scale of damage to farmland, homes and infrastructure 'unprecedented.' Separately, a mother and son were swept away and killed by fast-moving floodwater in Bandipora district of Jammu & Kashmir.
key_points: 10 killed in Assam in the last 24 hours alone
State's flood death toll for the week reaches 36
650,000+ people affected across 11 districts
Trigger: extreme rain fell in neighbouring Nagaland on July 18-20

depth.background: Assam sits on the Brahmaputra river's floodplain and floods almost every monsoon, but authorities are calling this week's flooding 'unprecedented.' It follows days of very heavy rain in the hills of neighbouring Nagaland, which drained down into Assam's rivers and pushed them over their banks. A separate weather system has also brought deadly flooding this week to parts of Pakistan and Afghanistan.

stories.title: Leinster Lightning thrash North West Warriors to win Ireland's Inter-Provincial Cup final
stories.what_happened: Leinster Lightning posted a huge 446/6 batting first in the Inter-Provincial Cup final in Dublin. North West Warriors, chasing the total, fell well short, finishing on 170/5 with Andy McBrine top-scoring with 86 off 81 balls, as Leinster completed a dominant win to take the trophy.
key_points: Leinster posted 446/6 batting first in the 50-over final in Dublin
North West Warriors finished well short on 170/5 chasing
Andy McBrine top-scored for the Warriors with 86 off 81 balls
Leinster complete the season having topped the group stage

depth.background: Ireland's Inter-Provincial Cup is the country's main domestic 50-over (List A) competition, contested by its provincial teams — the same pool many Ireland international players come through. Leinster Lightning had finished top of the group stage, setting up this final against North West Warriors in Dublin.

stories.title: Cadillac is still pointless at the halfway mark of its debut F1 season — after a penalty took away what would've been its first point
stories.what_happened: At the season's halfway point, Cadillac remains the only team without a single championship point. Perez had appeared to score the team's first-ever point with a 10th-place finish in Monaco, but a post-race penalty dropped him to 15th, erasing it. Heading into this weekend's Hungarian GP, Perez said he expects Aston Martin's heavily revised car — getting a full aerodynamic overhaul and weight cut in Budapest — to 'close the gap' and move ahead of Cadillac, while his own team brings a bolstered brakes package.
key_points: Cadillac has zero points through half of its debut 2026 season
Perez finished 10th in Monaco but a post-race penalty dropped him to 15th
Aston Martin's Hungary B-spec car could 'close the gap,' Perez warns
Cadillac brings its own brakes upgrade to Hungary

depth.background: Cadillac is the first entirely new team to join F1's grid since Haas in 2016, fielding experienced drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez for its first season in 2026. New teams typically take a few seasons to become competitive; Haas itself scored points in its debut year, so a winless half-season raises real questions about where Cadillac stands against that bar.

stories.title: Spain brings back a nearly-extinct native cow breed to fight wildfires with grazing, not firefighters
stories.what_happened: Community associations in Galicia, backed by regional subsidies to keep female calves rather than sell them, have rebuilt the native-livestock population to over 30,000 animals — including about 8,000 Cachena cows, up from just 400. Galicia is one of Spain's most fire-prone regions, having burned nearly 119,000 hectares (about double the area of Madrid) last year alone.
key_points: Galicia is reviving the Cachena, a small, nimble native cow nearly wiped out decades ago
Native livestock in the region has grown from 1,800 in the 1990s to over 30,000 today
Their grazing keeps flammable scrubland short, starving wildfires of fuel before they start
Comes the same week wildfires killed three firefighters across France, Italy and Greece

depth.background: Decades ago, mass planting of fast-growing pine and eucalyptus for the timber and pulp industry pushed out small native breeds like the Cachena — nicknamed 'goat-cows' for their ability to eat almost anything on steep terrain. Without grazing animals, scrubland grew unchecked into ready-made fuel for wildfires. A devastating 2017 fire in the Galician parish of Vincios pushed local communities to revive the old practice.

stories.title: Meesho halves its losses and grows revenue 48% in its first results as a listed company
stories.what_happened: Meesho's revenue from operations rose to ₹3,713 crore from ₹2,504 crore a year earlier, while its net loss shrank to ₹132.8 crore from ₹289.3 crore. Its EBITDA loss (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization — a measure of core operating losses before accounting adjustments) also narrowed, to ₹224.7 crore from ₹264.4 crore.
key_points: Net loss narrows 54% year-on-year to ₹132.8 crore, from ₹289.3 crore
Revenue jumps 48% to ₹3,713 crore
Transacting users up 29% to 274 million; orders up 29% to 725 million
Reported the same day as Infosys, IndiGo, Cipla and Dr Reddy's Q1 results

depth.background: Meesho is India's social-commerce and value e-commerce platform, built around reaching small-town and rural 'Bharat' shoppers rather than big-city customers, and recently listed on Indian stock exchanges. Like other new-age internet listings such as Paytm and Zomato's parent Eternal, investors are watching closely for a credible path to profitability.

stories.title: PM Modi announces fast-track courts for exam paper leaks, as the injured protester who galvanized the 'Cockroach' movement is taken off ventilator
stories.what_happened: Modi announced the government will set up fast-track courts specifically to deliver swift, stringent punishment in paper-leak cases, saying 'nothing is more important than the welfare and future of the youth' and 'no one who tampers with the future of our youth will be spared.' Separately, Delhi's RML Hospital confirmed the critically injured student protester has been extubated, is conscious and responding normally, with a normal brain and spine MRI.
key_points: Modi announces fast-track courts to punish paper-leak culprits: 'no one will be spared'
Comes three days after the Cockroach Janta Party's Parliament march turned violent
The 21-year-old student critically hurt in the police crackdown is now off ventilator, conscious
CNBC reports the youth movement is now seen as a direct test of Modi's political standing

depth.background: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) began as a social-media joke mocking a judge's remark comparing unemployed youth to 'cockroaches,' then grew into a genuine youth movement demanding accountability for the NEET medical-entrance exam paper-leak scandal and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. A march on Parliament last week ended in clashes, with over 118 police and around 60 protesters injured and a 21-year-old woman critically hurt after colliding with a barricade during the crackdown.

thread.previously: We explained how the Cockroach Janta Party movement began as a social-media joke mocking a judge's remark about unemployed youth, and grew into a mass youth movement demanding accountability for the NEET paper-leak scandal and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
thread.changed: PM Modi has now directly responded by announcing fast-track courts for paper-leak cases, while the 21-year-old protester critically injured in last week's police crackdown at Jantar Mantar has been taken off ventilator support and is recovering — and CNBC reports the movement is now seen as a genuine test of Modi's political leadership.

prev_ref.title: India's 'Cockroach' movement, explained: how a joke about students became a nationwide challenge to Modi

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants bowl out London Spirit for just 80 in The Hundred, as Ryana MacDonald-Gay takes four wickets
stories.what_happened: Put in to bat at Lord's, London Spirit were bowled out for just 80, with Ryana MacDonald-Gay taking 4 wickets to spearhead the collapse. Manchester Super Giants chased the target down with wickets to spare to seal the win.
key_points: London Spirit women collapse to 80 all out at Lord's — among their lowest-ever Hundred totals
Manchester Super Giants' Ryana MacDonald-Gay leads the rout with four wickets
Super Giants chase down the target comfortably to complete the win
Result boosts Manchester's push up The Hundred women's table

depth.background: The Hundred is England and Wales Cricket Board's 100-ball franchise competition, contested by eight city-based teams with parallel men's and women's tournaments that often share the same match day at the same venue.

stories.title: Colombo Kaps beat Kandy Royals by 23 runs in the Lanka Premier League, as Angelo Mathews' fightback falls short
stories.what_happened: Batting first, Colombo Kaps set Kandy Royals 193 to win. Kandy fell short at 169/8 in their 20 overs, despite a defiant unbeaten 38 from senior all-rounder Angelo Mathews, as Colombo's bowlers took the remaining wickets to close out a 23-run win.
key_points: Colombo Kaps post 192/9, then bowl out Kandy Royals for 169/8
Win by 23 runs at Dambulla
Veteran Angelo Mathews top-scores for Kandy with 38 not out but runs out of partners
Keeps Colombo Kaps' campaign in the hunt for a Lanka Premier League play-off spot

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League is Sri Lanka Cricket's marquee T20 franchise tournament, mixing capped Sri Lankan internationals with overseas players across a short group-stage-to-playoffs format.

stories.title: Three F1 stars — Sainz, Alonso and Colapinto — all say they'll decide their 2027 futures only after the summer break
stories.what_happened: Sainz, out of contract with Williams at the end of 2026 and long linked with a possible Audi move, said he won't seriously weigh his options until the summer break, while giving his clearest signal yet that he intends to stay. Alonso, whose Aston Martin deal also expires this year, said the new rules — not his 45th birthday — will determine whether he keeps racing. Alpine is expected to decide by the summer break whether Colapinto keeps his seat alongside Pierre Gasly for 2027.
key_points: Carlos Sainz says he's 'not really' considering his future beyond Williams until the summer break
Fernando Alonso, turning 45 this month, says F1's new 2027 rules will shape his decision on racing on
Franco Colapinto is fighting to keep his Alpine seat, with a team decision expected before the break
All three spoke at Thursday's Budapest press conference ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix

depth.background: Formula 1 introduces all-new technical and engine regulations in 2027, and teams are widely holding off on driver decisions until they know how competitive their 2027 cars will actually be. With roughly 17 driver contracts expiring at the end of this season, the sport's traditional August factory shutdown — the 'summer break' — has become the real deadline for this year's driver market.

stories.title: Red Bull says it's fixed the 'super dangerous' rear wing that caused two of Verstappen's crashes — as the FIA reviews the design's safety
stories.what_happened: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said the two failures were 'mechanical, and it was two different things — two different mechanical issues,' both traced to the wing's actuation mechanism, and says the team resolved them in an update introduced at Spa. Technical director Pierre Waché said the FIA is satisfied with the standard of Red Bull's design, but the governing body has asked both Red Bull and Ferrari for more technical detail to confirm the wings operate safely under all circumstances.
key_points: Verstappen's rear wing failed to close properly in crashes at two straight races
Red Bull says it found and fixed two separate mechanical faults in the wing's mechanism
FIA is now reviewing whether Red Bull's and Ferrari's similar 'active aero' wings are safe in all conditions
The review is about safety, not a rule-breach — the FIA says the design itself meets the technical rules

depth.background: F1 introduced 'active aero' this season: front and rear wings that open on straights to cut drag and close again in corners, nicknamed 'Macarena' wings for how they move. Red Bull's version came under scrutiny after Max Verstappen crashed at two consecutive races when his rear wing failed to close on entry to a corner.

stories.title: IndiGo swings to a ₹238 crore loss as fuel costs jump 86% — even as India's biggest airline keeps growing revenue
stories.what_happened: IndiGo reported a consolidated net loss of ₹238 crore for the quarter ended June 2026, compared with a ₹2,176 crore profit in the same quarter last year. Revenue actually grew 20% to ₹24,584 crore on strong travel demand, but total expenditure rose even faster — up 34% to ₹25,853 crore — mainly because fuel costs jumped 86% year-on-year. The airline still ended the quarter with ₹52,885 crore in cash, giving it room to absorb the hit.
key_points: Revenue grew 20% year-on-year to ₹24,584 crore
But total costs climbed 34%, driven by an 86% jump in fuel expenses
Net loss of ₹238 crore, versus a ₹2,176 crore profit a year ago
IndiGo still holds roughly 65% of India's domestic flight market

depth.background: IndiGo (run by InterGlobe Aviation) is India's largest airline by far, carrying roughly two-thirds of all domestic air passengers. Airlines are extremely sensitive to fuel prices because jet fuel is typically their single biggest cost — and India's fuel costs are also shaped by global crude oil prices, which have been rising due to ongoing Middle East tensions, including the Iran-related conflict escalating in the region.

stories.title: F1 drivers to confront the FIA at the Hungarian GP over recent penalties handed to Hamilton and Leclerc
stories.what_happened: F1 drivers are set to hold talks with the FIA during the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend specifically to discuss recent penalty verdicts given to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, adding a governance dispute to a weekend already packed with on-track storylines.
key_points: Drivers have requested talks with the FIA during the Hungary weekend
The meeting centers on recent stewarding decisions involving Hamilton and Leclerc
Comes amid ongoing driver frustration with inconsistent penalty calls
Separate from, but alongside, the usual Hungarian GP media and practice schedule

depth.background: F1's stewards — officials who review incidents during a race weekend — have faced repeated criticism this season from drivers who say penalty decisions feel inconsistent from race to race. The FIA (F1's governing body) sets and enforces the sporting rules; friction between the driver group and race officials over how those rules are applied has simmered for years but has grown louder this season.

stories.title: Red Bull says Max Verstappen will stay for 2027 — even though he's now free to leave
stories.what_happened: With the clause now formally active — Red Bull sits below second in the constructors' championship at the summer break — team boss Laurent Mekies said Red Bull's plan is to keep improving the car to convince Verstappen to stay, and multiple reports say he intends to remain with the team through 2027 rather than exercise the clause.
key_points: Verstappen's exit clause is active but he's expected to stay through 2027
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies says the focus is on improving the car to keep him
The clause triggered after Red Bull's rocky start to the 2026 rules era
Removes one of the biggest question marks hanging over the driver market

depth.background: Verstappen, a four-time world champion, signed a Red Bull contract running through 2028 that included a performance-based 'exit clause' — an escape hatch he could use if the team fell out of the top two in the championship by the summer break, written in because he was wary of how a major regulation change for 2026 might affect Red Bull's competitiveness. That regulation change did hurt the team's start to the season, and speculation mounted for months that Mercedes or Ferrari could lure him away.

thread.previously: We reported that Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause had formally become triggerable after the team's rough start to the season, with rival teams already circling.
thread.changed: Red Bull now says Verstappen intends to stay through 2027 despite being free to leave, closing off the uncertainty for now.

prev_ref.title: Verstappen can now trigger an exit clause to leave Red Bull for 2027 — and rival drivers are already calling

stories.title: Australia name Sam Konstas and two other young batters for a Bangladesh warm-up match
stories.what_happened: Cricket Australia named a 14-player CA XI, including young batters Sam Konstas and Campbell Kellaway and the more experienced Kurtis Patterson, to play a three-day, red-ball warm-up match against touring Bangladesh, starting August 6 at Marrara Cricket Ground in Darwin — a week before the first Test at the same venue on August 13. The match will be played 13-a-side by agreement between the two boards and won't have official first-class status.
key_points: A 14-player Cricket Australia XI will play Bangladesh in a 3-day warm-up from August 6 in Darwin
Sam Konstas, Campbell Kellaway and Kurtis Patterson are all included
It's a week before the first Test between Australia and Bangladesh
The match won't count as first-class cricket

depth.background: Australia host Bangladesh for a two-Test series in August (Darwin, then Mackay), part of the World Test Championship — the ongoing cycle that decides which two teams reach the WTC final. Before a Test series, home boards often schedule a warm-up match using a second-tier or development squad — the 'CA XI' here — so touring teams get proper match practice and Australia can look at fringe players without risking their senior Test squad.

stories.title: Pakistan's women beat Sri Lanka by 5 wickets, thanks to a 78 from Gull Feroza
stories.what_happened: At the Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium in Hambantota, Sri Lanka Women batted first and made 210/9 off their 50 overs. In reply, Pakistan Women chased the target down comfortably, reaching 211/5 in 43 overs — a 5-wicket win with 42 balls unused. Opener Gull Feroza was the standout, scoring 78 off 77 balls with 11 fours and reaching her half-century off just 47 balls; she shared a key partnership with Sidra Amin, who made 57. Feroza was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Sri Lanka Women posted 210/9 batting first
Pakistan chased it down with 42 balls to spare, finishing 211/5
Gull Feroza top-scored with 78 off 77 balls and won Player of the Match
Pakistan lead the 3-match ODI series 1-0

depth.background: This is the opening match of Pakistan Women's tour of Sri Lanka, a 3-match ODI series running July 23-28. Both sides have been building their white-ball squads ahead of future ICC events, making bilateral series like this important form guides.

stories.title: Hungary's tight, twisty track could turn Sunday's race into a one-stop gamble
stories.what_happened: Ahead of this weekend's race, technical previews rate the Hungaroring as the third-most difficult circuit on the 2026 calendar for overtaking. Williams is preparing for a two-stop race strategy, expecting moderate tyre degradation over a race distance. However, a roughly 20% reduction in tyre wear this season compared to recent years could make a one-stop strategy viable for some teams — a decision that will likely be shaped by Friday and Saturday practice running.
key_points: The Hungaroring is rated the third-hardest track on the 2026 calendar to overtake on
That makes Saturday's qualifying position more important than usual
Teams like Williams expect a two-stop race due to moderate tyre wear
A roughly 20% cut in tyre degradation this year could make a one-stop strategy possible instead

depth.background: The Hungaroring is a short, twisty circuit often compared to a 'go-kart track' because it has few long straights and lots of low-speed corners, which makes it very hard to pass another car on track. That means where a driver qualifies on Saturday tends to matter more here than at most other circuits, since overtaking during the race itself is difficult. Tyre strategy — how many pit stops a team plans to make to change worn tyres — is one of the few levers teams have to make up positions instead.

stories.title: Haas and Cadillac complete this weekend's F1 rookie lineup for Hungary
stories.what_happened: Haas confirmed Ryo Hirakawa — a Toyota-backed driver who has won Le Mans — will replace Oliver Bearman for his second Haas practice outing this season. Cadillac, F1's newest team, confirmed Colton Herta will replace Valtteri Bottas for his second Cadillac appearance, following his practice debut in Barcelona six weeks ago. They join three other teams already resting their regular drivers for the same session, completing a five-team rookie rotation this weekend.
key_points: Haas swaps Oliver Bearman out for Ryo Hirakawa in Friday's first practice
Cadillac swaps Valtteri Bottas out for Colton Herta
It's a rule: every F1 team must run a rookie driver in at least two practice sessions a year
Five teams are using this weekend, the last before the summer break, to fulfil it at once

depth.background: F1 rules require every team to give a 'rookie' driver — someone with two or fewer prior race starts — at least two practice-session outings across the season, to develop young talent without risking a race result. Because this Hungaroring weekend is the last race before F1's summer break and isn't a shortened 'Sprint' weekend, several teams are using Friday's first practice to tick the rule off at once.

stories.title: Championship leader Antonelli sits out Hungary FP1 — completing his rookie duty for the season
stories.what_happened: Mercedes will hand championship leader Kimi Antonelli's car to reserve driver Frederik Vesti for Friday's first practice session in Hungary, alongside four other teams doing the same for their regular drivers. Vesti previously drove Antonelli's car at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, meaning this session completes Antonelli's rookie-rule obligation for the year — he won't miss any further practice sessions in 2026.
key_points: Mercedes reserve Frederik Vesti drives Antonelli's car in Friday's first practice at the Hungaroring
F1 rules require every team to give a rookie driver two practice sessions per car each season
Antonelli already fulfilled his other mandatory rookie session at Barcelona, so this is his last for 2026
He leads the championship by 45 points over Hamilton, with Russell a further 50 points back

depth.background: Since 2023, F1 has required every team to run a driver who isn't one of their two regular race drivers for at least two practice sessions across the season, to give young talent track time in a real car. Teams try to schedule these sessions at lower-risk, less title-critical weekends, which is why several teams — not just Mercedes — are rotating in rookies this weekend.

stories.title: McLaren pulls Piastri from Hungary FP1 — reigning F2 champion Fornaroli gets the seat under F1's rookie rule
stories.what_happened: Oscar Piastri will not drive in Friday's first practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix. McLaren junior driver Leonardo Fornaroli, the reigning Formula 2 champion, takes his seat instead to satisfy F1's mandatory rookie rule. It's McLaren's turn in a wave of similar swaps this weekend, with Alpine, Haas, and Cadillac also fielding rookies or reserves in practice.
key_points: McLaren's Oscar Piastri sits out first practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix
Leonardo Fornaroli, McLaren's junior and reigning F2 champion, drives Piastri's car instead
It's mandated by F1's rookie rule, not a performance issue
Comes as McLaren brings a major upgrade package to Hungary to chase Mercedes and Ferrari

depth.background: F1 rules require every team to run a driver with two or fewer prior race starts in at least two Friday practice sessions per season, giving young talent track time in a real car. Fornaroli already drove Lando Norris's car at a practice session in Barcelona last month; this is his second outing.

stories.title: Houthis strike two Saudi oil tankers, leaving one ablaze in the Red Sea
stories.what_happened: The Houthis said they hit two Saudi Arabian oil tankers, the Encelia and the Layla, with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones as they sailed the Red Sea about 70 nautical miles southwest of Saudi Arabia's Al Shuqaiq. Saudi Arabia's state news agency confirmed a fire broke out on the Encelia's bow after it was struck, but said all crew members were safe and the vessel was not in danger of sinking.
key_points: Houthis fired missiles and drones at Saudi-flagged tankers Encelia and Layla
Saudi state media confirms a fire on Encelia's bow; all crew safe
Houthis say the ships broke a blockade they declared against Saudi Arabia on Monday
First real attacks under that new blockade — a fresh front beyond their old campaign

depth.background: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement has attacked shipping in the Red Sea since 2023, originally targeting vessels it linked to Israel or its allies over the Gaza war. This week that campaign took a new turn: on Monday the Houthis declared a naval blockade specifically against Saudi Arabia, in retaliation for a Saudi blockade on Yemen and a strike on Sanaa's international airport. Today's tanker attacks are the first strikes carried out under that new, Saudi-specific blockade — separate from, and in addition to, the Houthis' long-running campaign against Israel-linked ships.

thread.previously: Yesterday the Houthis announced they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in retaliation for a Saudi blockade on Yemen and an attack on Sanaa's airport — at that point it was a declaration, with no attacks yet reported.
thread.changed: Today the Houthis acted on that declaration for the first time, striking two named Saudi oil tankers and setting one on fire — moving the blockade from threat to reality.
